## Gotchas

> **Code / runtime / test failure-prevention, compressed to trigger + fix** (restructured 2026-05-28). Full forensic provenance (dates, commit SHAs, Codex rounds, findings docs) for every entry → [`docs/CLAUDE.md-archive.md`](docs/CLAUDE.md-archive.md) §"Appended 2026-05-28". The **process / review + brief-authoring disciplines** (the "Expansion #N" catalog + applied-research methodology) were relocated to [`docs/orchestrator-context.md`](docs/orchestrator-context.md) §"Pre-Codex review + brief-authoring disciplines". `#N` labels below are the cumulative-gotcha numbers referenced elsewhere in briefs.

### yfinance / market-data

- **yfinance rate-limits.** Use `threads=False` on `yf.download()` ONLY. `yf.Ticker(t).history()` does NOT accept `threads=` (raises `TypeError` on yfinance >= 1.2). Concurrency for `Ticker.history()` is bounded by the app executor; `PriceCache`/`OhlcvCache` sliding-window breakers are the real backpressure. **ONE authorized exception (operator, 2026-06-10):** the Arc-6 warm's multi-ticker BATCH chunk fetch (`_fetch_chunk`, ohlcv_archive.py) runs `threads=True` — the spec §8 stretch lever; safe because the warm is a pure accelerator with a proven per-ticker serial fallback (worst case = a slower night). The SINGLE-ticker path (`_yf_download_window`) stays `threads=False`.
- **yfinance `history(interval="1d")` includes the in-progress (partial) bar during market hours.** Strip it before computing SMAs / "previous close": `if df.index[-1].date() >= session: df = df.iloc[:-1]` where `session = action_session_for_run(datetime.now())`. Use the exchange-session helper, NOT `date.today()` (HST lags ET 5h).
- **yfinance `group_by='column'` returns a MultiIndex column** (`Price × Ticker`) even for single-ticker calls — `df["Close"]` is a DataFrame, not Series. Squeeze: `close = df["Close"]; if getattr(close,'ndim',1)==2: close = close.iloc[:,0]`.
- **`exchange_calendars.is_open_at_time` requires `pd.Timestamp`**, not `datetime.datetime` (raises `TypeError`). Wrap: `pd.Timestamp(datetime.now(timezone.utc))`. Log dependency-call exceptions instead of silently returning a degraded default.
- **Schwab `price_history` defaults to `(periodType=day, period=10, frequencyType=minute, frequency=1)`** — 10 days of 1-MINUTE bars, not daily. Any consumer wanting DAILY bars MUST pass `(year|month, N, daily, 1)` explicitly. Discriminating test asserts the kwargs via mock/signature.
- **OHLCV fetch scope = open-trade tickers ONLY.** `build_dashboard` computes `ohlcv_tickers = sorted({t.ticker for t in open_trades})` — do NOT union watchlist/active_tickers (burns quota, trips the breaker). Skip the fetch entirely with zero open trades.
- **External-API empty result must be treated as transient in write-through caches/archives** (F6). yfinance/broker/weather APIs return empty for rate-limit/network/weekend reasons — NEVER overwrite cached content with an empty response: retain existing, leave stale metadata so the next call retries, never blank. Applies to `swing/data/ohlcv_archive.py` + any future write-through cache. When the cache helper accepts a **dataclass**, enforce non-empty at the `__post_init__` construction barrier (rejecting in the helper is too late — the row is already built).
- **Shared-infrastructure cache hooks must return the FULL archive; consumers slice.** A fallback that pre-truncates to one consumer's minimum window silently caps every other consumer (e.g. chart needs ~145 business days vs SMA50's 60). Return full history; let each consumer slice.
- **(F6-addendum, Arc 8) Trailing-bar NaN-Close: trim, don't append.** yfinance can return the NEWEST bar with `Close=NaN` while O/H/L/V are present (the adjusted-close derivation artifact — DISTINCT from the all-NaN F6 case). The gap fetch starts at `latest_stored+1` so a stored ragged bar never self-heals until the ≤13-day staggered full refresh → NaN poisons SMAs/weather/charts for days (run #99, 2026-06-10: 134 archives, manual repair). **Fix:** the shared `_trim_trailing_ragged(df)` drops trailing rows where ANY of OHLC is NaN (Volume-only-NaN exempt; INTERIOR ragged rows PRESERVED — the Phase-15 bad-bar-accept posture for HISTORICAL bars is unchanged), applied at TWO sites — the serial `_yf_download_window` return (covers both serial branches) + the warm `_warm_one_window` per-ticker loop (covers both warm cohorts; trim-to-empty skips without fallback). Trim-to-empty composes with the existing empty-fetch guards (no write, meta stale, retry next call). Audit: per-trim `log.warning` (→ `pipeline.log`) + `WarmReport.trailing_nan_trimmed` → the runner #27 warning entry. Build tests from the REAL #99 shape (NaN Close, O/H/L/V present) — the all-NaN F6 case must still pass separately; the interior-NaN-preserved discriminator FAILS an over-eager drop-all-NaN-rows impl.

### Web / HTMX / templates / forms

- **HTMX 4xx fragments need an explicit config override.** HTMX 2.x default (`{code:"[45]..",swap:false}`) fires the error event but doesn't swap. `base.html.j2` has an `htmx.config.responseHandling` override enabling 4xx swapping — preserve it. TestClient won't catch a regression (it asserts body, not DOM).
- **Starlette middleware is LIFO.** `add_middleware` order is the REVERSE of request execution — later calls become more-outer. Security-critical middleware (OriginGuard strict-mode, request-id) must be added LAST so it wraps everything.
- **`base.html.j2` is shared — a new `vm.foo` field requires adding it (with a safe default) to EVERY base-layout VM** (`DashboardVM`, `PipelineVM`, `JournalVM`, `WatchlistVM`, `PageErrorVM`) or Jinja 500s unrelated routes with `UndefinedError`.
- **Cache + executor race: workers must not write shared state when the request thread cancels on deadline miss.** `Future.cancel()` is a no-op on a running worker. Worker returns a pure value; the request thread writes to `_store` ONLY for futures done in-deadline (`wait(timeout=deadline)`, iterate `done` not `pending`).
- **HTMX OOB-swap partials that hand-duplicate full-page markup drift silently.** OOB partials and full-page render must go through the SAME `{% include %}` target, never hand-duplicated fragments.
- **HTMX response leading with `<tr>` triggers `makeFragment` synthetic-table-wrap that DROPS `<table>` content inside OOB `<section>` chunks** (HTML5 nested-table parse rules; only in a real browser, not TestClient). Keep any new HTMX endpoint's primary content table-row-free at fragment root (use `<div>`/`<section>`); deliver new rows via OOB swap into the destination tbody.
- **HTMX `hx-target` INHERITS from ancestors — a lazy child element MUST set `hx-target="this"` when an ancestor already sets `hx-target`.** A `<td>` with `hx-get`+`hx-trigger="revealed"`+`hx-swap="innerHTML"` but NO explicit `hx-target`, inside a `<tr hx-target="closest tr">` (click-to-expand), inherits the row's target → the revealed lazy-load swaps its response into the WHOLE ROW's innerHTML, wiping every other cell (and breaking expand). Set `hx-target="this"` on the child so it swaps into itself. Browser-only (the initial render looks correct; only the live trigger fires it; caught at the Phase-14 close-out P14.N1 operator gate). A TestClient regression asserts the rendered child carries `hx-target="this"` (the exact attribute order, so it won't false-match the ancestor's target).
- **HTMX form endpoints have two browser-only failure surfaces TestClient cannot detect:** (1) embedded forms inside HTMX fragments need `hx-headers='{"HX-Request": "true"}'` or OriginGuard strict-mode 403s the submit; (2) success path must be `204` + `HX-Redirect: <url>`, NOT `303`→swap-target (htmx.js swallows 303). Operator-witnessed browser verification is BINDING for HTMX work.
- **HX-Redirect target route must be verified to exist** — TestClient verifies the header but doesn't follow. Assert the target is in `app.routes` OR follow the redirect with a second call asserting 200.
- **Matplotlib mathtext fires on `$` `^` `_` and unbalanced `\`** — silently italicizes text, eats the metacharacters, collapses whitespace in the RENDERED PNG. String-equality tests check the format string, not the render. Fix: omit the metacharacter from any `title=`/`xlabel=`/`ylabel=`/annotation entirely (escaping `\$` still triggers math mode). Manual visual verification of rendered text is non-optional.
- **Weather lookup in read-only UIs must NOT query by `action_session`.** Weather is keyed by `data_asof_date` (last completed session); `action_session` is forward-looking → silent `None` on weekends/evenings. Use `swing.data.repos.weather.get_latest(conn, ticker=...)` (most recent by `run_ts`).
- **Repo readers with a default-arg filter ≠ production config → silent false-negative.** `weather.get_latest(conn, *, ticker="QQQ")` DEFAULTS to QQQ, but production records weather under `cfg.rs.benchmark_ticker` (live = SPY) — a bare `get_latest(conn)` returns `None` on the live DB → false "no weather" on a current system. ALWAYS pass `ticker=cfg.rs.benchmark_ticker` (every production caller does: dashboard/open_positions/trades). Generalizes to ANY repo reader whose default-arg filter can diverge from the configured value. The 18-E tool-health monitor shipped this exact bug; 8326 byte-tests + 4 Codex rounds MISSED it (the seeded fixtures used the QQQ default) — only the operator live-DB witness caught it. **Verify read-path correctness against the LIVE DB shape, not just seeded fixtures.**
- **Session-anchor read/write mismatch** (forward-looking `action_session_for_run` vs backward-looking `last_completed_session`) silently invisibles UI display. Recurring family (weather, daily-mgmt badge, in-progress-bar). Read the WRITER's anchor function before locking a read predicate; add a write-then-read round-trip test. Inequality directionality: use `>=` for forward-looking anchors, strict `>` for backward-looking (the boundary bar is inclusive backward).
- **V1 single-operator forms with hidden audit fields (timestamps, session anchors, precision tiers): SERVER-STAMP, don't trust hidden inputs.** And "server-stamped" means the POST handler RE-COMPUTES from canonical state at POST time — NOT that a GET-rendered value is trusted on resubmit. Remove the hidden input; expose computed values as display-only `<span>`.
- **Form-render hidden anchors that drive POST-time validation MUST round-trip through the soft-warn confirm `form_values` dict** or a `force=true` resubmit drops the anchor → validation silently bypassed.
- **POST-time recompute of "latest-of-something" creates a GET/POST TOCTOU window.** If the operator saw the value at form-render time, emit it as a hidden anchor and validate the POST against that exact anchor's row — don't recompute "latest" at POST time.
- **Hidden-anchor 4-tier rejection ladder** for web forms with audit anchors: (a) malformed JSON → 400 + clear; (b) non-dict → 400 + clear; (c) missing required keys → 400 + clear; (d) invalid value shapes → 400 + clear. Plus a `claimed_auto_fill` consistency gate. On rejection the recovery form MUST clear the bad anchor (pass `submitted_*=None`), else the operator is trapped replaying it.
- **`selected_X_audit_id` is an AUDIT TRAIL, not a DEDUPE KEY.** Dedupe off the field reflecting the row's value-source (what was persisted), not what the operator picked.
- **Price-precision parity between template render and POST float comparison.** If the template renders `%.2f` and the POST compares with a tight epsilon, execution-grain prices falsely flip to "operator edited". Compare with `round(anchor,N) != round(submitted,N)` where N matches display precision.
- **`extended.pop(key, None)` for envelope keys that may not apply** — don't leave a stale form-render default; pop it so downstream dedupe falls through to the fallback match.
- **Audit-envelope empty state must be uniform `None` (not `"[]"`, not `""`) across BOTH the VM emit path and the persist write path** — `"[]"` is truthy and defeats the `... or None` SQL-nullability defense.

### SQLite / transactions / migrations / schema

- **`os.replace` requires same filesystem.** On Windows with Drive-synced dest + `$TMP` on another volume it raises `OSError 18`. Create temp files in the DESTINATION dir (`NamedTemporaryFile(dir=<dest_dir>)`). Never `shutil.move` expecting overwrite on Windows.
- **Python `... or ""` collides with SQL CHECK-constraint nullability** when the enum excludes empty string. Use `... or None` for nullable text columns with CHECK constraints; add a test submitting an empty field asserting NULL persisted.
- **SQLite `INSERT OR REPLACE` / bare `REPLACE` is `DELETE old + INSERT new`** — cascade-wipes child rows via `ON DELETE CASCADE`, issues a NEW PK, rewrites history. For audit/uniqueness tables use SELECT-then-UPDATE-or-INSERT. **(Amended 2026-08-25, the 22-A epoch finding): REPLACE's implicit DELETE does NOT fire DELETE triggers unless `PRAGMA recursive_triggers` is ON — it is OFF by default and ZERO hits repo-wide — so a DELETE-trigger barrier is FAIL-OPEN to `REPLACE`.** Guard immutable/seeded rows with a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger (created AFTER the seeding row), never a DELETE trigger alone.
- **Service-layer `with conn:` opens its own transaction** — do NOT call it from inside an outer single-transaction (inner context-manager commits the connection's single transaction). When composing multi-step atomic side-effects, call the REPO-level functions directly; preserve the repo-vs-service asymmetry.
- **(#9) `sqlite3.executescript()` issues an implicit COMMIT and runs statements in autocommit** — `conn.rollback()` can't undo intermediate statements. Migration runner MUST do explicit `BEGIN`+`executescript`+`COMMIT` with try/except `rollback()`+re-raise (`swing/data/db.py:_apply_migration`, foreign_keys=OFF at runner level). Test rollback through the real runner path, not bare `executescript`.
- **`in_transaction` "auto-detect outer transaction" guards re-introduce the race the explicit lock closed.** Single-transaction service contract: caller MUST NOT hold an open tx; function ALWAYS owns `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/COMMIT/ROLLBACK; REJECT (don't auto-detect) caller-held transactions. Environment short-circuits (sandbox/dry-run) live in the INNER (caller-tx) function so the outer tx-discipline (reject-caller-held / BEGIN IMMEDIATE) stays uniform.
- **Reconciliation flow pivot uses SAVEPOINT-per-discrepancy inside the outer run transaction** (`SAVEPOINT correction_sp_<id>` / RELEASE on success / ROLLBACK TO+RELEASE on exception) — without it a partial mutation commits on the outer COMMIT.
- **SELECT-first idempotency MUST precede payload validation** — a terminal-state row must return its existing audit-row id even with a stale/None payload. Step order: sandbox short-circuit → SELECT + None-check → terminal-state idempotent return → payload validation → atomic write.
- **Counter staleness after inline state mutation** — a flow that emits rows incrementing a counter AND later mutates those rows' states must decrement per-mutation OR recompute via `SELECT COUNT(*)` post-loop.
- **Queries `ORDER BY started_ts DESC` on `pipeline_runs` mask prior completes mid-run** (a NULL-`finished_ts` row wins). Two-read pattern: most-recent COMPLETED row's `finished_ts` for "last good data"; most-recent-started row's `state` for "what's happening now".
- **(#11) Schema-CHECK + Python-constant + dataclass-validator MUST land in ONE task** for atomic consistency — and this EXTENDS to semantic contracts layered atop the CHECK (cache-key shapes, partial-index existence semantics): mirror EACH in `__post_init__`, not just the schema CHECK. When widening a CHECK enum, grep ALL `swing/` for hardcoded copies of the old tuple/enum (multiple Python mirrors: constants, `__post_init__`, repo guards, per-surface `_call_endpoint` guards) AND audit each as manual-input-allowlist (tight) vs service-only (full-widened). Read-path `_row_to_*` mappers MUST be widened in the same task as the write-path. Schema-version-aware INSERT: detect version via `PRAGMA table_info` and branch column-lists OR migrate all pre-version fixtures. **(Amended 2026-08-24, the 22-A `freeze_tier` widening): once a value crosses SQL + Python + a TRIGGER body + a JSON envelope + prose, the canonical triple UNDERSTATES the mirror family — the measured count was ELEVEN sites (three stale, eight value-agnostic-by-luck), and THE ONLY MIRROR THAT DEFENDS THE SET IS THE COMPARATOR (the SQL-vs-Python drift test comparing two representations).** So: the widening sweep is closure-checked by READ (not token grep), and the drift test is a MANDATORY member of the mirror set. **(Second facet, 2026-08-25, the 22-A minting trigger — TWELFTH site): a VALUE-SET sweep does not find a HARD-CODED SINGLE MEMBER** (`tier='live_at_acceptance'` unconditionally, in the section that authoritatively specifies the trigger — a false structural-proof label written into the epoch's own migration). **Grep each enum member SEPARATELY, not the tuple**; the drift test remains the one instrument that does not depend on choosing the right grep.
- **Migration backup-gate uses STRICT equality `pre_version == (target - 1)`, NOT `<=`** (multi-version jumps must be separate two-step migrations). Copy the Phase 9 `pre_version == 16 AND target >= 17` clause shape verbatim.
- **sqlite3 cannot bind a list to a single `:name` placeholder** — build dynamic `?` expansion for IN clauses (`",".join("?"*len(values))`); short-circuit empty input (empty `IN ()` is invalid SQL) and return a dataclass with all required sentinel fields.
- **Python and SQLite ROUND DIFFERENTLY at the half: `round(1.125, 2)` = **1.12** in Python (half-to-EVEN) and **1.13** in SQLite (half AWAY FROM ZERO)** — verified by execution, 2026-08-25 (the 22-A option-C finding). A truthful evidence row computed in Python can be REJECTED by a SQLite trigger comparing "the same" values at display precision — a false refusal wearing a precision costume. **ONE ROUNDING AUTHORITY per comparison:** either the comparison runs entirely in one domain (service compares; SQL stores, never rounds), or canonical pre-rounded values are stored and compared BYTEWISE. Never let a Python-rounded value meet a SQLite-rounded value across an equality. Hits ANY Python-computes/SQL-validates price comparison (triggers, CHECKs, generated columns).
- **`date.fromisoformat()` at the TEXT-column → Python-`date` boundary.** When a SQL TEXT column feeds a helper expecting `date`, convert at the callsite; add a malformed-input test asserting a typed error, not a deep `TypeError`.
- **`reconciliation_corrections` is APPEND-ONLY** — tier-3 chains INSERT a new row + UPDATE the prior row's `superseded_by_correction_id`; never DELETE/UPDATE-in-place. Chain head has `superseded_by_correction_id IS NULL`.
- **`PriceCache._last_close` only sees tickers in today's `candidates` table.** Open-trade tickers that rotate out of finviz get stale closes; `_step_evaluate` unions `list_open_trades` and writes them `bucket='excluded'` to keep closes fresh. New "priced" surfaces must verify their tickers appear in `candidates`.
- **(#30) A RUN/BATCH-LEVEL STAMP IS NOT PROVENANCE FOR A PER-ROW VALUE.** Trigger: reading a per-row field alongside a run-level timestamp and treating that stamp as the row's own date. The stamp is an AGGREGATE (`max(...)`), so a row lagging the batch max is stamped FRESHER than it is — the write path never guarantees the coupling; the reader assumes it. Met TWICE in Phase 21-A: freeze-at-fire (read the FIRE's own `candidates` row), and `evaluation_runs.data_asof_date` (cohort-max) standing in for a per-ticker `candidates.close` → the mandate-shape check can bless the wrong order form off a stale price (a false ALL-CLEAR). **Fix:** carry per-row provenance at WRITE time, or treat the stamp as an UPPER BOUND — raise a MISMATCH alarm from it, never assert a MATCH (the same asymmetry ruled for stale closes + cached order state). Both instances are TIMESTAMP-shaped; do NOT widen without a third. Full forensic + file:line → [`docs/CLAUDE.md-archive.md`](docs/CLAUDE.md-archive.md) §"Appended 2026-07-28".
- **(#31) A SEAM COMMENT PROMISING FUTURE INHERITANCE IS UNENFORCEABLE BY CONSTRUCTION — and its failure is INVISIBLE because the comment still reads true.** Trigger: a comment asserting that a LATER arc's improvement will "flow through automatically" to this call site. That is a claim about work THAT HAS NOT HAPPENED, so no test can pin it; when the later arc lands and changes a DIFFERENT half of the contract, the comment silently becomes false while still reading as an invariant. **Live instance (21-G × 21-B, 2026-07-31):** `swing/web/view_models/latches.py` carried *"THE 21-A SEAM, NEVER RE-IMPLEMENTED. Whatever 21-G does to make the close sound flows through automatically."* True for `expected_mandate_order_type` (the comparison, correctly not duplicated) — but 21-G's soundness work landed in **the caller's decision whether to pass a price at all**, and that half did NOT flow through, so the prepared-order form kept 21-A's retired stamp gate and ASSERTED a regime from a close the same card refused to date, persisting the unproven date into the parity ledger. The existing test pinned the wrong half — that the module contains no independent comparison (what the code does NOT do) rather than what the caller MUST do. **Fix:** a comment may describe what the code does TODAY; it may NOT promise what a future change will do to it. Pin the CALLER-SIDE OBLIGATION with a test, not the callee's absence. **Related class (CHARC, harness-architecture §5.1): no rung of the review ladder reviews the COMPOSITION of two arcs** — each rung reviews one arc's diff/plan/encoding/screens, so a cross-arc defect is catchable only at rebase/merge-integration. Treat that step as a GATE, not mechanics, whenever parallel arcs land.

### Pattern detectors (Phase 13)

- **High-tight-flag post-pole sub-window is named `consolidation_*`, NOT `flag_*`** (spec §5.5 criterion lock strings). Read the spec's criterion lock strings, not the colloquial pattern name, for canonical sub-window field names.
- **Cross-bundle pin fixture-shape mismatch silently extends a test-skip pin beyond its schedule** — verify fixture-shape compatibility BEFORE a pin promises an un-skip date.
- **Evidence-tier vs composite-tier score cap distinction** — evidence-tier may reach its spec'd upper bound (e.g. 1.10 undercut bonus); composite-tier clamps at the composite cap (e.g. `min(1.0,...)`). Downstream histograms/normalizers MUST consume the CLAMPED composite, not the raw evidence, or `ValueError`s poison the emit loop.
- **Bounded backward-slice search for anchor-relative detectors** — bound the back-walk by the spec's max-duration constraint (e.g. HTF pole 4-8 weeks); "most recent" / "absolute max" lets a stale historical landmark capture the algorithm.
- **DBW (and any `CandidateWindow` consumer) must check `anchor_reason.startswith("zigzag_pivot")`** to interpret `anchor_date` semantic: `zigzag_pivot*` = base START (swing-low); `ma_crossover`/`high_low_breakout` = TRIGGER event. Raise if a non-zigzag mode is supplied where a swing-low is required.
- **Bad-exemplar isolation in retrieval functions** — per-element try/except around the normalize/transform helper (skip the bad exemplar, continue the cohort) rather than letting one NaN/inf array's `ValueError` bubble up and stamp the whole call `None`.
- **DTW Sakoe-Chiba band infeasibility on asymmetric series → skip-as-no-match** (final DP cell stays `inf`) is the correct V1 semantic; a candidate much shorter/longer than the exemplar corpus may yield zero hits even with planted same-class exemplars.
- **Universe histogram must reflect the POST-template composite** — when a pipeline step mutates `composite_score` after the universe-snapshot point, seed the histogram from the final persisted values, not the pre-template placeholder.
- **(#27) Silent-skip-without-audit in pipeline steps masks state drift.** An early-return "no work" guard inside a best-effort try/except (which only catches exceptions) completes "successfully" with zero work + zero audit. Empty-pool/early-return paths MUST emit a `warnings_json` entry (expected vs actual pool size + reason). Also: dispatch briefs MUST verify "since X shipped" run-count claims against `git log` of the cited commit.
- **(#28) Pattern-exemplar OHLCV cache discipline:** exemplar tickers are OUTSIDE the candidate universe, so their bars are never fetched by `_step_ohlcv`; template-match Pass 2 then silently no-ops with all-`None` scores (cache miss swallowed per bad-exemplar isolation). A detection harness relying on an exemplar corpus MUST pre-fetch exemplar OHLCV OR emit an `exemplar_load_failure_count` + WARNING OR document the precondition.
- **(#29) Exemplar OHLCV pre-fetch HISTORICAL DEPTH:** yfinance default `period="5y"` is insufficient for pre-2021 historical exemplar `end_date`s (manifests as the SAME 100%-`None` symptom as #28 even after presence is fixed — `OhlcvCoverageError: sliced=0`). Pre-fetch with `period="max"` (or a window from `MIN(end_date) - 200d`). Multi-stage silent-no-op chains need stage-by-stage manifest counters to localize the next blocker.

### Research-harness V1↔V2 parity (applied research)

- **(#24) Parallel-archive freshness desync** — when two archive shapes exist for the same logical data (`{T}.parquet` legacy + `{T}.yfinance.parquet` Shape A) and a reader consumes ONE, asymmetric writer schedules create per-ticker boundary-bar staleness that invalidates V1↔V2 baseline-parity claims. - **(#25) Sentinel-bucket parity-comparison discipline** — baseline-parity tests comparing two systems' bucket assignments MUST filter SENTINEL buckets one system pre-empts (`excluded`/`error`) and the other naively recomputes (e.g. V1 short-circuits open-position/ETF-blocklist; V2's `bucket_for` only emits `{aplus,watch,skip}`). Filter sentinel-bucket candidates from the parity diff.
- **(#26) OHLCV archive bar-content TEMPORAL mutation** between V1's persisted-eval-run time and V2's current-archive read time (`write_window` drop_duplicates `keep='last'`; yfinance re-fetch drifts historical bars ~0.5-3%) invalidates V1↔V2 criterion-level parity. ### Windows / tooling / test-discipline

- **Windows PowerShell stdout defaults to cp1252; non-ASCII glyphs (§ → ↔ ✓ ✗ em-dash, fractions, etc.) in any `print()`/`click.echo()`/`sys.stdout.write()` path raise `UnicodeEncodeError` and crash the CLI.** pytest `capsys` bypasses the OS encoder so tests pass against code that crashes in production. Fix: prefer ASCII swaps in user-facing strings (canonical pattern); the `sys.stdout`/`stderr` UTF-8 `errors='replace'` reconfigure at CLI entry is the safety net. Add a subprocess-through-PowerShell test for stdout encoding.
- **Tests exercising `swing/config_user.py:write_user_overrides` MUST monkeypatch BOTH `USERPROFILE` AND `HOME`** before invoking — `_user_home()` reads them unmonkeypatched and writes leak to the operator's real `~/swing-data/user-config.toml`.
- **Byte-parity / algorithmic tests are INSUFFICIENT substitutes for operator-visual gates when fixtures bypass the production data-derivation path.** A byte-parity test where both paths consume identical stub fixtures only asserts "same inputs → same outputs"; it misses regressions in HOW inputs are derived (e.g. the Schwab minute-default footgun). Production-path regression tests must exercise the actual wiring; never call an algorithmic test a "STRONG" visual-gate substitute without verifying it hits the production derivation path.
- **Phase 9 risk_policy ratification is single-fire at v16→v17** (gated `pre_version <= 16 AND post_version >= 17`); re-firing would clobber operator CLI policy edits. Repair path: per-field `swing config policy import-from-toml`. Add a run-db-migrate-twice no-op test.

Future emitters MUST mirror it; add a `test_<emitter>_no_op_value_does_not_supersede`.
- **Research L2 tests that raw `del sys.modules` + re-import are xdist-order-fragile.** Several harness L2-reinforcement tests (`pattern_cohort`, `double_bottom_w`, `w_bottom`) delete + re-import their package + the forbidden modules WITHOUT restoring; a sibling cross-module `is`-identity assertion (`test_ohlcv_reader_re_export_identity`) can then intermittently fail under `-n auto` (`--dist load`, where `@pytest.mark.xdist_group` is INERT — only `--dist loadgroup` honors it). Adding tests perturbs worker balance and surfaces latent instances; reproduce with `-n 0` + explicit test ordering, not by re-running `-n auto`. **(RESOLVED for `swing.*` 2026-06-13, Phase 17 Arc 17-D.4, `f14c5b6e`..`0867337d`):** a `tests/research/conftest.py` autouse fixture (+ `_sys_modules_isolation.py`) now snapshots `swing.*` at each research test's setup and restores the `sys.modules` entry + parent-package attr at teardown, healing the raw-`del` polluter for the whole class (the trigger here was the unrestored `del` of `swing.integrations.schwab.*` rebuilding exception classes with new identities → `swing/web/routes/schwab.py`'s import-bound `except` missing them → intermittent web-route 500s). Scope is `swing.*` ONLY (restoring `research.harness.*` would frankenstein that tree). A NEW raw-`del` of a `swing.*` module under `tests/research/` is now self-healing; the same pattern OUTSIDE `tests/research/`, or a raw-`del` of a non-`swing.*` module, would still need its own hermetic teardown.
- **Adding a write-barrier to a repo WRITE function breaks tests that seed invalid/edge data THROUGH that function — and the break can be CROSS-ARC (only the merged-head suite catches it).** A guard rejecting non-finite/malformed input at the sole writer (e.g. the 18-B.1 OHLC barrier in `insert_observation`) rejects the very rows that DETECTION / monitor / consumer tests plant. **Fix:** a test needing a "bad" pre-existing row MUST plant it via RAW `conn.execute` INSERT (bypassing the barrier) — it tests DETECTION of historical bad data, not the write path (the same technique as 18-B.1's read-preservation lock). **Cross-arc trap:** when the barrier and the seeding tests ship in SEPARATE arcs off DIVERGENT bases (one base predates the other's tests), neither arc's own before-review suite sees the interaction — ONLY the orchestrator's merged-head no-false-green re-run does (its reason for existing). 18-B.1×18-D, 2026-06-15, `e7c61f98`.
- **A release/finalization test MUST replicate the FULL production reference graph** — every closure / cache / caller that holds the resource — not just the one reference the brief named. **18-H.4:** the WinError-32 self-lock fix cleared `app.state.schwab_client` + `gc.collect()`, but two ladder closures (`_quote_hook`/`_bars_hook`, `swing/web/app.py:351/:379`, stored on the app-lifetime price/ohlcv caches) hold TWO MORE strong refs → `gc` can't finalize → the `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` handle stays open → the lock PERSISTS. The regression test injected a bare stub (ONE ref; ladder-inactive in the test → no cache closures) → it went GREEN against an INEFFECTIVE fix (the synthetic-vs-production-emitter gotcha family). **Fix:** a release/finalize test installs the REAL holders (the production closures/caches/callers) over the resource + asserts the release actually FINALIZES it (the handle is freed), not just that one ref is cleared. (Paired with the recipe's PRODUCTION-CODE repo-access review note — a diff-only review is blind to the surrounding closures.) 18-H.4×codex-auto-review, 2026-06-16.
- **A session-scoped suite invariant over a LIVE MUTABLE SHARED tree (`comms/`, `exports/`) is inherently flaky in this multi-agent repo — scope the belt to the THREAT SIGNATURE, never to world-frozenness.** The 19-B comms-isolation DETECTION belt (`tests/conftest.py:_fail_suite_on_real_comms_write`) `rglob`-snapshotted the WHOLE real `comms/` tree at session start and asserted it unchanged at teardown. Under `-n auto` a session-scoped autouse fixture runs ONCE PER WORKER (this box = 16 cores → 16 workers), and `comms/` legitimately churns during a multi-minute run (director/orchestrator mail, `inbox→read` acks) → every worker's teardown assert tripped on that churn → **16 spurious per-worker ERRORS on the merged-head run, gone on re-run** (a mechanism argument, not a clean re-run, is the flake proof). **Fix:** key the belt on the production PUSH SIGNATURE (`_LATEST_JSON_POINTER`, IMPORTED not hard-coded so it can't silently rot — the D21 decay class), scope to ADDED `inbox/` files only (drop the removals check — `inbox→read` is legit churn), and make the failure message disambiguate leaked-test-push vs genuine-concurrent-production-push (list paths + first lines + "verify run-id against `pipeline_runs`"). The function-scoped seam-redirect fixture is the real PREVENTION; the session belt only guards the forgot-the-seam class. 19-B×RD+CHARC, 2026-07-04.

## Quick Start

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev,web]"
swing --help                         # CLI: trade, journal, pipeline, web, finviz, etc.
swing web                            # FastAPI + HTMX dashboard on 127.0.0.1:8080
python -m pytest -m "not slow" -q    # fast suite (~7038 tests as of 2026-06-02, ~3min with xdist)
python -m pytest -m slow             # pipeline/yfinance e2e (minutes, needs network)
ruff check swing/
```

**Windows PATH for `swing` CLI:** `pip install -e` places the `swing.exe` entry point in `%APPDATA%\Python\Python314\Scripts\` (user install, not `C:\Python314\Scripts`). Add that dir to the user PATH permanently via System Properties, or per-session: `$env:PATH = "$env:APPDATA\Python\Python314\Scripts;$env:PATH"`.

**Finviz inbox:** `data/finviz-inbox/` (configured in `swing.config.toml`). Pipeline now fetches the screen via Finviz Elite API automatically (`_step_finviz_fetch`); manual CSV drop remains a fallback override (file-collision skip in the pipeline step). Save manual exports as `finvizDDMmmYYYY.csv` (1-2 digit day, 3-letter month, 4-digit year — e.g. `finviz5May2026.csv`). API-emitted CSVs use the same filename pattern, anchored on `action_session_for_run(datetime.now())` per [`swing/pipeline/runner.py:_step_finviz_fetch`](swing/pipeline/runner.py). Validator requires 13 columns: `No., Ticker, Sector, Industry, Country, Price, Change, Average Volume, Relative Volume, Average True Range, 52-Week High, 52-Week Low, Market Cap`. Missing columns → CSV moved to `data/finviz-inbox/rejected/` with a sidecar `.rejected-reasons.json`. Pipeline outputs go to `exports/<action_session_date>/` (briefing.md + briefing.html + charts/).

**Pipeline lease-acquisition wait** (`web.pipeline_lease_wait_seconds`, default 5s): how long POST `/pipeline/run` waits for the spawned subprocess to insert its `pipeline_runs` row. Python 3.14 cold-start + heavy imports on Windows regularly cross 2s; bump if you see false "did not acquire lease" errors on a slow box.

## Strategy

The project follows a bifurcated architecture (research branch + operational trader-facing branch) per:

- `reference/Future Work/2026-04-23-bifurcated-strategic-implementation-proposal-v2.1.md` — governing strategy.
- `reference/Future Work/2026-04-23-rebuttal-response-for-implementors.md` — binding clarifications (minimum viable governance, toleranced parity, bootstrap-first data).

Source-of-truth methodology references live in `reference/methodology/`. These are reference-only; any production change driven by a methodology reference must route through the source-of-truth correction protocol (V2.1 §VII.F), not a direct patch.

**Transcribed book corpus** (the underlying source frameworks — Minervini, O'Neil disciples, Weinstein stage analysis, Qullamaggie, Schwager, psychology): full electronic `.md` + figures under `reference/Books/<slug>/`, gitignored/local-only + regenerable via [`scripts/convert_books_pdf_to_md.py`](scripts/convert_books_pdf_to_md.py). Indexed (titles, paths, what-each-is-for) at [`reference/books-corpus-index.md`](reference/books-corpus-index.md) — consult it before assuming a source is unavailable.

The research branch lives at `research/` (created Tranche B-research, 2026-04-23). Method records in `research/method-records/` follow the V2.1 §IV.B minimum viable field list; studies in `research/studies/` follow the format established by `earnings-proximity-exclusion.md`. Phase 0 tasks in `research/phase-0-tasks.md`. No runtime code is under `research/` as of this writing — it is pure documentation and study artifacts.

Older strategy documents are archived at `reference/Future Work/archive/`.

## Architecture

`swing/` — application package:
- `data/` — SQLite schema (`migrations/*.sql`), dataclass models, repo functions
- `pipeline/` — nightly orchestrator, lease fencing, finviz CSV select+validate, step runners
- `trades/` — entry/exit/stop_adjust services + reconciliation flow + auto-correction service (Phase 12 C); advisory rules; equity math
- `recommendations/` — `compute_shares` / `SizingResult` (position sizing)
- `evaluation/` — A+ criteria, bucket rules, date semantics (`action_session_for_run`)
- `web/` — FastAPI + HTMX (`app.py`, `routes/`, `view_models/`, `templates/`, `middleware/`, `price_cache.py`)
- `integrations/` — Finviz Elite API (`finviz/`) + Schwab Trader/Market Data APIs (`schwab/`); per-vendor sub-packages (post-Phase-11)
- `metrics/` — Phase 10 dashboard metric surfaces (9 surface routes; Phase 13 T2.SB6b pattern-outcomes 9th tile shipped at `6ec989e`)
- `patterns/` — Phase 13/14 pattern detectors (VCP, flat-base, cup-handle, HTF, DBW), composite scoring, template matching, active learning
- `watchlist/` — the pure watchlist lifecycle service (`compute_watchlist_changes`: add/requalify/streak/remove + the Arc-7 pin veto)
- `journal/` — trade-journal analysis (`analyze.py`, `stats.py`, `flags.py`) + the TOS account-statement import (`tos_import.py`)
- `weather/` — the market-weather classifier + runner (benchmark SMA/slope regime classification)
- `rendering/` — nightly briefing emit (md/html) + pipeline chart rendering
- `diagnostics/` — operator one-off/maintenance harnesses (sector backfill, metrics wiring audit, chart-cache prune)
- `tools/` — repo/ops utilities (prices-cache migration)
- `monitoring/` — the Phase-18 read-only operational + research health monitors (`tool_health` + `research_health` → the §3 status envelope) + the `stoplights` framework feeding the GUI topbar health stoplights
- `logging_config.py` / `logging_setup.py` / `log_correlation.py` / `logs_maintenance.py` — the Phase-16 Arc-2 logging system (the Schwab-agnostic seam, the redaction-by-construction composition root, run/request correlation, the operator-gated log compaction)
- `cli.py` (+ `cli_config.py`, `cli_schwab.py`) — click-based `swing` CLI entry point

`tests/` mirrors `swing/`. `docs/superpowers/specs/` and `/plans/` hold per-phase design docs.

## Gotchas

> **Code / runtime / test failure-prevention, compressed to trigger + fix** (restructured 2026-05-28). Full forensic provenance (dates, commit SHAs, Codex rounds, findings docs) for every entry → [`docs/CLAUDE.md-archive.md`](docs/CLAUDE.md-archive.md) §"Appended 2026-05-28". The **process / review + brief-authoring disciplines** (the "Expansion #N" catalog + applied-research methodology) were relocated to [`docs/orchestrator-context.md`](docs/orchestrator-context.md) §"Pre-Codex review + brief-authoring disciplines". `#N` labels below are the cumulative-gotcha numbers referenced elsewhere in briefs.

### yfinance / market-data

- **yfinance rate-limits.** Use `threads=False` on `yf.download()` ONLY. `yf.Ticker(t).history()` does NOT accept `threads=` (raises `TypeError` on yfinance >= 1.2). Concurrency for `Ticker.history()` is bounded by the app executor; `PriceCache`/`OhlcvCache` sliding-window breakers are the real backpressure. **ONE authorized exception (operator, 2026-06-10):** the Arc-6 warm's multi-ticker BATCH chunk fetch (`_fetch_chunk`, ohlcv_archive.py) runs `threads=True` — the spec §8 stretch lever; safe because the warm is a pure accelerator with a proven per-ticker serial fallback (worst case = a slower night). The SINGLE-ticker path (`_yf_download_window`) stays `threads=False`.
- **yfinance `history(interval="1d")` includes the in-progress (partial) bar during market hours.** Strip it before computing SMAs / "previous close": `if df.index[-1].date() >= session: df = df.iloc[:-1]` where `session = action_session_for_run(datetime.now())`. Use the exchange-session helper, NOT `date.today()` (HST lags ET 5h).
- **yfinance `group_by='column'` returns a MultiIndex column** (`Price × Ticker`) even for single-ticker calls — `df["Close"]` is a DataFrame, not Series. Squeeze: `close = df["Close"]; if getattr(close,'ndim',1)==2: close = close.iloc[:,0]`.
- **`exchange_calendars.is_open_at_time` requires `pd.Timestamp`**, not `datetime.datetime` (raises `TypeError`). Wrap: `pd.Timestamp(datetime.now(timezone.utc))`. Log dependency-call exceptions instead of silently returning a degraded default.
- **Schwab `price_history` defaults to `(periodType=day, period=10, frequencyType=minute, frequency=1)`** — 10 days of 1-MINUTE bars, not daily. Any consumer wanting DAILY bars MUST pass `(year|month, N, daily, 1)` explicitly. Discriminating test asserts the kwargs via mock/signature.
- **OHLCV fetch scope = open-trade tickers ONLY.** `build_dashboard` computes `ohlcv_tickers = sorted({t.ticker for t in open_trades})` — do NOT union watchlist/active_tickers (burns quota, trips the breaker). Skip the fetch entirely with zero open trades.
- **External-API empty result must be treated as transient in write-through caches/archives** (F6). yfinance/broker/weather APIs return empty for rate-limit/network/weekend reasons — NEVER overwrite cached content with an empty response: retain existing, leave stale metadata so the next call retries, never blank. Applies to `swing/data/ohlcv_archive.py` + any future write-through cache. When the cache helper accepts a **dataclass**, enforce non-empty at the `__post_init__` construction barrier (rejecting in the helper is too late — the row is already built).
- **Shared-infrastructure cache hooks must return the FULL archive; consumers slice.** A fallback that pre-truncates to one consumer's minimum window silently caps every other consumer (e.g. chart needs ~145 business days vs SMA50's 60). Return full history; let each consumer slice.
- **(F6-addendum, Arc 8) Trailing-bar NaN-Close: trim, don't append.** yfinance can return the NEWEST bar with `Close=NaN` while O/H/L/V are present (the adjusted-close derivation artifact — DISTINCT from the all-NaN F6 case). The gap fetch starts at `latest_stored+1` so a stored ragged bar never self-heals until the ≤13-day staggered full refresh → NaN poisons SMAs/weather/charts for days (run #99, 2026-06-10: 134 archives, manual repair). **Fix:** the shared `_trim_trailing_ragged(df)` drops trailing rows where ANY of OHLC is NaN (Volume-only-NaN exempt; INTERIOR ragged rows PRESERVED — the Phase-15 bad-bar-accept posture for HISTORICAL bars is unchanged), applied at TWO sites — the serial `_yf_download_window` return (covers both serial branches) + the warm `_warm_one_window` per-ticker loop (covers both warm cohorts; trim-to-empty skips without fallback). Trim-to-empty composes with the existing empty-fetch guards (no write, meta stale, retry next call). Audit: per-trim `log.warning` (→ `pipeline.log`) + `WarmReport.trailing_nan_trimmed` → the runner #27 warning entry. Build tests from the REAL #99 shape (NaN Close, O/H/L/V present) — the all-NaN F6 case must still pass separately; the interior-NaN-preserved discriminator FAILS an over-eager drop-all-NaN-rows impl.

### Web / HTMX / templates / forms

- **HTMX 4xx fragments need an explicit config override.** HTMX 2.x default (`{code:"[45]..",swap:false}`) fires the error event but doesn't swap. `base.html.j2` has an `htmx.config.responseHandling` override enabling 4xx swapping — preserve it. TestClient won't catch a regression (it asserts body, not DOM).
- **Starlette middleware is LIFO.** `add_middleware` order is the REVERSE of request execution — later calls become more-outer. Security-critical middleware (OriginGuard strict-mode, request-id) must be added LAST so it wraps everything.
- **`base.html.j2` is shared — a new `vm.foo` field requires adding it (with a safe default) to EVERY base-layout VM** (`DashboardVM`, `PipelineVM`, `JournalVM`, `WatchlistVM`, `PageErrorVM`) or Jinja 500s unrelated routes with `UndefinedError`.
- **Cache + executor race: workers must not write shared state when the request thread cancels on deadline miss.** `Future.cancel()` is a no-op on a running worker. Worker returns a pure value; the request thread writes to `_store` ONLY for futures done in-deadline (`wait(timeout=deadline)`, iterate `done` not `pending`).
- **HTMX OOB-swap partials that hand-duplicate full-page markup drift silently.** OOB partials and full-page render must go through the SAME `{% include %}` target, never hand-duplicated fragments.
- **HTMX response leading with `<tr>` triggers `makeFragment` synthetic-table-wrap that DROPS `<table>` content inside OOB `<section>` chunks** (HTML5 nested-table parse rules; only in a real browser, not TestClient). Keep any new HTMX endpoint's primary content table-row-free at fragment root (use `<div>`/`<section>`); deliver new rows via OOB swap into the destination tbody.
- **HTMX `hx-target` INHERITS from ancestors — a lazy child element MUST set `hx-target="this"` when an ancestor already sets `hx-target`.** A `<td>` with `hx-get`+`hx-trigger="revealed"`+`hx-swap="innerHTML"` but NO explicit `hx-target`, inside a `<tr hx-target="closest tr">` (click-to-expand), inherits the row's target → the revealed lazy-load swaps its response into the WHOLE ROW's innerHTML, wiping every other cell (and breaking expand). Set `hx-target="this"` on the child so it swaps into itself. Browser-only (the initial render looks correct; only the live trigger fires it; caught at the Phase-14 close-out P14.N1 operator gate). A TestClient regression asserts the rendered child carries `hx-target="this"` (the exact attribute order, so it won't false-match the ancestor's target).
- **HTMX form endpoints have two browser-only failure surfaces TestClient cannot detect:** (1) embedded forms inside HTMX fragments need `hx-headers='{"HX-Request": "true"}'` or OriginGuard strict-mode 403s the submit; (2) success path must be `204` + `HX-Redirect: <url>`, NOT `303`→swap-target (htmx.js swallows 303). Operator-witnessed browser verification is BINDING for HTMX work.
- **HX-Redirect target route must be verified to exist** — TestClient verifies the header but doesn't follow. Assert the target is in `app.routes` OR follow the redirect with a second call asserting 200.
- **Matplotlib mathtext fires on `$` `^` `_` and unbalanced `\`** — silently italicizes text, eats the metacharacters, collapses whitespace in the RENDERED PNG. String-equality tests check the format string, not the render. Fix: omit the metacharacter from any `title=`/`xlabel=`/`ylabel=`/annotation entirely (escaping `\$` still triggers math mode). Manual visual verification of rendered text is non-optional.
- **Weather lookup in read-only UIs must NOT query by `action_session`.** Weather is keyed by `data_asof_date` (last completed session); `action_session` is forward-looking → silent `None` on weekends/evenings. Use `swing.data.repos.weather.get_latest(conn, ticker=...)` (most recent by `run_ts`).
- **Repo readers with a default-arg filter ≠ production config → silent false-negative.** `weather.get_latest(conn, *, ticker="QQQ")` DEFAULTS to QQQ, but production records weather under `cfg.rs.benchmark_ticker` (live = SPY) — a bare `get_latest(conn)` returns `None` on the live DB → false "no weather" on a current system. ALWAYS pass `ticker=cfg.rs.benchmark_ticker` (every production caller does: dashboard/open_positions/trades). Generalizes to ANY repo reader whose default-arg filter can diverge from the configured value. The 18-E tool-health monitor shipped this exact bug; 8326 byte-tests + 4 Codex rounds MISSED it (the seeded fixtures used the QQQ default) — only the operator live-DB witness caught it. **Verify read-path correctness against the LIVE DB shape, not just seeded fixtures.**
- **Session-anchor read/write mismatch** (forward-looking `action_session_for_run` vs backward-looking `last_completed_session`) silently invisibles UI display. Recurring family (weather, daily-mgmt badge, in-progress-bar). Read the WRITER's anchor function before locking a read predicate; add a write-then-read round-trip test. Inequality directionality: use `>=` for forward-looking anchors, strict `>` for backward-looking (the boundary bar is inclusive backward).
- **V1 single-operator forms with hidden audit fields (timestamps, session anchors, precision tiers): SERVER-STAMP, don't trust hidden inputs.** And "server-stamped" means the POST handler RE-COMPUTES from canonical state at POST time — NOT that a GET-rendered value is trusted on resubmit. Remove the hidden input; expose computed values as display-only `<span>`.
- **Form-render hidden anchors that drive POST-time validation MUST round-trip through the soft-warn confirm `form_values` dict** or a `force=true` resubmit drops the anchor → validation silently bypassed.
- **POST-time recompute of "latest-of-something" creates a GET/POST TOCTOU window.** If the operator saw the value at form-render time, emit it as a hidden anchor and validate the POST against that exact anchor's row — don't recompute "latest" at POST time.
- **Hidden-anchor 4-tier rejection ladder** for web forms with audit anchors: (a) malformed JSON → 400 + clear; (b) non-dict → 400 + clear; (c) missing required keys → 400 + clear; (d) invalid value shapes → 400 + clear. Plus a `claimed_auto_fill` consistency gate. On rejection the recovery form MUST clear the bad anchor (pass `submitted_*=None`), else the operator is trapped replaying it.
- **`selected_X_audit_id` is an AUDIT TRAIL, not a DEDUPE KEY.** Dedupe off the field reflecting the row's value-source (what was persisted), not what the operator picked.
- **Price-precision parity between template render and POST float comparison.** If the template renders `%.2f` and the POST compares with a tight epsilon, execution-grain prices falsely flip to "operator edited". Compare with `round(anchor,N) != round(submitted,N)` where N matches display precision.
- **`extended.pop(key, None)` for envelope keys that may not apply** — don't leave a stale form-render default; pop it so downstream dedupe falls through to the fallback match.
- **Audit-envelope empty state must be uniform `None` (not `"[]"`, not `""`) across BOTH the VM emit path and the persist write path** — `"[]"` is truthy and defeats the `... or None` SQL-nullability defense.

### SQLite / transactions / migrations / schema

- **`os.replace` requires same filesystem.** On Windows with Drive-synced dest + `$TMP` on another volume it raises `OSError 18`. Create temp files in the DESTINATION dir (`NamedTemporaryFile(dir=<dest_dir>)`). Never `shutil.move` expecting overwrite on Windows.
- **Python `... or ""` collides with SQL CHECK-constraint nullability** when the enum excludes empty string. Use `... or None` for nullable text columns with CHECK constraints; add a test submitting an empty field asserting NULL persisted.
- **SQLite `INSERT OR REPLACE` / bare `REPLACE` is `DELETE old + INSERT new`** — cascade-wipes child rows via `ON DELETE CASCADE`, issues a NEW PK, rewrites history. For audit/uniqueness tables use SELECT-then-UPDATE-or-INSERT. **(Amended 2026-08-25, the 22-A epoch finding): REPLACE's implicit DELETE does NOT fire DELETE triggers unless `PRAGMA recursive_triggers` is ON — it is OFF by default and ZERO hits repo-wide — so a DELETE-trigger barrier is FAIL-OPEN to `REPLACE`.** Guard immutable/seeded rows with a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger (created AFTER the seeding row), never a DELETE trigger alone.
- **Service-layer `with conn:` opens its own transaction** — do NOT call it from inside an outer single-transaction (inner context-manager commits the connection's single transaction). When composing multi-step atomic side-effects, call the REPO-level functions directly; preserve the repo-vs-service asymmetry.
- **(#9) `sqlite3.executescript()` issues an implicit COMMIT and runs statements in autocommit** — `conn.rollback()` can't undo intermediate statements. Migration runner MUST do explicit `BEGIN`+`executescript`+`COMMIT` with try/except `rollback()`+re-raise (`swing/data/db.py:_apply_migration`, foreign_keys=OFF at runner level). Test rollback through the real runner path, not bare `executescript`.
- **`in_transaction` "auto-detect outer transaction" guards re-introduce the race the explicit lock closed.** Single-transaction service contract: caller MUST NOT hold an open tx; function ALWAYS owns `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/COMMIT/ROLLBACK; REJECT (don't auto-detect) caller-held transactions. Environment short-circuits (sandbox/dry-run) live in the INNER (caller-tx) function so the outer tx-discipline (reject-caller-held / BEGIN IMMEDIATE) stays uniform.
- **Reconciliation flow pivot uses SAVEPOINT-per-discrepancy inside the outer run transaction** (`SAVEPOINT correction_sp_<id>` / RELEASE on success / ROLLBACK TO+RELEASE on exception) — without it a partial mutation commits on the outer COMMIT.
- **SELECT-first idempotency MUST precede payload validation** — a terminal-state row must return its existing audit-row id even with a stale/None payload. Step order: sandbox short-circuit → SELECT + None-check → terminal-state idempotent return → payload validation → atomic write.
- **Counter staleness after inline state mutation** — a flow that emits rows incrementing a counter AND later mutates those rows' states must decrement per-mutation OR recompute via `SELECT COUNT(*)` post-loop.
- **Queries `ORDER BY started_ts DESC` on `pipeline_runs` mask prior completes mid-run** (a NULL-`finished_ts` row wins). Two-read pattern: most-recent COMPLETED row's `finished_ts` for "last good data"; most-recent-started row's `state` for "what's happening now".
- **(#11) Schema-CHECK + Python-constant + dataclass-validator MUST land in ONE task** for atomic consistency — and this EXTENDS to semantic contracts layered atop the CHECK (cache-key shapes, partial-index existence semantics): mirror EACH in `__post_init__`, not just the schema CHECK. When widening a CHECK enum, grep ALL `swing/` for hardcoded copies of the old tuple/enum (multiple Python mirrors: constants, `__post_init__`, repo guards, per-surface `_call_endpoint` guards) AND audit each as manual-input-allowlist (tight) vs service-only (full-widened). Read-path `_row_to_*` mappers MUST be widened in the same task as the write-path. Schema-version-aware INSERT: detect version via `PRAGMA table_info` and branch column-lists OR migrate all pre-version fixtures. **(Amended 2026-08-24, the 22-A `freeze_tier` widening): once a value crosses SQL + Python + a TRIGGER body + a JSON envelope + prose, the canonical triple UNDERSTATES the mirror family — the measured count was ELEVEN sites (three stale, eight value-agnostic-by-luck), and THE ONLY MIRROR THAT DEFENDS THE SET IS THE COMPARATOR (the SQL-vs-Python drift test comparing two representations).** So: the widening sweep is closure-checked by READ (not token grep), and the drift test is a MANDATORY member of the mirror set. **(Second facet, 2026-08-25, the 22-A minting trigger — TWELFTH site): a VALUE-SET sweep does not find a HARD-CODED SINGLE MEMBER** (`tier='live_at_acceptance'` unconditionally, in the section that authoritatively specifies the trigger — a false structural-proof label written into the epoch's own migration). **Grep each enum member SEPARATELY, not the tuple**; the drift test remains the one instrument that does not depend on choosing the right grep.
- **Migration backup-gate uses STRICT equality `pre_version == (target - 1)`, NOT `<=`** (multi-version jumps must be separate two-step migrations). Copy the Phase 9 `pre_version == 16 AND target >= 17` clause shape verbatim.
- **sqlite3 cannot bind a list to a single `:name` placeholder** — build dynamic `?` expansion for IN clauses (`",".join("?"*len(values))`); short-circuit empty input (empty `IN ()` is invalid SQL) and return a dataclass with all required sentinel fields.
- **Python and SQLite ROUND DIFFERENTLY at the half: `round(1.125, 2)` = **1.12** in Python (half-to-EVEN) and **1.13** in SQLite (half AWAY FROM ZERO)** — verified by execution, 2026-08-25 (the 22-A option-C finding). A truthful evidence row computed in Python can be REJECTED by a SQLite trigger comparing "the same" values at display precision — a false refusal wearing a precision costume. **ONE ROUNDING AUTHORITY per comparison:** either the comparison runs entirely in one domain (service compares; SQL stores, never rounds), or canonical pre-rounded values are stored and compared BYTEWISE. Never let a Python-rounded value meet a SQLite-rounded value across an equality. Hits ANY Python-computes/SQL-validates price comparison (triggers, CHECKs, generated columns).

- **Cross-bundle pin fixture-shape mismatch silently extends a test-skip pin beyond its schedule** — verify fixture-shape compatibility BEFORE a pin promises an un-skip date.
- **Evidence-tier vs composite-tier score cap distinction** — evidence-tier may reach its spec'd upper bound (e.g. 1.10 undercut bonus); composite-tier clamps at the composite cap (e.g. `min(1.0,...)`). Downstream histograms/normalizers MUST consume the CLAMPED composite, not the raw evidence, or `ValueError`s poison the emit loop.
- **Bounded backward-slice search for anchor-relative detectors** — bound the back-walk by the spec's max-duration constraint (e.g. HTF pole 4-8 weeks); "most recent" / "absolute max" lets a stale historical landmark capture the algorithm.
- **DBW (and any `CandidateWindow` consumer) must check `anchor_reason.startswith("zigzag_pivot")`** to interpret `anchor_date` semantic: `zigzag_pivot*` = base START (swing-low); `ma_crossover`/`high_low_breakout` = TRIGGER event. Raise if a non-zigzag mode is supplied where a swing-low is required.
- **Bad-exemplar isolation in retrieval functions** — per-element try/except around the normalize/transform helper (skip the bad exemplar, continue the cohort) rather than letting one NaN/inf array's `ValueError` bubble up and stamp the whole call `None`.
- **DTW Sakoe-Chiba band infeasibility on asymmetric series → skip-as-no-match** (final DP cell stays `inf`) is the correct V1 semantic; a candidate much shorter/longer than the exemplar corpus may yield zero hits even with planted same-class exemplars.
- **Universe histogram must reflect the POST-template composite** — when a pipeline step mutates `composite_score` after the universe-snapshot point, seed the histogram from the final persisted values, not the pre-template placeholder.
- **(#27) Silent-skip-without-audit in pipeline steps masks state drift.** An early-return "no work" guard inside a best-effort try/except (which only catches exceptions) completes "successfully" with zero work + zero audit. Empty-pool/early-return paths MUST emit a `warnings_json` entry (expected vs actual pool size + reason). Also: dispatch briefs MUST verify "since X shipped" run-count claims against `git log` of the cited commit.
- **(#28) Pattern-exemplar OHLCV cache discipline:** exemplar tickers are OUTSIDE the candidate universe, so their bars are never fetched by `_step_ohlcv`; template-match Pass 2 then silently no-ops with all-`None` scores (cache miss swallowed per bad-exemplar isolation). A detection harness relying on an exemplar corpus MUST pre-fetch exemplar OHLCV OR emit an `exemplar_load_failure_count` + WARNING OR document the precondition.
- **(#29) Exemplar OHLCV pre-fetch HISTORICAL DEPTH:** yfinance default `period="5y"` is insufficient for pre-2021 historical exemplar `end_date`s (manifests as the SAME 100%-`None` symptom as #28 even after presence is fixed — `OhlcvCoverageError: sliced=0`). Pre-fetch with `period="max"` (or a window from `MIN(end_date) - 200d`). Multi-stage silent-no-op chains need stage-by-stage manifest counters to localize the next blocker.

### Research-harness V1↔V2 parity (applied research)

- **(#24) Parallel-archive freshness desync** — when two archive shapes exist for the same logical data (`{T}.parquet` legacy + `{T}.yfinance.parquet` Shape A) and a reader consumes ONE, asymmetric writer schedules create per-ticker boundary-bar staleness that invalidates V1↔V2 baseline-parity claims. Document the producer/consumer set per shape + freshness precondition; V2.5 candidate: prefer-fresher-by-mtime gate.
- **(#25) Sentinel-bucket parity-comparison discipline** — baseline-parity tests comparing two systems' bucket assignments MUST filter SENTINEL buckets one system pre-empts (`excluded`/`error`) and the other naively recomputes (e.g. V1 short-circuits open-position/ETF-blocklist; V2's `bucket_for` only emits `{aplus,watch,skip}`). Filter sentinel-bucket candidates from the parity diff.
- **(#26) OHLCV archive bar-content TEMPORAL mutation** between V1's persisted-eval-run time and V2's current-archive read time (`write_window` drop_duplicates `keep='last'`; yfinance re-fetch drifts historical bars ~0.5-3%) invalidates V1↔V2 criterion-level parity. V2 evaluator is correct given inputs; characterize as an L6-style limitation (immutable-archive-snapshot is the V2/V3 fix). Distinguish skip→watch flips (delta_watch only) from skip→aplus (affects binding-variable ranking).

### Windows / tooling / test-discipline

- **Windows PowerShell stdout defaults to cp1252; non-ASCII glyphs (§ → ↔ ✓ ✗ em-dash, fractions, etc.) in any `print()`/`click.echo()`/`sys.stdout.write()` path raise `UnicodeEncodeError` and crash the CLI.** pytest `capsys` bypasses the OS encoder so tests pass against code that crashes in production. Fix: prefer ASCII swaps in user-facing strings (canonical pattern); the `sys.stdout`/`stderr` UTF-8 `errors='replace'` reconfigure at CLI entry is the safety net. Add a subprocess-through-PowerShell test for stdout encoding.
- **Tests exercising `swing/config_user.py:write_user_overrides` MUST monkeypatch BOTH `USERPROFILE` AND `HOME`** before invoking — `_user_home()` reads them unmonkeypatched and writes leak to the operator's real `~/swing-data/user-config.toml`.
- **Byte-parity / algorithmic tests are INSUFFICIENT substitutes for operator-visual gates when fixtures bypass the production data-derivation path.** A byte-parity test where both paths consume identical stub fixtures only asserts "same inputs → same outputs"; it misses regressions in HOW inputs are derived (e.g. the Schwab minute-default footgun). Production-path regression tests must exercise the actual wiring; never call an algorithmic test a "STRONG" visual-gate substitute without verifying it hits the production derivation path.
- **Phase 9 risk_policy ratification is single-fire at v16→v17** (gated `pre_version <= 16 AND post_version >= 17`); re-firing would clobber operator CLI policy edits. Repair path: per-field `swing config policy import-from-toml`. Add a run-db-migrate-twice no-op test.
- **All four risk_policy cascade emitters MUST do the no-op-skip check before `supersede_active_policy`** (CLI `policy set`, CLI `reset`, web `POST /config`, web `POST /config/reset/{field}`); a no-op action otherwise creates a spurious `policy_id` + clobbers the predecessor's `effective_to`. Future emitters MUST mirror it; add a `test_<emitter>_no_op_value_does_not_supersede`.
- **Research L2 tests that raw `del sys.modules` + re-import are xdist-order-fragile.** Several harness L2-reinforcement tests (`pattern_cohort`, `double_bottom_w`, `w_bottom`) delete + re-import their package + the forbidden modules WITHOUT restoring; a sibling cross-module `is`-identity assertion (`test_ohlcv_reader_re_export_identity`) can then intermittently fail under `-n auto` (`--dist load`, where `@pytest.mark.xdist_group` is INERT — only `--dist loadgroup` honors it). Fix pattern: make the identity test reconcile both modules from ONE fresh import + restore prior `sys.modules` (order-independent, `4f3ccfe3`), OR make the raw-`del` tests hermetic. Adding tests perturbs worker balance and surfaces latent instances; reproduce with `-n 0` + explicit test ordering, not by re-running `-n auto`. **(RESOLVED for `swing.*` 2026-06-13, Phase 17 Arc 17-D.4, `f14c5b6e`..`0867337d`):** a `tests/research/conftest.py` autouse fixture (+ `_sys_modules_isolation.py`) now snapshots `swing.*` at each research test's setup and restores the `sys.modules` entry + parent-package attr at teardown, healing the raw-`del` polluter for the whole class (the trigger here was the unrestored `del` of `swing.integrations.schwab.*` rebuilding exception classes with new identities → `swing/web/routes/schwab.py`'s import-bound `except` missing them → intermittent web-route 500s). Scope is `swing.*` ONLY (restoring `research.harness.*` would frankenstein that tree). A NEW raw-`del` of a `swing.*` module under `tests/research/` is now self-healing; the same pattern OUTSIDE `tests/research/`, or a raw-`del` of a non-`swing.*` module, would still need its own hermetic teardown.
- **Adding a write-barrier to a repo WRITE function breaks tests that seed invalid/edge data THROUGH that function — and the break can be CROSS-ARC (only the merged-head suite catches it).** A guard rejecting non-finite/malformed input at the sole writer (e.g. the 18-B.1 OHLC barrier in `insert_observation`) rejects the very rows that DETECTION / monitor / consumer tests plant. **Fix:** a test needing a "bad" pre-existing row MUST plant it via RAW `conn.execute` INSERT (bypassing the barrier) — it tests DETECTION of historical bad data, not the write path (the same technique as 18-B.1's read-preservation lock). **Cross-arc trap:** when the barrier and the seeding tests ship in SEPARATE arcs off DIVERGENT bases (one base predates the other's tests), neither arc's own before-review suite sees the interaction — ONLY the orchestrator's merged-head no-false-green re-run does (its reason for existing). 18-B.1×18-D, 2026-06-15, `e7c61f98`.
- **A release/finalization test MUST replicate the FULL production reference graph** — every closure / cache / caller that holds the resource — not just the one reference the brief named. **18-H.4:** the WinError-32 self-lock fix cleared `app.state.schwab_client` + `gc.collect()`, but two ladder closures (`_quote_hook`/`_bars_hook`, `swing/web/app.py:351/:379`, stored on the app-lifetime price/ohlcv caches) hold TWO MORE strong refs → `gc` can't finalize → the `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` handle stays open → the lock PERSISTS. The regression test injected a bare stub (ONE ref; ladder-inactive in the test → no cache closures) → it went GREEN against an INEFFECTIVE fix (the synthetic-vs-production-emitter gotcha family). **Fix:** a release/finalize test installs the REAL holders (the production closures/caches/callers) over the resource + asserts the release actually FINALIZES it (the handle is freed), not just that one ref is cleared. (Paired with the recipe's PRODUCTION-CODE repo-access review note — a diff-only review is blind to the surrounding closures.) 18-H.4×codex-auto-review, 2026-06-16.
- **A session-scoped suite invariant over a LIVE MUTABLE SHARED tree (`comms/`, `exports/`) is inherently flaky in this multi-agent repo — scope the belt to the THREAT SIGNATURE, never to world-frozenness.** The 19-B comms-isolation DETECTION belt (`tests/conftest.py:_fail_suite_on_real_comms_write`) `rglob`-snapshotted the WHOLE real `comms/` tree at session start and asserted it unchanged at teardown. Under `-n auto` a session-scoped autouse fixture runs ONCE PER WORKER (this box = 16 cores → 16 workers), and `comms/` legitimately churns during a multi-minute run (director/orchestrator mail, `inbox→read` acks) → every worker's teardown assert tripped on that churn → **16 spurious per-worker ERRORS on the merged-head run, gone on re-run** (a mechanism argument, not a clean re-run, is the flake proof). **Fix:** key the belt on the production PUSH SIGNATURE (`_LATEST_JSON_POINTER`, IMPORTED not hard-coded so it can't silently rot — the D21 decay class), scope to ADDED `inbox/` files only (drop the removals check — `inbox→read` is legit churn), and make the failure message disambiguate leaked-test-push vs genuine-concurrent-production-push (list paths + first lines + "verify run-id against `pipeline_runs`"). The function-scoped seam-redirect fixture is the real PREVENTION; the session belt only guards the forgot-the-seam class. 19-B×RD+CHARC, 2026-07-04.

This file is project-specific and lives in the repo. ## Role and operating pattern

You are the **orchestrator instance** for the Swing Trading project. Your collaborator is the developer (Reid Smythe). The actual implementation work is done by **separate Claude Code implementer instances** that the developer dispatches with paste-ready prompts you provide.

**The pattern is:**

1. Developer raises a need (bug, strategic question, feature, study).
2. You and the developer discuss tradeoffs and decide on scope.
3. You draft a comprehensive **dispatch brief** as a Markdown file in `docs/`.
4. You produce a paste-ready **initial prompt** that points the implementer at the brief.
5. Developer dispatches a fresh Claude Code instance with that prompt.
6. Implementer executes the brief (TDD, adversarial review, etc.) and returns a structured **return report**.
7. Developer relays the return report to you.
8. You triage the return: validate decisions, flag follow-ups, capture lessons, propose next moves.
9. Loop.

**Key principle: the developer drives, you serve.** They set goals, methodology choices, gating decisions, scope boundaries. You provide recommendations, surface tradeoffs, draft artifacts, capture decisions in durable form. You do NOT decide on the developer's behalf when they haven't yet decided. When in doubt, present options with your recommendation and ask.

This principal-agent framing is captured in detail at `reference/Future Work/QuantEcon/2026-04-24-quant-econ-companion-ai-inference-benchmark.md` §"AI's role in this project — operator drives, agent serves."

## Three-branch architecture (key refinement to V2.1)

V2.1 specifies two branches: Operational + Research-and-Verification. A 2026-04-24 refinement distinguishes two sub-branches within Research:

| Branch | Activity | Per-study horizon | Canonical example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Operational** | Daily decision-making with promoted methods | Continuous | The `swing/` codebase |
| **Applied Research** | Testing rules developed elsewhere | Weeks–months per study | Earnings-proximity-exclusion (Sessions 2a/b/c) |
| **Basic Research** | Discovering/refining rules at first principles | Months–years per investigation | QuantEcon program (Themes 1–4) |

**Branches are permanent capability, not time-bounded projects.** Idle ≠ failure ≠ dismantle. Branch infrastructure (harness scaffolding, method-record format, cache directories, study templates) persists across idle periods. Time budget is allocated dynamically — 100% to whichever branch has an active study/investigation, idle when none.

Promotion path: Basic Research → Applied Research → Operational.

Full detail: `reference/Future Work/QuantEcon/2026-04-24-quant-econ-companion-trigger-purpose-three-branch.md`.
