## Pre-Codex review + brief-authoring disciplines

> **Relocated (compressed) from CLAUDE.md 2026-05-28** per the operator-paired CLAUDE.md size restructure (Option B: compress code gotchas in CLAUDE.md + split process/review disciplines here). These are the **process / review / brief-authoring meta-disciplines** — they fire at orchestrator / dispatch / Codex-review time, NOT at code-write time (code-failure gotchas stay in `CLAUDE.md`). Full pre-compression verbatim text (dates, commit SHAs, Codex rounds, findings docs) → [`docs/CLAUDE.md-archive.md`](docs/CLAUDE.md-archive.md) §"Appended 2026-05-28". `#N` / "Expansion #N" labels are preserved so cross-references in shipped briefs still resolve. **Apply all of these in the pre-Codex review pass at every dispatch's brainstorming + writing-plans + executing-plans phases** (the cumulative "C.C lesson #6 validation").

### Pre-Codex review "Expansion #N" catalog (verify-before-lock)

- **Expansion #2 — brief-vs-actual-production-function-signature.** When a brief/spec/plan references a production function, grep its DEFINITION + verify (a) signature (param names, positional vs keyword, types); (b) side-effect contract (read-only vs write vs fetch-on-miss); (c) error semantics (raises vs None vs default); (d) documented invariants. Re-grep at writing-plans.
  - **#2 sub-refinement — cascade-call-graph.** Also verify whether the function invokes its documented sibling helpers (grep the body); don't infer cascade from naming/docstring. Under `from __future__ import annotations`, resolve return annotations via `typing.get_type_hints`, not raw `inspect.signature` (returns string forms).
- **Expansion #4 — SQL skeleton column verification.** Every SQL skeleton's columns / JOIN-ON / WHERE / subquery verified against the actual `swing/data/migrations/*.sql` before publishing. Brief-vs-actual schema reality check: grep migrations for any proposed NEW table/column before claiming it's new (it may already exist).
  - **#4 refinement — JOIN-cardinality + downstream-sufficiency.** Per JOIN, enumerate 1:1 vs 1:N; verify the result row-set is SUFFICIENT for the consumer (e.g. an RS-criterion evaluator needs the FULL universe, not just candidates); re-check the universe after any harness mutation (cleanup/fetch/fill).
  - **#4 sub-refinement — runtime-binding-shape + empty-result-set.** Per parameterized SQL, enumerate the binding shape (scalar vs list vs dict) and empty-input handling. (The sqlite3 list-bind / dynamic-`?` / empty-short-circuit specifics are also kept as a code gotcha in CLAUDE.md.)
- **Expansion #6 — content-completeness audit.** For each spec data-surface checklist item, enumerate per-field disposition LIVE / V1 PLACEHOLDER / V1 STUB before Codex. Silently rendering a stub as if it were live is the failure mode.
- **Expansion #7 — cross-row semantic scope audit.** For any POST handler consuming operator input + a cross-row lookup, enumerate the lookup SCOPE (ticker / pattern_class / candidate / pipeline_run) + cross-check against the spec's wording; add a plant-different-scope discriminating test.
- **Expansion #8 — per-counter / SQL-aggregation UNIT audit.** For each COUNT/SUM/GROUP BY AND each Python accumulator, state what unit it counts; add DISTINCT or CTE-then-aggregate to prevent JOIN-cardinality inflation; verify LIMIT applies at the right unit. Applies to ANY counter, not just SQL aggregates.
- **Expansion #9 — form-render anchor lifecycle audit.** For any hidden form anchor driving POST-time validation, audit 4 dimensions: (a) soft-warn confirm `form_values` round-trip; (b) GET-time query-param consumption; (c) candidate-snapshot consistency across pipeline runs; (d) explicit-anchor-vs-latest-snapshot validation order. (POST-time rejection-ladder + server-recompute are code gotchas in CLAUDE.md.)
- **Expansion #10 — architecture-location audit (+ 4 sub-disciplines).** When wiring NEW logic into an EXISTING module, verify the module has the dependency-context to host it (else new module + DI). Sub-disciplines: (a) triangulate template-vs-VM-parser-vs-emitter for "doesn't render" gaps; (b) renderer-kwargs uniformity LOCK + cache-collision test when a surface enum is reused by 2+ callers; (c) SQL LIKE wildcard-escape raw-vs-escaped per binding position; (d) orphan-label preservation when refactoring exact-match → delimiter-aware groupings.
- **Expansion #11 — taxonomy / attribution propagation audit.** When introducing a NEW enum (`kind`/`status`/`type`) OR any attribution metadata (`variable_name`/`source`/`tier`), propagate to all derived dataclasses + serializers (CSV/JSON/markdown headers) + test fixtures; downstream rendering must map by the FIELD, not a value-matching heuristic; paired `old_X`/`new_X` must source from the SAME baseline.
- **Expansion #12 — sibling-route audit under single-anchor-binding.** When introducing a single-anchor-binding discipline at one route, enumerate ALL sibling routes touching the same data/cache layer + verify each carries the anchor; the NO-RUN scenario must refuse a silent "resolve-latest-now" fallback (explicit None-guard + unavailable banner).
- **Expansion #13 — cumulative regression cascade audit.** When a Codex MAJOR fix RESTRUCTURES code (extract function / move logic out of a loop / new field), run an "imagined next-round" pass for 2nd-order regressions before invoking the next round; add tests for the NEW invariants the restructure creates.
- **Expansion #14 — recency / filter / dedup semantic-ordering audit.** For N sequential filter/dedup/aggregation steps, audit order of operations + attribution-metadata propagation (max/min/all of which field) + the downstream consumer's reference asof (filter-admit vs walk-forward must use the same asof).
- **Expansion #15 — narrative artifact path/fact lag.** A post-fix-bundle commit MUST sweep ALL narrative docs (findings, return reports, study writeups, status lines) for stale artifact paths + per-row facts (entry dates, R-values, session/column counts) whenever a new smoke artifact is emitted or any outcome shifts.
- **Expansion #16 — ASCII discipline scope clarity.** Declare ASCII scope EXPLICITLY across ALL flowing-through-stdout surfaces (narrative + source + tests + smoke + manifest + CLI help) and assert programmatically via `text.encode("ascii")` over the declared set. (The CLI-stdout cp1252 crash is a code gotcha in CLAUDE.md.)
- **Expansion #6/#7 process note — the 5-expansion pass does NOT catch content-completeness vs spec text NOR cross-row semantic scope on operator-input flows** unless #6 + #7 are run explicitly; pre-Codex review must walk each spec data-surface item + each cross-row lookup scope.
- **Pre-Codex review must cross-check spec source-of-truth against dispatch-brief sketches** — the brief's prescriptions (caps, tuples, thresholds) may be wrong vs the spec's BINDING text at the cited section; verify against the spec, not the brief alone.

### Brief-authoring + applied-research methodology disciplines

- **(#33) Cohort-validity-vs-verdict-criteria.** Briefs with criterion-based verdict thresholds MUST additionally bind the evaluation cohort; if the canonical cohort yields fewer than N patterns, report INSUFFICIENT SAMPLE — do NOT substitute a more-favorable alternative cohort. (Banned narrative terms LOCK also lives here.)
- **(#34) Brief-prescription cross-table verification.** When a brief prescribes a (sweep_point + count) tuple from an analytical artifact, cross-check the artifact SUMMARY TABLE (authoritative) against the per-variable drill-down header; the summary table wins on disagreement.
- **(#35) Substrate-density metric disambiguation.** When a brief carries a numerical anchor (density/survival/rate/fraction) from a prior arc, quote the exact numerator + denominator + pre-filter + semantic intent; verify metric-compatibility with the new brief's usage (e.g. `F/T` per-ticker productivity ≠ `F/R_raw` survival rate).
- **(#36) Two-Codex-chain default for applied research dispatches.** Default to TWO Codex chains: chain #1 implementation review BEFORE smoke-artifact emission; chain #2 methodology + narrative review AFTER smoke + findings draft. Single-chain requires explicit Sec 7 justification (e.g. <100 LoC, no smoke, no findings narrative). The single C.C-lesson-#6 validation slot spans both chains.
- **(#37) Substrate-freshness sensitivity.** Briefs carrying a prior-arc cohort fixture + R-value anchor MUST cite (a) the cohort fixture SHA; (b) the filter params; (c) the source-artifact SHA the fixture derived from; (d) a regeneration-stability assertion. Implementer Slice-1 discriminating test asserts brief-stated N matches actual filtered-N within tolerance; escalate via Brief Amendment on mismatch (cohort fixtures regenerated over time drift their FILTERED membership — `max_observed_asof_date` shifts patterns in/out of recency windows).
- **(#38) Pre-commission premise verification — does the capability already exist?** Before scoping a NEW-capability arc (new command/module/mechanism), grep ALL of `swing/` for a PRE-EXISTING mechanism that already provides it — not just the one adjacent mechanism you happen to know. The capability-level analog of Expansion #4's "grep migrations before claiming a table is new." Failure mode (17-C, 2026-06-13): the orchestrator commissioned `swing exports cleanup` for exports retention having found only the adjacent `_prune_shadow_expectancy_artifacts`; `swing/rendering/retention.py:archive_old_exports` (a DIFFERENT package) already zip-retained dated `exports/<date>/` dirs every pipeline run → the arc was redundant at the 90d default + data-UNSAFE at shorter windows. Caught only at writing-plans by the implementer's brief-vs-live-code grounding (Expansion #2). Grep BEYOND the package you expect; verify the arc's FOUNDING PREMISE ("X doesn't exist yet"), not just the referenced-function signatures. Memory: `feedback_brief_premise_check_existing_mechanism`.
- **(#39) Schema-boundary defensive-scope — don't build per-case handling for schema-forbidden data (operator, 2026-06-15).** Data states the SCHEMA forbids (`NOT NULL` / `CHECK` / `UNIQUE` / typed columns) are caught at the WRITE boundary (the constrained writer / repo / migration). A downstream READER (monitor / consumer / aggregator over OUR OWN constrained DB) MUST NOT proliferate per-value-shape branches for out-of-schema values; it needs only (a) a GENERAL error handler that degrades gracefully (never crashes) + (b) LOGGING sufficient to IDENTIFY the gap if a hole ever lets bad data pass. In briefs/plans for readers, scope defensive handling to genuinely-unconstrained inputs (missing / pre-schema tables, absent / corrupt FILES, external-API payloads) + that one general degrade+log path — NOT per-malformed-value cases for schema-constrained columns. **Review-adjudication corollary:** a Codex finding premised SOLELY on a malformed / out-of-range / duplicate / NULL value inside a schema-typed column is OUT-OF-SCOPE-for-V1 (cite the constraint) — NOT a blocking major; converge once only that class remains. This BOUNDS what counts as a blocking major; it does NOT reinstate the suspended round cap (memory `feedback_codex_round_limit_suspended`). Origin: the 18-D executing review treadmill (~13 `review-strong` rounds, most surfacing new degraded-VALUE permutations on the same coverage/structural date-parsing — one guard against a schema-`UNIQUE`-prevented duplicate whose test skipped; one R10→R11 fix-introduced regression). Memory: `feedback_schema_boundary_defensive_scope`. **Orchestrator QA check (CHARC-mandated, 2026-06-15; `docs/18-D-treadmill-review-adjudication-charc.md` `a8632d41`; recipe §3 `94ac2905`):** at convergence-verification (the transcript-read of `.copowers-findings.md`), confirm EVERY finding adjudicated "schema-prevented / out-of-scope" CITES the exact constraint (the migration / `CHECK` / `UNIQUE` / `NOT NULL` / FK line) AND verify that constraint actually prevents the value — READ the migration; never ASSUME the defense (the 18-E lesson: a `CHECK` weaker than claimed, or a column missing the constraint, is a REAL hole, not dead code). A dismissal WITHOUT a verified citation is wrongly-dismissed → re-open it (it stays in-scope). This citation-verification is the safety valve that keeps the corollary from becoming a footgun.
- **V1-simplification banking discipline.** Every V1 placeholder / stub / simplification the implementer ships MUST be enumerated in the return report (§6 or equivalent) WITH its V2 dependency cited. Pre-Codex review's content-completeness audit (#6) is the gate; the return-report table is the permanent ledger.

### Process hygiene

- **(#1) Test-count drift in plan docs.** Plan/brief test-count estimates go stale — trust `pytest` output, not the plan. (Same failure family as cohort-size estimates being empirically falsified.)
- **Auto-memory staleness.** The auto-memory at `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/` can go stale (e.g. `project_refactor_intent`); verify against current `git log` before relying on it.
- **Executing dispatches run the FULL fast suite BEFORE the Codex review AND after it converges (universal; banked 2026-06-15, operator-directed).** Two runs, two distinct failure modes: **(1) BEFORE** — after all task-commits land, run `pytest -m "not slow" -q` and fix any failure BEFORE starting the Codex loop, so the review converges on a GREEN diff. This catches **cross-cutting / global-invariant tests** that per-task TDD does NOT exercise — e.g. `test_topbar_cross_vm_consistency` ("every base-layout VM in the manifest"), `test_theme_css` ("no raw hex outside the theme blocks"), schema-enum-mirror tests — which otherwise stay latent until the end-of-run suite, AFTER the review has already converged, forcing a wasted fix + re-review cycle (the 18-F cost: the theme-token + VM-manifest regressions surfaced only at the final full-suite run, post-convergence → an extra cycle). **(2) AFTER** — once Codex converges, re-run the full suite on the final diff: the binding no-false-green gate that catches review-FIX-introduced breaks. The orchestrator includes BOTH runs in every executing-dispatch prompt's verification steps. (Flagged to CHARC 2026-06-15 to mirror this in `docs/implementer-dispatch-recipe.md` §verification — the implementer SPOF.)

## Maintenance: retention discipline

> Added 2026-05-05 as part of the handoff-document structural separation refactor. This section governs ongoing curation of this file + `docs/phase3e-todo.md` to keep fresh-orchestrator bootstrap consumption bounded over time.

### Active vs archive boundary

Two pairs of handoff docs:

- `docs/orchestrator-context.md` (active; canonical filename) + `docs/orchestrator-context-archive.md`
- `docs/phase3e-todo.md` (active; canonical filename) + `docs/phase3e-todo-archive.md`

Bootstrap discipline: fresh-orchestrator session reads only the active files (this one + `docs/phase3e-todo.md`) + `CLAUDE.md` + `git log -20` + `git status`. Archive companions are searchable on demand via Grep / Read.

### Brief-corpus archival at phase close (CHARC-authored — harness convention; canonical text in `tool-director-context.md §4.3`)

At each phase close, the close-housekeeping ritual `git mv`s that phase's DEAD dispatch artifacts — commissioning/dispatch briefs, writing-/executing-plans, implementation plans, orchestrator handoffs, per-arc audits + Codex review transcripts — into `docs/archive/phase<N>/`. **No cooldown** (a merged arc's brief is dead; this differs from the one-phase-cooldown for `phase3e-todo.md` SHIPPED entries below). The live durable docs stay top-level: charters, the `*-state.md` pointers, `harness-architecture.md`, the active-phase `todo`, `implementer-dispatch-recipe.md`, `runbooks/`, comms-design docs, references. This makes the existing `docs/archive/phase16`/`phase17` practice a standing rule. The probe (`harness_probe.py`, §4.2) counts top-level `docs/*.md`, so this archival reduces the tracked corpus. **Phase-18 close = ALSO sweep the one-time pre-phase-16 + Phase-18 backlog (~450 top-level files; bucket by phase where determinable, else a `docs/archive/pre-phase-16/` catch-all).** CHARC's phase-close audit verifies the top-level count dropped. **Sweep safety (CHARC-authored 2026-07-03 — D21):** a docs-only `git mv` is NOT suite-neutral — research L2-reinforcement tests hard-code `docs/<brief>.md` paths (6 broke at the Phase-18 sweep; main sat 6-red for 6 days). Before committing a sweep, grep `tests/` + `swing/` + `scripts/` for every moved filename (repath or defer any referenced file); re-run the fast suite AFTER the sweep commit — the close's "suite green" claim must postdate the close ritual's LAST commit. When that grep hits a TEST reference, consult the test's retirement marker: brief-coupled doc-assertions are ARC-LIFECYCLE-SCOPED (RD standard 2026-07-03, D21) — retire-at-close once the content is banked per RD's close-time check, repath only the rare still-load-bearing case; artifact/harness LOCKS in the same files stay.

### Cooldown rules (when to migrate)

Migration triggers, in order of frequency:

1. **End of phase ship.** When a phase merges to main, migrate that phase's SHIPPED `phase3e-todo.md` entries to the archive. One-phase cooldown (don't archive the same phase that just shipped — give one ship-cycle of "still warm" context). Worked example: Phase 7 shipped 2026-05-05 at `c617777`; Phase 6 SHIPPED entries (Phase 6 sub-bundle of journal v1.2) migrated to archive at this dispatch. Phase 7 SHIPPED entry migrates to archive at end of next phase ship (Phase 8 or Phase 9, whichever lands first).
2. **Lessons-captured cap.** Active `Lessons captured` section maintains last ~30 entries. When a new lesson lands and pushes the count past 30, the oldest lesson migrates to archive (or promotes to CLAUDE.md if it's durable code-failure prevention; see below).
3. **Recent-decisions supersession.** When a "Recent decisions and framings" entry is fully superseded by a later decision, archive the old entry with a cross-ref to the superseding one. When refined (not fully superseded), keep both with cross-ref. Default-conservative: when in doubt, KEEP in active. Re-litigation risk dominates.
4. **Tripwire-fired entries.** When a trigger-gated `phase3e-todo.md` entry resolves (e.g., 2026-05-04 worktree-cleanup-script entry RESOLVED 2026-05-05), migrate to archive with `TRIGGER FIRED + RESOLVED YYYY-MM-DD` footer. Mirror the worktree-cleanup-script + handoff-document-growth precedents.

### Lesson promotion: archive vs CLAUDE.md

For lessons being aged out of the active section:

- **Promote to CLAUDE.md gotchas** if the lesson durably prevents code failure for future sessions (e.g., yfinance API regressions; HTMX failure surfaces; Windows ACL gotchas; SQL/Python idiom collisions; matplotlib mathtext quirks). CLAUDE.md is auto-loaded so the gotcha fires every session, not just when grep'd.
- **Archive (no promotion)** if the lesson is process-only / single-incident-historical / discipline-applied-to-orchestrator-thread (e.g., commit-message convention refinements; subagent-collision diagnosis history; specific phase-handoff items).

Most older lessons (the 96 archived 2026-05-05) fall into "archive only" — their durable code-failure prevention has already landed in CLAUDE.md gotchas. Re-promotion would duplicate.

### Archive-split trigger (hierarchical decomposition deferred)

If an archive file exceeds **~80k tokens** (mirrors the active-file pressure point that motivated the original split), revisit hierarchical decomposition. Likely categorization at that point: SHIPPED-by-phase + lessons-by-domain (HTMX / yfinance / Windows / SQLite / dispatch-discipline / brief-drafting) + decisions-by-quarter. Defer category invention until the trigger fires — data informs categories better than upfront design.

### Size-check trigger at housekeeping-commit time (added 2026-05-18 PM per CLAUDE.md evaluator pass — Option B2 restructure)

At every housekeeping-commit step (when appending a new SHIPPED entry to status-tracking docs), verify the following soft thresholds — if exceeded, the housekeeping commit MUST include a triage step (archive-split, restructure, or compact-summary swap) rather than silently growing the surface:

| Doc | Surface | Soft threshold | Trigger response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` line 3 ("Current state" summary) | Single paragraph; pointer-heavy; not a SHIPPED ledger | **>2,000 chars** | Trim back to ~5-10 sentences; preserve as compact summary; do NOT regress to a ledger paragraph (history goes to `docs/CLAUDE.md-archive.md`). |
| `CLAUDE.md` §"Gotchas" (added 2026-05-28 Option B) | Code/runtime/test failure-prevention; **trigger + fix only** | **>~55K chars total, OR any single gotcha >~700 chars, OR a process/review discipline added here instead of to orchestrator-context** | Compress the new/oversized gotcha to trigger+fix at banking time; relocate any process/review/brief-authoring discipline to this file's §"Pre-Codex review + brief-authoring disciplines"; append the full forensic detail (dates/SHAs/Codex-rounds) to `docs/CLAUDE.md-archive.md`. Do NOT bank verbose multi-paragraph forensic gotchas into CLAUDE.md. |
| `docs/orchestrator-context.md` §"Currently in-flight work" | Active + "Prior state" sub-sections | **>10 "Prior state" sub-sections retained** (per L-W2 conservative cap) | Trim oldest "Prior state" sub-sections to `docs/orchestrator-context-archive.md`. |
| `docs/orchestrator-context.md` §"Lessons captured" | Most-recent N retained per cap target | **>~40 entries** (cap target ~30; trigger at +10 over) | Migrate oldest 5-10 to archive companion. |
| `docs/phase3e-todo.md` (active SHIPPED entries) | Top-prepended SHIPPED entries | **>~25 SHIPPED entries** retained (or one quarter's worth) | Archive-split old SHIPPED entries to `docs/phase3e-todo-archive.md`. |
| `docs/CLAUDE.md-archive.md` + `docs/orchestrator-context-archive.md` + `docs/phase3e-todo-archive.md` | Append-only history companions | **No size threshold** (append-only by design) | N/A — companion docs grow; grep-on-demand only. Per §"Archive-split trigger" above, hierarchical decomposition reconsidered at ~80k tokens per file. |

**Rationale for the line 3 cap:** the Phase 12.5 #3 evaluator pass (2026-05-18 PM) surfaced that line 3 had grown to ~133K chars (~40K-50K tokens loaded into every fresh Claude Code session). Option B2 restructure replaced it with a compact ~1.3K-char "Current state" summary; this cap discipline prevents regression to the wall-of-text shape. The "current state" line is meant to be a 5-10-sentence orientation for fresh sessions, pointing them at `docs/orchestrator-context.md` + `docs/phase3e-todo.md` for detail.

**Pattern for triage at housekeeping-commit time (operator-driven OR orchestrator-self-checked):**
1. Pre-commit (before drafting the housekeeping commit message): compute size of each surface above (`wc -c`, char counts, sub-section counts).
2. If any threshold exceeded: PAUSE the housekeeping-commit + draft a restructure plan + escalate to operator decision (do NOT defer to next session — defer leads to drift; the wall-of-text shape that motivated this discipline emerged precisely because per-session size pressure was below per-session deferral pressure for months).
3. If thresholds clear: proceed with housekeeping-commit normally.

**Where this discipline applies:** every housekeeping commit landing after an integration merge OR after a meaningful in-flight decision worth recording in handoff docs. The operator-facing daily routine at [`docs/cycle-checklist.md`](docs/cycle-checklist.md) does NOT include this discipline (it's purely operator-trading-cadence; housekeeping is an orchestrator action). A brief cross-reference is added at the bottom of cycle-checklist.md so operators reviewing the routine doc are aware that orchestrator-side housekeeping discipline lives here.

- Orchestrator's wall-clock duration estimates for dispatched work are routinely 3-5x too long. When estimating Phase work, divide naive estimate by 3-5x to land on operator's actual experienced wall-clock.

- Per-run-vs-per-fill re-emission family: each fresh reconciliation_run that finds no Schwab match for an open fill emits a new `unmatched_open_fill` discrepancy on that same fill, regardless of prior resolutions.
- Bash tool's persistent cwd across invocations CAN drift away from the primary worktree if earlier commands `cd` into a subdirectory. Use `git -C "<absolute-path>"` for cross-worktree git operations rather than relying on cwd.

## Session-start checklist for fresh orchestrator sessions

1. Read this file end-to-end.
2. Check `git log --oneline -20` to see recent commits.
3. Check `git status` to see untracked files or modified files.
4. Read `CLAUDE.md` (auto-loaded but worth re-skimming for the gotchas list).
5. Skim `docs/phase3e-todo.md` for current operational backlog.
6. Ask the developer: "What's currently in flight or recently dispatched? What's today's question?"
7. If the developer is mid-decision, present options with recommendation; don't decide for them.
8. If the developer raises a new strategic question, propose where in the existing framing it fits before drafting anything.

---

## Session-end checklist (when wrapping up a working session)

1. Update §"Currently in-flight work" with current state.
2. If a meaningful framing decision was made, add to §"Recent decisions and framings."
3. If a process insight was captured, add to §"Lessons captured."
4. If a new file or convention was introduced, update §"Key file locations" or §"Operating processes."
5. **Retention discipline check (per §"Maintenance: retention discipline" above):** end of phase ship → migrate that phase's SHIPPED `phase3e-todo.md` entries to archive (one-phase cooldown); lessons-captured cap exceeded → migrate oldest to archive (or promote to CLAUDE.md if durable code-failure prevention).
6. Don't update for trivia. Bias toward fewer, higher-quality updates.

---

## How to update this file

Small commits via the regular implementer-dispatch pattern, OR direct orchestrator edit during conversation (the developer will commit later as part of housekeeping). Either is fine.

When updating: keep sections in their current order. Add new sub-bullets rather than restructuring sections. The next orchestrator's mental model is shaped by the current organization; preserve it unless the developer agrees to a reorganization.

If active sections grow large enough that bootstrap becomes a token-budget issue, see §"Maintenance: retention discipline" — the structural-separation pattern is established (active vs archive companion); migrate aged content to `docs/orchestrator-context-archive.md` rather than splitting active into multiple files.

   207	def canonicalize_hypothesis_label(raw: str | None) -> str | None:
   208	    """Canonicalize the operator-frozen hypothesis label at the persistence
   209	    boundary so journal-review grouping is invariant to input whitespace,
   210	    embedded control bytes, invisible Unicode format characters, and
   211	    NFC/NFD encoding differences (adversarial review rounds 1 + 2).
   212	
   213	    Steps:
   214	      1. Apply Unicode NFC normalization so canonically-equivalent text
   215	         (composed `é` vs decomposed `e + ̀`) yields one stored form.
   216	      2. Drop any character in Unicode category ``Cf`` (format) — zero-width
   217	         space U+200B, ZWJ U+200D, bidi overrides U+202E/U+2066+, etc. —
   218	         which would otherwise let two visually-identical labels group as
   219	         distinct buckets (R2 M1 spoofing concern).
   220	      3. Replace any character in Unicode category ``Cc`` (control: `\\n`,
   221	         `\\r`, `\\t`, NUL, …) with a single space.
   222	      4. Collapse all whitespace runs to a single space.
   223	      5. Strip leading/trailing whitespace.
   224	      6. Empty result → ``None`` (so an all-whitespace input persists as
   225	         NULL, not as an unnamed labeled bucket).
   226	
   227	    Operator-typed semantic spacing inside a label is preserved (single
   228	    spaces between words); only artifacts that would split otherwise-
   229	    identical labels into distinct grouping keys are removed.
   230	    """
   231	    if raw is None:
   232	        return None
   233	    nfc = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", raw)
   234	    cleaned_chars = []
   235	    for c in nfc:
   236	        cat = unicodedata.category(c)
   237	        if cat == "Cf":
   238	            continue  # invisible format chars: drop entirely
   239	        if cat == "Cc":
   240	            cleaned_chars.append(" ")  # control bytes: replace with space
   241	        else:
   242	            cleaned_chars.append(c)
   243	    canonical = " ".join("".join(cleaned_chars).split())
   244	    return canonical or None
   245

   247	def record_entry(
   248	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, req: EntryRequest, *,
   249	    soft_warn: int, hard_cap: int, force: bool,
   250	    cfg=None,
   251	) -> EntryResult:
   252	    """22-A adds ONE keyword-only parameter, ``cfg``, and that is the whole
   253	    signature change in the arc.  Both production call sites already have it
   254	    (``swing/cli.py``, ``swing/web/routes/trades.py``).
   255	
   256	    ``cfg=None`` DECLINES the latch path with reason ``no_config`` and leaves
   257	    every persisted value byte-identical to the pre-arc behaviour, so every
   258	    pre-existing caller and test is unaffected.
   259	    """
   260	    # Phase 7 Sub-B B.1 — non-bypassable pre-trade required-field gate. Per
   261	    # spec §9.3, MissingPreTradeFieldsException is NOT force-bypassable; it
   262	    # fires BEFORE the existing stop / duplicate / cap checks so an operator
   263	    # can never sneak a partial-state row past the lock by toggling --force.
   264	    # The validator's required-field set + conditional rules live in
   265	    # ``swing.trades.state``; this service just calls + raises.
   266	    #
   267	    # Note: the validator's "always required" set includes `trade_origin` +
   268	    # `pre_trade_locked_at`, which the route/CLI layer doesn't populate on
   269	    # EntryRequest. `pre_trade_locked_at` still uses an interim shim
   270	    # (event_ts); the canonical atomic insert+fill flow lands at B.3.
   271	    #
   272	    # B.2: `trade_origin` is now derived BEFORE validation via the origin
   273	    # service so the validator and the eventual INSERT see the same value
   274	    # the row will be persisted with. The 4-value enum returned by
   275	    # derive_trade_origin always satisfies the validator's required-field
   276	    # check (non-NULL string), so this preserves the gate-fires-first
   277	    # discipline regardless of (bucket × entry_path) combo.
   278	    derived_origin = derive_trade_origin(conn, req.ticker, req.entry_path)
   279	    req_view: dict = {
   280	        f: getattr(req, f, None)
   281	        for f in (
   282	            "ticker", "entry_date", "entry_price", "initial_stop",
   283	            "thesis", "why_now", "invalidation_condition", "expected_scenario",
   284	            "premortem_technical", "premortem_market_sector",
   285	            "premortem_execution", "event_risk_present", "event_handling",
   286	            "event_type", "event_date", "gap_risk_present",
   287	            "gap_risk_handling", "emotional_state_pre_trade",
   288	            "market_regime", "catalyst", "catalyst_other_description",
   289	            "manual_entry_confidence",
   290	        )
   291	    }
   292	    req_view["initial_shares"] = req.shares
   293	    req_view["trade_origin"] = derived_origin
   294	    # Codex R4 Major 1: pre_trade_locked_at + first-fill datetime must
   295	    # reflect when the trade actually entered the market (req.entry_date),
   296	    # not when the operator typed the command (req.event_ts).
   297	    # Codex R5 Major 1: trades.entry_date column is date-only and downstream
   298	    # consumers (advisory, journal/flags+analyze, briefing, CLI hold-duration)
   299	    # call date.fromisoformat(trade.entry_date) directly. So entry_date must
   300	    # remain YYYY-MM-DD only at the API boundary; reject T-form before
   301	    # storing. Synthesis of T16:00:00 for fill_datetime / pre_trade_locked_at
   302	    # happens via the shared helper after the date-only guard.
   303	    from swing.trades.exit import _normalize_trade_event_date_to_iso
   304	    if "T" in req.entry_date:

    65	def _parse_optional_float(raw: str | None) -> float | None:
    66	    if raw is None or raw.strip() == "":
    67	        return None
    68	    try:
    69	        return float(raw)
    70	    except ValueError:
    71	        return None

    73	
    74	def _validate_rationale(
    75	    rationale: str, notes: str | None, rationale_enum,
    76	) -> str | None:
    77	    """Tranche B-ops T4/T5: shared rationale validator.
    78	
    79	    Returns an error message when invalid, or ``None`` when valid. Used by
    80	    the entry and stop-adjust POST routes to enforce closed-taxonomy
    81	    rationale values and the ``other`` → ``notes`` required coupling.
    82	    """
    83	    try:
    84	        value = rationale_enum(rationale)
    85	    except ValueError:
    86	        valid = ", ".join(r.value for r in rationale_enum)
    87	        return f"Invalid rationale: {rationale!r}. Choose one of: {valid}."
    88	    if value.value == "other" and not (notes and notes.strip()):
    89	        return "Notes are required when rationale = Other."
    90	    return None

    93	def _rerender_stop_form_with_error(
    94	    *, request: Request, templates, cfg, trade_id: int,
    95	    new_stop: float, rationale: str, notes: str | None,
    96	    error_message: str,
    97	) -> HTMLResponse:
    98	    """T7: re-render trade_stop_form with preservation fields + banner at 400.
    99	
   100	    Preservation mirrors TradeEntryFormVM's duplicate-re-render pattern:
   101	    typed ``new_stop`` echoes back via ``new_stop_input``; submitted
   102	    ``rationale`` and ``notes`` pre-select/populate their inputs on the
   103	    re-render. ``force`` is deliberately NOT preserved — spec §5 requires
   104	    the operator to tick the Force checkbox each time they want to submit
   105	    a regression-intentional stop, so the rerender path discards the
   106	    submitted force value.
   107	    """
   108	    from dataclasses import replace as dc_replace
   109	    vm = build_stop_form_vm(trade_id=trade_id, cfg=cfg)
   110	    if vm is not None:
   111	        vm = dc_replace(
   112	            vm,
   113	            new_stop_input=new_stop,
   114	            rationale=rationale,
   115	            notes=notes or "",
   116	        )
   117	        return templates.TemplateResponse(
   118	            request, "partials/trade_stop_form.html.j2",
   119	            {"vm": vm, "error_message": error_message},
   120	            status_code=400,
   121	        )
   122	    return templates.TemplateResponse(
   123	        request, "partials/trade_form_error.html.j2",
   124	        {"error_message": error_message},
   125	        status_code=400,
   126	    )

   129	def _emit_sector_tamper_audit(
   130	    *,
   131	    cfg,
   132	    ticker: str,
   133	    cached_sector: str,
   134	    cached_industry: str,
   135	    form_sector: str,
   136	    form_industry: str,
   137	    cand_session_iso: str,
   138	    run_session_iso: str,
   139	    field_name: str,
   140	) -> int:
   141	    """Phase 9 Sub-bundle D Task D.2 — emit ad-hoc system_audit
   142	    reconciliation_run + sector_tamper discrepancy on tamper rejection.
   143	
   144	    Owns its own connection + ``with conn:`` deferred transaction
   145	    (plan §A.4.1: SEPARATE TRANSACTION from any entry-POST tx — entry
   146	    POST is rejected and never commits its own tx). Uses Bundle B's repo
   147	    entry points (``insert_run`` + ``insert_discrepancy`` +
   148	    ``update_run_completed``) directly per plan §A.4 + Sub-bundle B
   149	    return report §10 #1 — does NOT route through Bundle B's
   150	    ``run_tos_reconciliation`` service (which is ``source='tos_csv'``
   151	    only).
   152	
   153	    Returns the inserted ``discrepancy_id`` for test plumbing.
   154	
   155	    Spec §3.3.1 ``sector_tamper`` JSON shapes:
   156	      expected = {"sector": cached_sector, "industry": cached_industry,
   157	                  "session": cand_session_iso}     # cached candidate anchor
   158	      actual   = {"sector": form_sector, "industry": form_industry}
   159	
   160	    Plan §A.4.1: reconciliation_run row's ``period_{start,end}`` =
   161	    ``run_session_iso`` (today's ``action_session_for_run(now())``) —
   162	    describes WHEN the audit happened. Distinct from
   163	    ``cand_session_iso`` which is the cached candidate's
   164	    ``eval_run.action_session_date`` (i.e., the session anchor for the
   165	    data the operator saw at form-render time). The two MAY differ when
   166	    the form was rendered before today's pipeline run completed (Codex
   167	    R1 Major #1 anchor-alignment fix).
   168	
   169	    ``MATERIAL_BY_TYPE['sector_tamper'] = 0`` per spec §3.3.2 V1
   170	    advisory; V2 elevates when sector-concentration becomes a hard
   171	    gate. The lookup is authoritative per Bundle B Codex R1 M#2 —
   172	    DO NOT hand-set inline.
   173	    """
   174	    import json as _json
   175	
   176	    from swing.data.datetime_helpers import now_ms
   177	    from swing.data.repos.reconciliation import (
   178	        insert_discrepancy,
   179	        insert_run,
   180	        update_run_completed,
   181	    )
   182	    from swing.trades.reconciliation import MATERIAL_BY_TYPE
   183	
   184	    expected_value_json = _json.dumps(
   185	        {
   186	            "sector": cached_sector,
   187	            "industry": cached_industry,
   188	            "session": cand_session_iso,
   189	        },
   190	        separators=(",", ":"),
   191	    )
   192	    actual_value_json = _json.dumps(
   193	        {"sector": form_sector, "industry": form_industry},
   194	        separators=(",", ":"),
   195	    )
   196	    started_ts = now_ms()
   197	    conn = connect(cfg.paths.db_path)
   198	    try:
   199	        with conn:
   200	            run_id = insert_run(
   201	                conn,
   202	                source="system_audit",
   203	                started_ts=started_ts,
   204	                state="running",
   205	                period_start=run_session_iso,
   206	                period_end=run_session_iso,
   207	            )
   208	            disc_id = insert_discrepancy(
   209	                conn,
   210	                run_id=run_id,
   211	                discrepancy_type="sector_tamper",
   212	                field_name=field_name,
   213	                material_to_review=MATERIAL_BY_TYPE["sector_tamper"],
   214	                created_at=started_ts,
   215	                ticker=ticker,
   216	                expected_value_json=expected_value_json,
   217	                actual_value_json=actual_value_json,
   218	            )
   219	            update_run_completed(
   220	                conn,
   221	                run_id=run_id,
   222	                finished_ts=now_ms(),
   223	                discrepancies_count=1,
   224	                unresolved_discrepancies_count=1,
   225	            )
   226	    finally:
   227	        conn.close()
   228	    return disc_id
   229

   231	def _rerender_entry_form_with_error(
   232	    *, request: Request, templates, cfg, cache, executor,
   233	    ticker: str, entry_date: str, entry_price: float, shares: int,
   234	    initial_stop: float, rationale: str, notes: str | None,
   235	    error_message: str, origin: str = "watchlist",
   236	    # Phase 13 T3.SB1 Codex R1 Major #3 fix — preserve the submitted
   237	    # auto-fill anchors across validation error re-renders. Without
   238	    # these, ``build_entry_form_vm`` below fires a FRESH Schwab Trader
   239	    # API call on every validation retry — bleeding the lookback
   240	    # window + drifting the anchor away from the operator's original
   241	    # submission + potentially overwriting a tampered anchor with a
   242	    # genuine one on retry. Defaults None preserve backward compat for
   243	    # callers without auto-fill semantics.
   244	    submitted_schwab_source_value_json: str | None = None,
   245	    submitted_auto_fill_audit_at: str | None = None,
   246	    submitted_fill_origin_at_form_render: str | None = None,
   247	) -> HTMLResponse:
   248	    """T4: re-render trade_entry_form with preserved values + banner at 400.
   249	
   250	    Mirrors the duplicate-error re-render path but called from rationale
   251	    validation failures before record_entry is invoked.
   252	
   253	    Task 8 (R4-Major-1): ``origin`` threads through so the re-rendered
   254	    form's colspan + Cancel target match the originating surface
   255	    (hyp-recs vs watchlist). Defaults to 'watchlist' for backward
   256	    compat with any caller that omits the kwarg.
   257	    """
   258	    from dataclasses import replace as dc_replace
   259	    vm = build_entry_form_vm(
   260	        ticker=ticker.upper(), cfg=cfg, cache=cache, executor=executor,
   261	        origin=origin,
   262	    )
   263	    if vm is not None:
   264	        vm = dc_replace(
   265	            vm,
   266	            entry_date=entry_date,
   267	            entry_price=entry_price,
   268	            initial_stop=initial_stop,
   269	            input_shares=shares,
   270	            rationale=rationale,
   271	            notes=notes or "",
   272	        )
   273	        # Phase 13 T3.SB1 Codex R1 Major #3 fix — overwrite the freshly-
   274	        # rebuilt auto-fill anchors with the SUBMITTED values, so the
   275	        # operator's force=true / retry submit replays the same anchor
   276	        # the original validation-failed POST carried. This prevents the
   277	        # build_entry_form_vm-driven fresh Schwab fetch from substituting
   278	        # a different anchor mid-flight.
   279	        if submitted_schwab_source_value_json is not None:
   280	            # Codex R2 Minor #1 fix — when restoring a submitted populated
   281	            # anchor on retry, also restore ``auto_fill_kind='populated'``
   282	            # AND clear ``auto_fill_advisory_text``. Otherwise the freshly-
   283	            # rebuilt VM's stale kind/advisory (from the new Schwab fetch
   284	            # that may have returned 'empty' / 'degraded') leaks into the
   285	            # rendered banner, showing "no match" while the hidden anchor
   286	            # still claims auto-fill — confusing the operator.
   287	            submitted_claim = (
   288	                submitted_fill_origin_at_form_render or "operator_typed"
   289	            )
   290	            preserved_kind = (
   291	                "populated"
   292	                if (
   293	                    submitted_schwab_source_value_json
   294	                    and submitted_claim in (
   295	                        "schwab_auto",
   296	                        "schwab_auto_then_operator_corrected",
   297	                    )
   298	                )
   299	                else vm.auto_fill_kind
   300	            )
   301	            preserved_advisory = (
   302	                None
   303	                if preserved_kind == "populated"
   304	                else vm.auto_fill_advisory_text
   305	            )
   306	            vm = dc_replace(
   307	                vm,
   308	                auto_fill_schwab_source_value_json=(
   309	                    submitted_schwab_source_value_json or None
   310	                ),
   311	                auto_fill_audit_at=(
   312	                    submitted_auto_fill_audit_at or None
   313	                ),
   314	                auto_fill_fill_origin=submitted_claim,
   315	                auto_fill_kind=preserved_kind,
   316	                auto_fill_advisory_text=preserved_advisory,
   317	            )
   318	        return templates.TemplateResponse(
   319	            request, "partials/trade_entry_form.html.j2",
   320	            {"vm": vm, "error_message": error_message},
   321	            status_code=400,
   322	        )
   323	    return templates.TemplateResponse(
   324	        request, "partials/trade_form_error.html.j2",
   325	        {"error_message": error_message},
   326	        status_code=400,
   327	    )

   330	@router.get("/trades/entry/sizing-hint", response_class=HTMLResponse)
   331	def sizing_hint(
   332	    request: Request,
   333	    entry_price: str | None = None,
   334	    initial_stop: str | None = None,
   335	) -> HTMLResponse:
   336	    """Tolerant sizing-hint endpoint (spec §4.6). Always 200.
   337	
   338	    Mode contract:
   339	      - Missing / blank / non-numeric / non-positive / stop >= entry
   340	        → 'dim' guidance fragment ("Enter a valid entry price and stop...").
   341	      - Valid inputs + SizingResult(feasible=True) → numbers fragment.
   342	      - SizingResult(feasible=False) → dim fragment with the specific reason.
   343	      - Any unexpected exception → caught, logged WARNING, dim fallback fragment.
   344	    """
   345	    templates = request.app.state.templates
   346	    cfg = apply_overrides(request.app.state.cfg)
   347	    entry = _parse_optional_float(entry_price)
   348	    stop = _parse_optional_float(initial_stop)
   349	
   350	    if entry is None or stop is None or entry <= 0 or stop <= 0 or stop >= entry:
   351	        return templates.TemplateResponse(
   352	            request, "partials/sizing_hint.html.j2",
   353	            {"guidance": "Enter a valid entry price and stop (stop < entry) to see sizing"},
   354	        )
   355	
   356	    try:
   357	        # C.10: routed through the view-model adapter so equity computation
   358	        # consumes non-entry fills via the shared _ExitShape pattern.
   359	        from swing.web.view_models.trades import (
   360	            _list_all_exitshape_via_fills,
   361	        )
   362	
   363	        conn = connect(cfg.paths.db_path)
   364	        try:
   365	            with conn:
   366	                exits = _list_all_exitshape_via_fills(conn)
   367	                cash_movements = list_cash(conn)
   368	        finally:
   369	            conn.close()
   370	        equity = current_equity(
   371	            starting_equity=cfg.account.starting_equity,
   372	            exits=exits, cash_movements=cash_movements,
   373	        )
   374	        sizing: SizingResult = compute_shares(
   375	            entry=entry, stop=stop, equity=equity,
   376	            max_risk_pct=cfg.risk.max_risk_pct,
   377	            position_pct_cap=cfg.sizing.position_pct_cap,
   378	        )
   379	    except Exception as exc:
   380	        log.warning("sizing-hint unexpected exception: %s", exc)
   381	        return templates.TemplateResponse(
   382	            request, "partials/sizing_hint.html.j2",
   383	            {"guidance": "Sizing unavailable — check values"},
   384	        )
   385	
   386	    if not sizing.feasible:
   387	        if sizing.constraint == "no_equity":
   388	            reason = "No equity recorded — add a cash_movement or set account.starting_equity"
   389	        else:
   390	            reason = "Risk cap too tight for 1 share at this stop"
   391	        return templates.TemplateResponse(
   392	            request, "partials/sizing_hint.html.j2",
   393	            {"guidance": reason},
   394	        )
   395	
   396	    return templates.TemplateResponse(
   397	        request, "partials/sizing_hint.html.j2",
   398	        {"sizing": sizing},
   399	    )
   400

   402	@router.get("/trades/entry/form", response_class=HTMLResponse)
   403	def entry_form(
   404	    request: Request,
   405	    ticker: str,
   406	    origin: str = "watchlist",
   407	    # Phase 13 T2.SB6c T-A.6c.4 Codex R1 MAJOR #2 closure — explicit
   408	    # hyp-rec-emitted ``?pattern_evaluation_id=<id>`` query param so the
   409	    # form-render binds to the operator-chosen PE row (multi-pattern-
   410	    # class disambiguation). Falls back to highest-composite when the
   411	    # param is absent OR the explicit id fails validation against the
   412	    # form's (pipeline_run_id, ticker) context (defense-in-depth: a
   413	    # malformed / cross-ticker / cross-run id is silently dropped to
   414	    # the fallback, NOT 500'd).
   415	    pattern_evaluation_id: int | None = Query(None),
   416	    # Phase 13 T2.SB6c Codex R2 MAJOR #1 closure — explicit hyp-rec-
   417	    # emitted ``?pipeline_run_id_at_form_render=<id>`` query param so
   418	    # the form-render binds to the pipeline_run the operator SAW on the
   419	    # expanded card. Without this anchor, a fresh pipeline run completing
   420	    # between expanded-card render and form GET would silently rebind to
   421	    # the new run's highest-composite PE (reintroducing operator-intent
   422	    # drift through a new race path). When the explicit run id is present
   423	    # and matches the PE row's pipeline_run_id, the form pins to that
   424	    # operator-witnessed run. Validation failure (run mismatch, PE
   425	    # missing, ticker mismatch) falls back to the legacy
   426	    # latest_completed_pipeline_run() highest-composite path. When only
   427	    # an explicit PE id arrives WITHOUT this run anchor, behavior is
   428	    # unchanged (validation against latest_completed_pipeline_run); this
   429	    # preserves backwards-compat for any external integration that links
   430	    # without the run anchor.
   431	    pipeline_run_id_at_form_render: int | None = Query(None),
   432	):
   433	    cfg = apply_overrides(request.app.state.cfg)
   434	    cache = request.app.state.price_cache
   435	    executor = request.app.state.price_fetch_executor
   436	    templates = request.app.state.templates
   437	    vm = build_entry_form_vm(
   438	        ticker=ticker, cfg=cfg, cache=cache, executor=executor,
   439	        origin=origin,
   440	        explicit_pattern_evaluation_id=pattern_evaluation_id,
   441	        explicit_pipeline_run_id_at_form_render=(
   442	            pipeline_run_id_at_form_render
   443	        ),
   444	    )
   445	    return templates.TemplateResponse(
   446	        request, "partials/trade_entry_form.html.j2", {"vm": vm},
   447	    )

   450	@router.post("/trades/entry", response_class=HTMLResponse)
   451	def entry_post(
   452	    request: Request,
   453	    ticker: str = Form(...),
   454	    entry_date: str = Form(...),
   455	    entry_price: float = Form(...),
   456	    shares: int = Form(...),
   457	    initial_stop: float = Form(...),
   458	    rationale: str = Form(...),
   459	    notes: str | None = Form(None),
   460	    watchlist_target: float | None = Form(None),
   461	    watchlist_stop: float | None = Form(None),
   462	    force: str | None = Form(None),
   463	    # Phase 5 spec §3.6 — chart-pattern snapshot from hidden form
   464	    # fields populated by build_entry_form_vm at form-render time;
   465	    # operator override + free-text companion field. Each is Optional
   466	    # so existing form submitters (CLI tests; bare cURL) keep working.
   467	    chart_pattern_algo: str | None = Form(None),
   468	    chart_pattern_algo_confidence: float | None = Form(None),
   469	    chart_pattern_classification_pipeline_run_id: int | None = Form(None),
   470	    chart_pattern_operator: str | None = Form(None),
   471	    chart_pattern_operator_other: str | None = Form(None),
   472	    # Task 6 — sector/industry snapshot from hidden form fields populated
   473	    # by build_entry_form_vm at form-render time (snapshot-at-entry-surface
   474	    # ToCToU pattern). Default to "" so existing form submitters (CLI tests;
   475	    # bare cURL) keep working.
   476	    sector: str = Form(""),
   477	    industry: str = Form(""),
   478	    # Phase 9 Bundle D — sector/industry tamper-hardening anchor (Codex
   479	    # R2 Major #1 fix). Carries the form-render's evaluation_run_id so
   480	    # POST validation reaches the same authoritative candidate row the
   481	    # operator saw. None when the form-render found no cached candidate
   482	    # OR when the form posts no anchor (bare cURL / CLI tests) — both
   483	    # cases route to the backward-compat skip path. Mirrors
   484	    # chart_pattern's pipeline_run_id hidden anchor.
   485	    sector_industry_evaluation_run_id: int | None = Form(None),
   486	    # Phase 4.5 — hypothesis_label snapshot from hidden form field
   487	    # populated by build_entry_form_vm at form-render time (snapshot-
   488	    # at-entry-surface ToCToU pattern). Default "" so existing form
   489	    # submitters (CLI tests; bare cURL) keep working. Empty-string is
   490	    # coerced to None at the EntryRequest construction site below;
   491	    # record_entry's canonicalize_hypothesis_label persists NULL.
   492	    hypothesis_label: str = Form(""),
   493	    # Task 8 (R4-Major-1) — origin discriminator survives POST round-trips.
   494	    # The hidden form field emitted by trade_entry_form.html.j2 carries the
   495	    # value resolved at form-render time. Default 'watchlist' preserves
   496	    # behavior for existing callers (CLI tests / bare cURL) that don't post
   497	    # the field. Whitelist-coerced via _coerce_origin to defend against
   498	    # tampered POSTs (XSS / open-redirect into the rendered Cancel target).
   499	    origin: str = Form("watchlist"),
   500	    # Tuition-vs-error (Task 3 / spec §5 + §7.3). The operator's explicit
   501	    # design-intent <select>. Default "" (unselected / bare cURL) is coerced
   502	    # to None at the EntryRequest construction below via `... or None`
   503	    # (the nullability gotcha — empty string would trip the CHECK enum). This
   504	    # is a server-stamp: the value flows straight to record_entry/Trade and
   505	    # is NEVER re-derived from the label.
   506	    entry_intent: str = Form(""),
   507	    # Phase 7 Sub-C C.3 — 18 pre-trade required fields (spec §1, §3.5.1).
   508	    # All `Form(None)` so legacy callers (existing tests, bare cURL) keep
   509	    # working until C.4 wires the operator-facing fieldset; the
   510	    # MissingPreTradeFieldsException catch path below re-renders a
   511	    # banner-only error fragment when any required field is missing.
   512	    # Nullable+CHECK columns persist via `... or None` (per CLAUDE.md
   513	    # gotcha 2026-05-04 — empty string would fail the CHECK enum).

   447	class CallerHeldEntryTransactionError(RuntimeError):
   448	    """``record_entry`` was called with an open transaction on the latched
   449	    path.  Single-transaction services own ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` / COMMIT /
   450	    ROLLBACK and REJECT a caller-held transaction (CLAUDE.md)."""
   451	
   452	
   453	@contextlib.contextmanager
   454	def _entry_transaction(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, immediate: bool):
   455	    """The ONE transaction the entry row is written in.
   456	
   457	    ``immediate=False`` is the pre-arc path, byte-for-byte: Python's sqlite3
   458	    implicit DEFERRED transaction via ``with conn:``.
   459	
   460	    ``immediate=True`` is the latched path.  ``with conn:`` acquires NO write
   461	    reservation until its first write, so a resolution performed "inside" it
   462	    still reads without reserving and another connection can commit between
   463	    that read and the INSERT.  The explicit ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` takes the
   464	    reservation FIRST, following Demand C's shape verbatim including its
   465	    caller-held-transaction refusal.
   466	    """
   467	    if not immediate:
   468	        with conn:
   469	            yield
   470	        return
   471	    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
   472	    try:
   473	        yield
   474	        # THE COMMIT IS INSIDE THE HANDLER'S REACH (Codex 22A-R4-03).  It sat
   475	        # in an `else:` clause, OUTSIDE `except BaseException:` -- so a commit
   476	        # that raises (SQLITE_BUSY, disk-full, I/O) left the transaction AND
   477	        # its write reservation open on a connection the caller goes on
   478	        # reusing.  A failed COMMIT is exactly the moment a rollback matters
   479	        # most, and it was the one path that did not get one.
   480	        conn.commit()
   481	    except BaseException:
   482	        with contextlib.suppress(sqlite3.Error):
   483	            conn.rollback()
   484	        raise
   485

   487	def _record_entry_inner(
   488	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, req: EntryRequest, *,

   494	) -> EntryResult:
   495	    """Never opens or closes a transaction; the caller owns it.
   496	
   497	    Every read below therefore sees the world the write lands in, which is the
   498	    entire point of the reservation.
   499	    """
   500	    from swing.trades.latched_origin import (
   501	        LatchedProvenance,
   502	        resolve_latched_provenance,

   504	    from swing.trades.origin import _latest_complete_evaluation_run_id
   505

   508	    if reserve:
   509	        # THE ORIGIN IS RE-DERIVED INSIDE THE RESERVATION (Codex 22A-R4-01).
   510	        # The preliminary value at the call site above is computed BEFORE
   511	        # `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so a pipeline run can commit between the two --
   512	        # and that value fed BOTH the persisted ordinary origin AND the PE-
   513	        # anchor guard below, whose comment claimed it read "the world the
   514	        # write lands in".  It did not.  A comment asserting an invariant the

   517	        #
   518	        # THE PRELIMINARY VALUE IS STILL LOAD-BEARING and is NOT removed: the

   520	        # would move LOCK clause (c)'s ordering.  The validator requires
   521	        # `trade_origin` for PRESENCE and never keys a rule on its VALUE

   523	        # so the two reads can differ without changing any pre-existing branch.
   524	        #
   525	        # ONLY the reserved path re-derives.  The unreserved path is the
   526	        # pre-arc path byte-for-byte and takes no reservation to be inside of.

   529	    # THE AUTHORITATIVE RESOLUTION, inside the reservation.  The preliminary
   530	    # answer computed outside it is DISCARDED -- it exists only to decide
   531	    # whether to reserve.
   532	    # THE UNRESERVED BRANCH ASKS THE SAME QUESTION, IN THE SAME WORDS (RD's
   533	    # 22A-R3-13 ruling). An absent envelope names no order, so it takes NO
   534	    # reservation -- LOCK clause (d) -- and therefore never reaches the
   535	    # resolver at all. The inconsistency check is a PURE, query-free predicate
   536	    # for exactly that reason, and it is IMPORTED rather than re-spelled here:
   537	    # two callers answering one question two ways is the class this arc has

   556	        latched = LatchedProvenance(

   558	            decline_reason="origin_envelope_inconsistent")
   559	    else:
   560	        latched = LatchedProvenance(

   581	    #
   582	    # AND IT FIRES ON THE ORDINARY PATH ONLY (RD, ruled 2026-08-25).  The
   583	    # condition was `not latched.admitted`, and `recognised_but_underivable`

   613	        # candidate but a NULL label is incoherent AND permanently
   614	        # uncorrectable: Demand C's `_gate_on_unset_state` refuses a trade
   615	        # carrying any of the three.
   616	        log.info(
   617	            "22-A: fill for %s admitted from latched mandate %s (link %s, "
   618	            "order %s, validity intent %s); writing trade_origin=%s "

   651	        derived_origin = "manual_off_pipeline"
   652	        resolved_candidate_id = None
   653	        hypothesis_label = None
   654	
   655	    if latched.admitted or latched.recognised_but_underivable:
   656	        pass                      # the ordinary chain is not consulted
   657	    elif resolved_candidate_id is None and derived_origin != "manual_off_pipeline":
   658	        _eval_run_for_candidate: int | None = None
   659	        if req.pattern_evaluation_id is not None:
   660	            _chain_row = conn.execute(
   661	                "SELECT pr.evaluation_run_id FROM pattern_evaluations pe "
   662	                "JOIN pipeline_runs pr ON pr.id = pe.pipeline_run_id "
   663	                "WHERE pe.id = ?",
   664	                (int(req.pattern_evaluation_id),),
   665	            ).fetchone()
   666	            if _chain_row is not None and _chain_row[0] is not None:
   667	                _eval_run_for_candidate = int(_chain_row[0])
   668	        if _eval_run_for_candidate is None:
   669	            _eval_run_for_candidate = _latest_complete_evaluation_run_id(conn)
   670	        if _eval_run_for_candidate is not None:
   671	            _cand_row = conn.execute(
   672	                "SELECT id FROM candidates "
   673	                "WHERE evaluation_run_id = ? AND ticker = ? "
   674	                "ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1",
   675	                (_eval_run_for_candidate, req.ticker),
   676	            ).fetchone()
   677	            if _cand_row is not None:
   678	                resolved_candidate_id = int(_cand_row[0])
   679	
   680	    trade = Trade(
   681	        id=None, ticker=req.ticker, entry_date=req.entry_date,
   682	        entry_price=req.entry_price, initial_shares=req.shares,
   683	        initial_stop=req.initial_stop, current_stop=req.initial_stop,
   684	        # Phase 7: state lifecycle replaces the legacy `status` column.
   685	        # New entries land in 'entered'; the state-mutation service
   686	        # transitions to 'managing' once the first non-entry fill arrives.
   687	        state="entered",
   688	        watchlist_entry_target=req.watchlist_entry_target,
   689	        watchlist_initial_stop=req.watchlist_initial_stop,
   690	        notes=req.notes,
   691	        hypothesis_label=canonicalize_hypothesis_label(hypothesis_label),
   692	        # Snapshot AS-IS — no re-resolve here (spec §3.6 ToCToU fix).
   693	        # The operator override re-uses canonicalize_hypothesis_label
   694	        # because spec §3.6 specifies identical NFC + control-byte rules
   695	        # for both free-text labels.
   696	        chart_pattern_algo=req.chart_pattern_algo,
   697	        chart_pattern_algo_confidence=req.chart_pattern_algo_confidence,
   698	        chart_pattern_operator=canonicalize_hypothesis_label(req.chart_pattern_operator),
   699	        chart_pattern_classification_pipeline_run_id=req.chart_pattern_classification_pipeline_run_id,
   700	        sector=req.sector,
   701	        industry=req.industry,
   702	        # Phase 7 lifecycle fields (NOT NULL in schema). `trade_origin`
   703	        # comes from derive_trade_origin (B.2); `pre_trade_locked_at`
   704	        # comes from entry_date-derived ISO datetime (Codex R4 M1 fix —
   705	        # was req.event_ts which is the command time, not the actual entry
   706	        # chronology — back-recorded entries broke aggregation).
   707	        trade_origin=derived_origin,
   708	        pre_trade_locked_at=entry_iso,
   709	        # Phase 7 pre-trade decision fields — passed through from the request.
   710	        thesis=req.thesis,
   711	        why_now=req.why_now,
   712	        invalidation_condition=req.invalidation_condition,
   713	        expected_scenario=req.expected_scenario,
   714	        premortem_technical=req.premortem_technical,
   715	        premortem_market_sector=req.premortem_market_sector,
   716	        premortem_execution=req.premortem_execution,
   717	        premortem_additional=req.premortem_additional,
   718	        event_risk_present=req.event_risk_present,
   719	        event_handling=req.event_handling,
   720	        event_type=req.event_type,
   721	        event_date=req.event_date,
   722	        gap_risk_present=req.gap_risk_present,
   723	        gap_risk_handling=req.gap_risk_handling,
   724	        emotional_state_pre_trade=req.emotional_state_pre_trade,
   725	        market_regime=req.market_regime,
   726	        catalyst=req.catalyst,
   727	        catalyst_other_description=req.catalyst_other_description,
   728	        # Phase 13 T2.SB6c T-A.6c.4 OQ-11 + OQ-12 lifecycle backlinks.
   729	        # candidate_id: resolved above via the latest-complete-evaluation-
   730	        # run lookup (Path 1 per plan §B.1); NULL for manual_off_pipeline.
   731	        # pattern_evaluation_id: server-re-derived value from the route
   732	        # handler's 5-tier rejection ladder (T3.SB3 R1 M#2 LOCK).
   733	        candidate_id=resolved_candidate_id,
   734	        pattern_evaluation_id=req.pattern_evaluation_id,
   735	        # Tuition-vs-error: persisted AS-IS from the operator's explicit
   736	        # choice (server-stamp); NEVER suggested from the label here (spec §5).

   738	    )
   739	
   740	    archived = False
   741	    try:
   742	        trade_id = insert_trade_with_event(
   743	            conn, trade, event_ts=req.event_ts, rationale=req.rationale,
   744	        )
   745	        # Phase 9 T-A.7 — stamp risk_policy_id_at_lock from the active
   746	        # policy in the SAME transaction. Spec §3.1.1: preserves
   747	        # at-trade-time semantics for capital_floor / scratch_epsilon /
   748	        # trail-MA periods even when the policy is later superseded.
   749	        # When no active policy exists (operator manually flipped seed

   751	        # NULL; spec §9.4 backwards-compatibility contract says NULL is
   752	        # legal and read paths fall back to current active policy.
   753	        conn.execute(
   754	            "UPDATE trades SET risk_policy_id_at_lock = "
   755	            "(SELECT policy_id FROM risk_policy WHERE is_active = 1) "
   756	            "WHERE id = ?",
   757	            (trade_id,),
   758	        )
   759	        # Phase 7 Sub-B B.3 — atomic first entry-fill insert in the
   760	        # SAME transaction as the trade row. The fill's

   771	                # chronology consistency (matches B.4 exit-side fix).

   776	                manual_entry_confidence=req.manual_entry_confidence,
   777	                # Phase 13 T3.SB1 T-B.1.4 — auto-fill provenance audit
   778	                # columns. Per spec §6.4 + plan §G.2 T-B.1.4. Defaults
   779	                # on the dataclass preserve backward-compat: when
   780	                # EntryRequest is built without these fields (CLI tests
   781	                # / bare cURL), Fill defaults to operator_typed + None.
   782	                fill_origin=req.fill_origin,
   783	                schwab_source_value_json=req.schwab_source_value_json,
   784	                operator_corrected_value_json=(
   785	                    req.operator_corrected_value_json
   786	                ),
   787	                auto_fill_audit_at=req.auto_fill_audit_at,
   788	            ),
   789	            event_ts=req.event_ts,
   790	            rationale=req.rationale,
   791	            # Hotfix 2026-05-05 (operator-witnessed gate finding S3):
   792	            # insert_trade_with_event above already emitted an 'entry'
   793	            # trade_event row; suppress the duplicate emission here.
   794	            emit_event=False,
   795	        )
   796	        wl = get_watchlist_entry(conn, req.ticker)
   797	        if wl is not None:
   798	            archive_watchlist_entry(conn, WatchlistArchiveEntry(
   799	                id=None, ticker=req.ticker, added_date=wl.added_date,
   800	                removed_date=req.entry_date, reason="entered",
   801	                qualification_count=wl.qualification_count,
   802	                last_data_asof_date=wl.last_data_asof_date,
   803	                notes=wl.notes,
   804	            ))
   805	            archived = True
   806	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
   807	        # Schema-level safety net (ux_trades_one_open_per_ticker, migration 0004):
   808	        # two concurrent record_entry calls raced past the app-layer list_open_trades
   809	        # check; the partial unique index rejected the second INSERT. Map to the same
   810	        # DuplicateOpenPositionError callers already handle.
   811	        if "UNIQUE" in str(exc) and "trades" in str(exc):
   812	            raise DuplicateOpenPositionError(
   813	                f"Already an open position in {req.ticker} (race-detected)"
   814	            ) from exc
   815	        raise
   816	
   817	    return EntryResult(trade_id=trade_id, warning=warning, watchlist_archived=archived)

   593	def broker_order_id_from_envelope(raw: str | None) -> str | None:
   594	    """The broker order id inside a fill's Schwab envelope, or ``None``.
   595	
   596	    NEVER RAISES.  This is a read-only consumer of an operator-submitted blob,
   597	    so the posture is graceful-degrade + log: malformed JSON, a non-dict, a
   598	    missing key, a non-string value and an empty string all return ``None``.
   599	    A WARNING fires only when the JSON is PRESENT but unusable -- an absent
   600	    envelope is the ordinary non-Schwab case and is not noteworthy.
   601	    """
   602	    if raw is None:
   603	        return None
   604	    if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.strip():
   605	        log.warning(
   606	            "22-A: fill envelope is present but not a JSON string (%r); "
   607	            "treating the order id as absent", type(raw).__name__,
   608	        )
   609	        return None
   610	    try:
   611	        payload = json.loads(raw)
   612	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 -- the TYPE ROSTER is the failure (SS-2)
   613	        # ENUMERATING THE RAISABLE TYPES IS THE HAND-MAINTAINED-ROSTER FAILURE
   614	        # -- 22A-R8-03's own ruling, applied to the readers that fix left
   615	        # behind.  This was `except (ValueError, TypeError)`, and `json.loads`
   616	        # raises `RecursionError`, a `RuntimeError`, on a deeply nested
   617	        # document (MEASURED on this interpreter).  These readers run BEFORE
   618	        # the resolver's containment, and one of them runs before
   619	        # `record_entry` opens a transaction at all, so an escape here rolled
   620	        # a money-bearing entry back over an unreadable audit blob.
   621	        #
   622	        # "Treat it as absent" is safe HERE only because
   623	        # `envelope_is_canonical` answers the SAME document FAIL-CLOSED, so
   624	        # the pair still RECOGNISES it and the row lands honest-unset instead
   625	        # of taking the ordinary chain.
   626	        log.warning(
   627	            "22-A: fill envelope could not be decoded; treating the order id "
   628	            "as absent (the fill still records, cohort bookkeeping degrades)"
   629	        )
   630	        return None
   631	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
   632	        log.warning(
   633	            "22-A: fill envelope decoded to %s, not an object; treating the "
   634	            "order id as absent", type(payload).__name__,
   635	        )
   636	        return None
   637	    value = payload.get(SCHWAB_ORDER_ID_ENVELOPE_KEY)
   638	    if value is None:
   639	        return None
   640	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
   641	        log.warning(
   642	            "22-A: fill envelope carries a non-string or empty %s; treating "
   643	            "the order id as absent", SCHWAB_ORDER_ID_ENVELOPE_KEY,
   644	        )
   645	        return None
   646	    return value.strip()
