   665	
   666	def envelope_is_canonical(raw: str | None) -> bool:
   667	    """Do PYTHON and SQL read the SAME value for EVERY key both domains read?
   668	
   669	    ONE AUTHORITY, APPLIED TO AN IDENTITY (Codex 22A-R8-01; it is AL-7's shape
   670	    one datum over).  The service STRIPS whitespace and ``json.loads`` keeps
   671	    the LAST duplicate key; SQLite's ``json_extract`` strips nothing and keeps
   672	    the FIRST -- both MEASURED.  So a padded or duplicated envelope gives the
   673	    service one value while every SQL scan over the same blob reads another.
   674	
   675	    The answer is NOT to canonicalise harder in one domain -- that is the
   676	    two-spellings-agree-today class.  It is to REFUSE an envelope the two
   677	    domains would read differently, so the value is either unambiguous or the
   678	    admission does not happen.  ``False`` becomes a recognised-but-underivable
   679	    refusal, never a fall-through.
   680	
   681	    THREE THINGS THE SELF-SWEEP CHANGED, each verified by execution:
   682	
   683	    * **THE ROSTER, NOT THE ORDER ID ALONE (SS-4).**  R8-01 stated the class
   684	      and fixed ONE instance.  The citation trigger ALSO binds
   685	      ``$.schwab_instrument_symbol`` by ``json_extract`` while the service
   686	      reads that key through ``instrument_symbol_from_envelope``, which
   687	      strips -- measured: the service admitted ``latch_ladder`` and the trigger
   688	      then ABORTED the correction with the generic citation-graph message, an
   689	      authorize-then-abort delivering an illegible refusal.
   690	    * **A NON-STRING VALUE IS A DISAGREEMENT, NOT AN ABSENCE (SS-1).**  The
   691	      earlier "the reader already returns None" line treated it as harmless.
   692	      It is not: ``json_extract`` yields a non-NULL scalar, and comparing that
   693	      to a TEXT column applies TEXT affinity -- MEASURED, an unquoted
   694	      ``1002937461`` MATCHES a link whose ``broker_order_id`` is the string
   695	      ``1002937461``.  Python reads absence; SQL reads a real mandate.
   696	    * **A BLANK OR PADDED VALUE LIKEWISE.**  Python strips it to nothing while
   697	      SQL returns the string.  Direction is a wrong REFUSAL on a shape that
   698	      names no order, which is the cheap one.
   699	
   700	    NEVER RAISES ON A DECODE FAILURE, and the breadth is deliberate: the
   701	    earlier ``except (ValueError, TypeError)`` was the hand-maintained-roster
   702	    failure 22A-R8-03 ruled against, applied to exception TYPES, and
   703	    ``json.loads`` raises ``RecursionError`` (a ``RuntimeError``, caught by
   704	    neither) on a deeply nested document -- MEASURED on this interpreter.
   705	
   706	    AND EVERY DECODE FAILURE ANSWERS ``False`` (Codex 22A-R11-01).  A document
   707	    the authority cannot decode is an UNANSWERED question, not an agreement;
   708	    see the handler below for what the split cost and why the mirror-shape
   709	    ground for the old ``True`` died with the mirror.
   710	
   711	    AND AN UNREADABLE **TYPE** IS A DECODE FAILURE TOO (Codex 22A-R13-01).
   712	    This began ``if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.strip(): return True``
   713	    -- one predicate answering TWO different questions, and the "nothing to
   714	    disagree about" ground is true of the first and false of the second.
   715	    SQLite does not enforce column affinity and no migration carries a
   716	    ``typeof(schwab_source_value_json) = 'text'`` CHECK, so a BLOB bound into
   717	    that TEXT column returns as ``bytes``; the readers answered ``None`` for
   718	    it, this guard answered ``True``, and ``canonical_envelope_identity``
   719	    PERSISTED ``('canonical', NULL, NULL)`` -- the authority recording "I read
   720	    this and it names no order" for a document it never opened.  Downstream,
   721	    the ``last_word`` branch admits on exactly that stored absence.  It is
   722	    R11-01's class on the WRONG-TYPE branch, which R11-01's merge of the two
   723	    decode branches left answering ``canonical``.
   724	    """
   725	    if raw is None or (isinstance(raw, str) and not raw.strip()):
   726	        return True                    # no envelope: nothing to disagree about
   727	    if not isinstance(raw, str):
   728	        log.warning(
   729	            "22-A: the fill envelope is a %s rather than a string, so the "
   730	            "authority cannot read it; the reading is REFUSED rather than "
   731	            "recorded as an absence of any order", type(raw).__name__)
   732	        return False
   733	    # THE COUNT IS THE ROOT OBJECT'S, NOT THE DOCUMENT'S (Codex 22A-R9-06).
   734	    # `object_pairs_hook` fires for EVERY nested object, so a first version
   735	    # counted a legitimate top-level id plus an unrelated nested field of the
   736	    # same name as a duplicate -- a wrong REFUSAL manufactured by the guard.
   737	    # Both readers address `$.<key>` at the ROOT, so the root is the only
   738	    # place the two can disagree. The hook records EVERY object's pairs and
   739	    # the LAST one it returns is the root, because the decoder builds
   740	    # inside-out.
   741	    objects: list[list[tuple]] = []
   742	
   743	    def _hook(pairs):
   744	        objects.append(list(pairs))
   745	        return dict(pairs)
   746	
   747	    try:
   748	        payload = json.loads(raw, object_pairs_hook=_hook)
   749	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 -- fail-CLOSED on an UNANSWERED question
   750	        # THE TWO DECODE BRANCHES ARE ONE (Codex 22A-R11-01).  This was split:
   751	        # a `ValueError`/`TypeError` returned True on the ground that "a
   752	        # document NEITHER DOMAIN can read agrees with itself -- both read
   753	        # absence", while a `RecursionError` returned False.  The first ground
   754	        # was TRUE OF THE MIRROR SHAPE and died with it.  Under PERSIST-
   755	        # CANONICAL there is no second domain to agree with: SQL never opens
   756	        # the document, so the question is no longer "do the two engines read
   757	        # it alike" but "can the AUTHORITY say what this document names", and
   758	        # for a document it cannot decode it cannot.
   759	        #
   760	        # WHAT THE SPLIT COST, MEASURED: `canonical_envelope_identity('{bad')`
   761	        # stored `state='canonical'` with both ids NULL -- indistinguishable
   762	        # from a decodable document that genuinely names nothing.  Rung 6's
   763	        # consumption scan matches on an order id such a row does not carry,
   764	        # and its unreadable-scan matches on `refused`, which it was not, so an
   765	        # UNREADABLE prior consumer was invisible to both and read as evidence
   766	        # of ABSENCE at the one rung that exists to stop a second consumer of
   767	        # one mandate.  Ignorance fails CLOSED here as it does everywhere else
   768	        # on this ladder.
   769	        #
   770	        # A DECODABLE document that names no order is UNAFFECTED and must be:
   771	        # `[1, 2, 3]` and `{}` are still canonical, because the authority READ
   772	        # them and they name nothing, which is a statement rather than a
   773	        # silence.  That distinction is what keeps the last_word ladder open
   774	        # for every pre-22-A fill.
   775	        log.exception(
   776	            "22-A: the fill envelope could not be DECODED, so the authority "
   777	            "cannot say what it names; the reading is REFUSED and the entry "
   778	            "records with honest-unset cohort keys rather than with the "
   779	            "latest run's candidate")
   780	        return False
   781	    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or not objects:
   782	        return True
   783	    root = objects[-1]
   784	    for key in ENVELOPE_KEYS_READ_BY_BOTH_DOMAINS:
   785	        seen = [k for k, _v in root if k == key]
   786	        if len(seen) > 1:
   787	            log.warning(
   788	                "22-A: fill envelope carries %d %s keys; Python keeps the LAST "
   789	                "and SQLite keeps the FIRST, so the two domains would read "
   790	                "DIFFERENT values", len(seen), key)
   791	            return False
   792	        if key not in payload:
   793	            continue                   # absent in BOTH domains
   794	        value = payload[key]
   795	        if value is None:
   796	            continue                   # JSON null: json_extract reads NULL too
   797	        if not isinstance(value, str):
   798	            log.warning(
   799	                "22-A: fill envelope's %s is a %s rather than a string (%r); "
   800	                "the service treats it as ABSENT while json_extract returns "
   801	                "it, and TEXT affinity can still match a stored identity",
   802	                key, type(value).__name__, value)
   803	            return False
   804	        if value != value.strip() or not value.strip():
   805	            log.warning(
   806	                "22-A: fill envelope's %s is whitespace-padded or blank (%r); "
   807	                "the service strips it and SQL does not, so the two domains "
   808	                "would read DIFFERENT values", key, value)
   809	            return False
   810	    return True
   811

   813	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   814	class EnvelopeIdentity:
   815	    """The authority's ONE reading of one envelope document."""
   816	
   817	    state: str                        # ENVELOPE_CANONICAL | ENVELOPE_REFUSED
   818	    broker_order_id: str | None
   819	    instrument_symbol: str | None
   820	
   821	
   822	def canonical_envelope_identity(raw: str | None) -> EnvelopeIdentity:
   823	    """THE ONE DERIVATION.  Everything downstream compares its STORED OUTPUT.
   824	
   825	    PERSIST-CANONICAL (CHARC + RD, 2026-08-26).  Ten review rounds never
   826	    converged because migration 0037 was made to RE-DERIVE this function's
   827	    judgment in SQL, and the two engines disagree in at least three independent
   828	    ways -- ``json.loads`` accepts ``NaN`` where ``json_valid`` rejects the
   829	    document; ``str.strip`` removes tab/newline/NBSP where ``trim()`` removes
   830	    ASCII space only; ``1002937461 == '1002937461'`` is False in Python and
   831	    True in SQL against a TEXT-affinity column.  Three rounds, three
   832	    divergences, each found only after the previous was fixed, and nothing said
   833	    three was the last.  So the mirror is gone: this function decides, its
   834	    answer is PERSISTED against the exact document it read
   835	    (``fill_envelope_identity.envelope_raw``), and SQL compares stored values.
   836	
   837	    IT IS COMPOSED OF THE THREE EXISTING READERS AND ADDS NO FOURTH SPELLING.
   838	    ``envelope_is_canonical`` still asks whether the document can be read to a
   839	    single unambiguous value; the two readers still say what it says.  What
   840	    changed is that nothing asks the question TWICE.
   841	
   842	    NEVER RAISES: every constituent contains its own decode failure, and
   843	    ``envelope_is_canonical`` answers a document it cannot decode with
   844	    ``False`` -- fail CLOSED, because an unanswerable question is not a pass.
   845	    """
   846	    if not envelope_is_canonical(raw):
   847	        return EnvelopeIdentity(ENVELOPE_REFUSED, None, None)
   848	    return EnvelopeIdentity(
   849	        ENVELOPE_CANONICAL,
   850	        broker_order_id_from_envelope(raw),
   851	        instrument_symbol_from_envelope(raw),
   852	    )

   855	def origin_and_envelope_are_inconsistent(fill_origin, raw) -> bool:
   856	    """A TRUSTED origin whose envelope names NOTHING (RD, ruled on 22A-R3-13).
   857	
   858	    THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE INCONSISTENT EVIDENCE PAIR, NEVER THE ORIGIN.
   859	    A `schwab_auto` fill carries an envelope BY CONSTRUCTION -- established by
   860	    READING both writers, not by grepping:
   861	
   862	      * `swing/trades/entry_auto_fill.py` -- the `kind='populated'` branch of
   863	        `EntryAutoFillResult.__post_init__` REQUIRES
   864	        `fill_origin='schwab_auto'`, and the one `populated` return builds
   865	        `schwab_source_value_json` in the same expression that sets it.
   866	      * `swing/web/routes/trades.py` -- a trusted `resolved_fill_origin` is
   867	        stamped ONLY inside the block that also assigns
   868	        `resolved_schwab_source_value_json`, and that block is entered only
   869	        when the submitted envelope parsed to a dict.
   870	
   871	    So the pair is a state no production writer produces: the envelope was
   872	    STRIPPED, TAMPERED WITH or CORRUPTED.  Writing TODAY's candidate for such a
   873	    fill would be attribution from a TIMING COINCIDENCE -- gotcha #30's family,
   874	    and the exact misattribution this arc exists to prevent.
   875	
   876	    WHY NOT THE ORIGIN ALONE, which is the tempting rule: an envelope-BEARING
   877	    Schwab fill that simply never had a latch is the ORDINARY post-integration
   878	    state, and suppressing it would erase correct pipeline provenance across
   879	    the whole journal.  Both directions are pinned by cases, because the two
   880	    implementations agree on everything except the twin.
   881	
   882	    PURE, and query-free by construction: LOCK clause (d) says a request with
   883	    no usable order id costs ZERO additional database queries, and this
   884	    predicate is the reason the answer can be reached without reserving.
   885	    """
   886	    if fill_origin not in TRUSTED_LATCH_FILL_ORIGINS:
   887	        return False
   888	    return not (isinstance(raw, str) and raw.strip())

   891	def envelope_recognises_an_order(raw: str | None) -> bool:
   892	    """THE ONE RECOGNITION TRIGGER, shared by every caller (self-sweep SS-1).
   893	
   894	    "Does this request carry a usable broker order id?" was asked at THREE
   895	    sites -- ``record_entry``'s reservation, the entry route's EXT-2 deferral,
   896	    and the resolver -- and all three asked it of the PYTHON reader ALONE.  So
   897	    an envelope Python reads as ABSENT and SQL reads as a REAL LINKED order
   898	    took no reservation, never reached the canonicality guard 22A-R8-01 added
   899	    for exactly that disagreement, and ran the ordinary current-candidate
   900	    chain.  MEASURED end to end on three shapes: the persisted row was
   901	    ``('pipeline_aplus', <today's candidate>)`` for a fill SQL binds to an
   902	    accepted mandate.
   903	
   904	    That is 22A-R9-01 one step further back.  R9-01 moved the canonicality
   905	    question above the link LOOKUP; it still sat below the order-id READ, and
   906	    the read is where a disagreeing envelope disappears.
   907	
   908	    The question therefore INCLUDES the disagreement: an envelope the two
   909	    domains read differently is RECOGNISED, so it is refused rather than
   910	    silently attributed.  Three spellings became one, which is also what stops
   911	    a fourth caller reintroducing the split.
   912	
   913	    PURE STRING READ, ZERO QUERIES -- LOCK clause (d), "a fill with no usable
   914	    broker order id costs ZERO additional database queries", is preserved by
   915	    construction, and its subject is unchanged: an envelope naming no order
   916	    and reading the same in both domains is still not recognised and still
   917	    takes the deferred ``with conn:`` exactly as before.
   918	    """
   919	    return (broker_order_id_from_envelope(raw) is not None
   920	            or not envelope_is_canonical(raw))

   950	def assert_fill_consistent_with_order(
   951	    order: AcceptedLatchOrder,
   952	    *,
   953	    ticker: str,
   954	    price: float,
   955	    shares: float,
   956	    fill_origin: str,
   957	    envelope_symbol: str | None,
   958	) -> str | None:
   959	    """The FIVE envelope guards.  Returns a decline reason, or ``None``.
   960	
   961	    THESE ARE REFUSAL GUARDS, NOT IDENTITY EVIDENCE, and the plan demotes them
   962	    deliberately (S2.4.1): ``fill_origin`` is computed server-side but FROM the
   963	    same hidden inputs, so no rung here is independent evidence.  The residual
   964	    is declared at L10 with its threat model.
   965	
   966	    CONNECTION-FREE BY DESIGN.  A pure function over the order and the
   967	    submitted envelope is what makes every envelope guard testable without a
   968	    database and keeps all five in one place.  That is why
   969	    ``actual_limit_price`` was added to ``AcceptedLatchOrder`` rather than the
   970	    signature growing a connection.

  1112	def find_accepted_latch_order(
  1113	    conn, *, broker_order_id: str,
  1114	) -> list[AcceptedLatchOrder]:
  1115	    """Every link naming this broker order, oldest first.  NO rungs run here.
  1116	
  1117	    ``actual_limit_price`` comes from the validity JOIN this lookup already
  1118	    performs, so the envelope guards stay a PURE function over the dataclass
  1119	    (plan S5.1) rather than growing a connection argument.
  1120	
  1121	    **THE FIVE FIELDS RUNG 3c BINDS ARE CARRIED AS STORED, NOT COERCED (Codex
  1122	    22A-FIX-R7-01; orchestrator-ruled IN SCOPE 2026-09-01).**  ``int()`` and
  1123	    ``str()`` are LOSSY on exactly the values rung 3c exists to catch: SQLite
  1124	    applies no affinity to a REAL written into an ``INTEGER`` column, so a raw
  1125	    link carrying ``evaluation_run_id = 121.5`` or ``actual_quantity = 2.5``
  1126	    is schema-legal under those columns' own ``> 0`` CHECKs -- and ``int()``
  1127	    collapsed them to ``121`` / ``2``, which then MATCHED the authoritative
  1128	    ``121`` / ``2`` in rung 3c's Python comparison.  The citation trigger
  1129	    compares the STORED values and refuses, so the service ADMITTED and SQL
  1130	    aborted: the authorize-then-abort shape, on the very rung whose job is to
  1131	    bind the link's duplicated fields back to their sources.
  1132	
  1133	    Carrying them as stored makes the two domains answer alike -- a drifted
  1134	    value now FAILS rung 3c with ``link_field_unbound``, which is the refusal
  1135	    the trigger already gives.  The IDENTITY fields (``link_id``, the two
  1136	    intent ids, ``candidate_id``) keep their coercion: they are not rung-3c
  1137	    bindings, they are keys this module indexes and logs by, and widening the
  1138	    change to them would be a different edit than the one this finding names.
  1139	    """
  1140	    rows = conn.execute(
  1141	        "SELECT l.link_id, l.validity_intent_id, l.place_intent_id, "
  1142	        "       l.candidate_id, l.evaluation_run_id, l.ticker, "
  1143	        "       l.detection_date, l.broker_order_id, l.frozen_pivot, "

  1145	        "       v.actual_limit_price "
  1146	        "  FROM latch_order_mandate_links l "
  1147	        "  JOIN latch_order_intents v ON v.intent_id = l.validity_intent_id "
  1148	        " WHERE l.broker_order_id = ? "
  1149	        " ORDER BY l.link_id",
  1150	        (broker_order_id,),
  1151	    ).fetchall()
  1152	    return [
  1153	        AcceptedLatchOrder(
  1154	            link_id=int(r[0]), validity_intent_id=int(r[1]),
  1155	            place_intent_id=int(r[2]), candidate_id=int(r[3]),
  1156	            # AS STORED -- see the docstring.  These five are rung 3c's
  1157	            # bindings, and a coercion here answers a different question from
  1158	            # the one the citation trigger asks of the same columns.

  1162	            actual_quantity=r[10],

  1298	def _authorization_block(inputs: dict) -> dict:
  1299	    """``{key: {"input": ..., "verdict": "pass"}}`` over the WHOLE roster."""
  1300	    missing = sorted(set(AUTHORIZATION_KEYS) - set(inputs))
  1301	    extra = sorted(set(inputs) - set(AUTHORIZATION_KEYS))
  1302	    if missing or extra:
  1303	        raise KeyError(
  1304	            f"authorization block does not match AUTHORIZATION_CLAUSES: "
  1305	            f"missing {missing}, extra {extra}")

  1307	            for key in AUTHORIZATION_KEYS}

  1943	    """``(reason_or_None, consulted)`` -- the ordering verdict AND its INPUT.

  1950	    ticker.

  1955	    THE SCAN COVERS EVERY LATCH ON THE TICKER, NOT ONLY THE SELECTED ONE
  1956	    (Codex R1, and the scope is what makes the guard reachable at all). The
  1957	    fold consumes decisions WITHOUT any `recorded_ts` bound, so an intent that
  1958	    post-dates the fill can CHANGE THE TOPOLOGY -- a post-fill decline on fire A
  1959	    closes A, and a later same-pivot fire B that would have folded in as A's
  1960	    re-confirmation instead opens its OWN latch. Scanning only the selected
  1961	    latch's family then never sees the offending decline, because the decline
  1962	    lives on the latch it created. Scanning every same-ticker latch does.
  1963

  1967	    decisions by `recorded_ts` -- a FOURTH EXT-1 parameter, and EXT-1 is
  1968	    approved as exactly THREE. **The ground is the governing asymmetry: a wrong
  1969	    REFUSAL costs a legible message, and a wrong ACCEPTANCE contaminates H1.**
  1970	    A detected-not-derived as-of world is an HONEST LIMITATION, not a defect --
  1971	    and the fourth parameter is not this arc's to take. If 22-A2's proof
  1972	    machinery needs the derivation itself, that is 22-A2's envelope question.
  1973	    Recorded in the accepted-limitations list so a review measuring against a
  1974	    contract that omits it does not re-find it every round.
  1975	
  1976	    THE WINDOW IS THE LADDER'S OWN, IMPORTED. `decision_bounds_for` +

    52	--

    61	-- ITSELF BE RECORDED: it is performed ONLY inside a NEW numbered migration,
    62	-- which is the record. That is the procedural half.
    63	--
    64	-- THE MECHANICAL HALF, which is what makes single-state coherent: the
    65	-- admission reader verifies BOTH barrier triggers exist AT READ TIME -- and
    66	-- compares their BODIES against a verbatim pinned copy, not their names --
    67	-- and refuses barrier_not_installed if either is absent or altered. So a drop

   171	-- ============================================================================
   172	CREATE TRIGGER trg_candidates_no_update BEFORE UPDATE ON candidates
   173	BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, '22-A barrier trg_candidates_no_update: candidates rows are IMMUTABLE from migration 0037. A re-evaluation APPENDS a new row; it never edits an existing one. To change a fire''s recorded values you must add an evaluation run. To retire the barrier see the reversibility header of 0037_latch_order_mandate_links.sql.'); END;
   174	
   175	CREATE TRIGGER trg_candidates_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON candidates
   176	BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, '22-A barrier trg_candidates_no_delete: candidates rows are PERMANENT from migration 0037. The latch identity space and every provenance citation address rows by a REUSABLE rowid, so a delete would silently repoint them. Pruning is a migration-level operation -- see the reversibility header of 0037_latch_order_mandate_links.sql.'); END;
   177	
   178	-- THE UPDATE+DELETE PAIR IS FAIL-OPEN TO REPLACE, ON THIS ARC'S LOAD-BEARING
   179	-- TABLE, AND IT IS WORSE HERE THAN ON THE EPOCH (CHARC's generalisation of the
   180	-- epoch finding, 2026-08-24). MEASURED at production settings
   181	-- (recursive_triggers default OFF, foreign_keys ON) against the real candidates
   182	-- shape, which carries TWO conflict targets -- id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and
   183	-- UNIQUE(evaluation_run_id, ticker):
   184	--
   185	--   INSERT OR REPLACE on the UNIQUE  -> SUCCEEDS: id moved 12284 -> 12285,
   186	--                                       pivot/stop rewritten,
   187	--                                       candidate_criteria CASCADE-wiped 1 -> 0
   188	--   bare REPLACE on the rowid PK     -> SUCCEEDS: id preserved, pivot/stop
   189	--                                       rewritten, candidate_criteria wiped
   190	--
   191	-- That is exactly the id-reuse catastrophe the DELETE half exists to prevent,
   192	-- reached with BOTH barrier triggers present, canonical and UNFIRED -- so the
   193	-- admission reader's body-comparison integrity check cannot see it. The
   194	-- triggers are not altered; they are BYPASSED.
   195	--
   196	-- ONE THING INCIDENTALLY PROTECTS THE WRONG HALF and must not be mistaken for a
   197	-- defence: with a citing link row present, candidate_id REFERENCES
   198	-- candidates(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT blocks both REPLACE paths. So the FK covers
   199	-- the POST-acceptance population and leaves the PRE-acceptance population fully
   200	-- exposed -- and pre-acceptance is precisely the window that matters, because
   201	-- the link copies frozen_pivot / frozen_invalidation AT MINT TIME. A REPLACE
   202	-- before acceptance rewrites the very values that are then frozen and stamped
   203	-- live_at_acceptance.
   204	--
   205	-- THE FIX CANNOT BE THE EPOCH'S. candidates must accept ordinary INSERTs every
   206	-- night, so a blanket BEFORE INSERT barrier is unavailable. What is available
   207	-- is a CONFLICT-SCOPED one: refuse an INSERT that would COLLIDE with an
   208	-- existing row, so REPLACE can never reach its delete half. BEFORE INSERT
   209	-- triggers fire BEFORE conflict resolution deletes anything -- the property the
   210	-- fix rests on, measured rather than assumed.
   211	--
   212	-- TWO BEHAVIOUR CHANGES, DECLARED rather than discovered at the live pipeline
   213	-- gate: (a) INSERT OR IGNORE on a duplicate candidate now ABORTS where it
   214	-- previously no-op'd, and (b) a plain duplicate INSERT now aborts with THIS
   215	-- message rather than SQLite's UNIQUE message -- same outcome, different text,
   216	-- and this text is the more useful of the two. Neither is reachable from
   217	-- production today: a case-insensitive grep for "insert or replace|replace
   218	-- into" across swing/ (*.py, *.sql) returns ZERO executable statements (every
   219	-- hit is a comment FORBIDDING the idiom) and insert_candidates uses a plain
   220	-- INSERT. That is SERVICE-prevention at an incidence of zero, which is exactly
   221	-- the posture the barrier exists to replace.
   222	--
   223	-- THE PK CONFLICT CLAUSE READS `NEW.<pk> != -1`, AND THE `IS NOT NULL` FORM IT
   224	-- REPLACES NEVER FIRED (Codex 22A-R8-02; CHARC-ruled 2026-08-26). In a BEFORE
   225	-- INSERT trigger an OMITTED `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` -- and an explicit NULL --
   226	-- both present as `-1`, reproduced independently on sqlite 3.50.4. So
   227	-- `NEW.<pk> IS NULL` is ALWAYS false: the old clause was dead text that
   228	-- happened to work, and the moment a row at id `-1` exists it ABORTS every
   229	-- ordinary id-omitting append. All four no-REPLACE barriers in this migration
   230	-- use the `!= -1` form, and each ships the three-direction discriminating set
   231	-- the ruling names -- an ordinary append SUCCEEDS, a conflicting REPLACE
   232	-- ABORTS, an explicit conflicting id ABORTS.
   233	--
   234	-- THE RESIDUAL ON AN EXISTING TABLE, DECLARED: `candidates`,
   235	-- `latch_order_intents` and `provenance_corrections` cannot carry a
   236	-- `CHECK (pk > 0)` without a table rebuild, so on those three an EXPLICIT `-1`
   237	-- INSERT is indistinguishable from an omitted one and would re-open exactly
   238	-- the hazard above. INCIDENCE ZERO, established by READING each production
   239	-- writer's column list rather than by grepping for the column name -- all
   240	-- three omit the PK entirely, and a test reads those three lists so the
   241	-- declaration cannot rot into prose. `latch_order_mandate_links` is NEW and
   242	-- carries the CHECK instead.
   243	CREATE TRIGGER trg_candidates_no_replace BEFORE INSERT ON candidates
   244	WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM candidates
   245	              WHERE (evaluation_run_id = NEW.evaluation_run_id AND ticker = NEW.ticker)
   246	                 OR (NEW.id != -1 AND id = NEW.id))
   247	BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, '22-A barrier trg_candidates_no_replace: candidates rows are PERMANENT from migration 0037. A conflicting INSERT (INSERT OR REPLACE / REPLACE / INSERT OR IGNORE) would DELETE the existing row, bypassing trg_candidates_no_delete, reusing its id and cascade-wiping candidate_criteria. A re-evaluation APPENDS a new row under a new evaluation_run_id. To retire the barrier see the reversibility header of 0037_latch_order_mandate_links.sql.'); END;
   248	
   249	-- ============================================================================
   250	-- 3. THE LINK: one row per BROKER-ACCEPTED latch order.
   251	--
   252	-- WHY A NEW TABLE AT ALL. The acceptance row in latch_order_intents genuinely
   253	-- IS a durable order<->mandate link -- append-only, trigger-protected, carrying
   254	-- actual_broker_order_id and candidate_id on one row. What it does NOT carry is
   255	-- the fire's INVALIDATION, and it can never be made to: trg_loi_no_update and
   256	-- trg_loi_no_delete ABORT every UPDATE and DELETE (0033), so a new column on
   257	-- that table could never be back-filled for an existing acceptance. An
   258	-- implementation built on it alone must read candidates.initial_stop live at
   259	-- comparison time with nothing to check it against -- precisely the shape RD's
   260	-- frozen-value gate refuses.

   455	-- ============================================================================
   456	-- 3d. THE STORED CANONICAL READING OF A FILL'S ENVELOPE -- PERSIST-CANONICAL.
   457	--
   458	-- THE RULING THIS TABLE EXISTS TO ENCODE (CHARC 2026-08-26, adopting RD's
   459	-- sentence verbatim):
   460	--
   461	--     SQL VERIFIES A FACT; IT MUST NEVER RE-DERIVE A JUDGMENT ACROSS AN ENGINE
   462	--     BOUNDARY -- the twin mirrors the AUTHORITY by consuming its OUTPUT, not
   463	--     by reimplementing its reasoning.
   464	--
   465	-- WHAT IT REPLACES, AND WHY THE REPLACEMENT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN ANOTHER
   466	-- FIX. Ten review rounds ran without converging, and three CONSECUTIVE rounds
   467	-- each produced a DISTINCT engine-semantic divergence -- every one real, every
   468	-- one found only after the previous had been fixed:
   469	--
   470	--   NaN inside a document   python json.loads ACCEPTS  |  sqlite json_valid REJECTS
   471	--   trim/strip ASCII space  both strip                 |  AGREE
   472	--   trim/strip tab/NL/NBSP  python strips              |  sqlite does NOT
   473	--   1002937461 == '..'      python False               |  SQL (TEXT affinity) True
   474	--
   475	-- Zero findings were ever reopened, so this was not careless execution: it is a
   476	-- structural property of mirroring a nontrivial predicate across two engines
   477	-- that disagree in at least three independent ways, and nothing said three was
   478	-- the last. So the mirror is REMOVED. The SERVICE canonicalises a fill's
   479	-- envelope ONCE, PERSISTS its reading here, and every SQL site downstream
   480	-- compares a STORED VALUE instead of parsing the document again.
   481	--
   482	-- envelope_raw IS THE BINDING, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS IS A FACT CHECK.
   483	-- The row records WHICH DOCUMENT was judged, verbatim. Every consumer joins on
   484	-- `fei.envelope_raw = fills.schwab_source_value_json` -- a plain TEXT equality,
   485	-- no parsing, no normalisation, no coercion -- so a reading whose document
   486	-- later changed simply stops matching and the surface fails CLOSED. That is
   487	-- what lets a trigger consume a judgment it is forbidden to make.
   488	--
   489	-- TWO STATES, NOT THREE. 'canonical' means the authority read the document and
   490	-- these are its values (either may be NULL: a well-formed envelope naming no
   491	-- order is canonical and names nothing). 'refused' means the authority could
   492	-- NOT read it to a single unambiguous value. A fill whose envelope is NULL has
   493	-- NO ROW AT ALL and needs none -- `schwab_source_value_json IS NULL` is itself
   494	-- a fact, and it is how every pre-22-A fill passes.
   495	--
   496	-- NO BACKFILL, DELIBERATELY, and this is the load-bearing consequence of the
   497	-- ruling. A SQL backfill would have to decide, in SQL, what each existing
   498	-- envelope says -- which is the re-derivation this table exists to delete,
   499	-- merely moved from verification time to migration time. So the migration
   500	-- creates the table EMPTY and the SERVICE fills it: existing fills are
   501	-- canonicalised on demand by the one authority, inside the same write
   502	-- reservation that consumes the result. CONDITION 4 is satisfied exactly as
   503	-- section 3's own backfill satisfies it -- nothing rebuilt, nothing dropped,
   504	-- NO EXISTING ROW TOUCHED.
   505	--
   506	-- WHAT THIS TABLE CANNOT DO, declared here rather than discovered later: a raw
   507	-- writer that stores an identity row AND a citation that AGREE WITH EACH OTHER
   508	-- but disagree with the envelope passes every check below. That is the SAME
   509	-- trust boundary as before -- the trigger never could judge truth, only
   510	-- CONSISTENCY -- and stating it is the condition on which the reshape was
   511	-- ruled. See section 6's limitations block for the full statement.
   512	--
   513	-- identity_id is a plain INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (a rowid alias): nothing cites an
   514	-- identity row by id, so the AUTOINCREMENT reuse hazard the link table pays
   515	-- for does not apply here. UNIQUE(fill_id, envelope_raw) is the key every
   516	-- consumer addresses, and it is what makes the lookup single-valued.
   517	-- ============================================================================
   518	CREATE TABLE fill_envelope_identity (
   519	    -- CHECK (identity_id > 0) IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE SENTINEL CONTRACT, and
   520	    -- it was MISSING here while the link table carried it (Codex 22A-R11-06).
   521	    -- REPRODUCED on sqlite 3.50.4 at the default recursive_triggers=0: insert
   522	    -- a row explicitly at -1, then INSERT OR REPLACE a -1 row with a DIFFERENT
   523	    -- (fill_id, envelope_raw); the first row was SILENTLY DELETED and
   524	    -- replaced, trg_fei_no_delete never fired, and this table's append-only
   525	    -- guarantee -- the whole reason a stored reading can be trusted -- was
   526	    -- false. The barrier below must ignore NEW.identity_id = -1 because an
   527	    -- OMITTED integer primary key presents as -1 rather than NULL, so the
   528	    -- sentinel has to be impossible as a STORED value. A NEW table can
   529	    -- guarantee that with a CHECK; the three EXISTING tables cannot without a
   530	    -- rebuild this convention forbids, which is why they DECLARE the residual
   531	    -- and every NEW table closes it by construction. A test walks both new
   532	    -- tables rather than the one that happened to be remembered.
   533	    identity_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (identity_id > 0),
   534

   536	    -- `split_into_partials` DELETEs the consolidated fill and rebuilds it as

   538	    -- PRESERVES the envelope onto the rebuilt rows -- so an envelope-bearing
   539	    -- fill genuinely does get deleted on a supported operational path. All
   540	    -- THREE delete actions block it, verified by execution on sqlite 3.50.4 at
   541	    -- the default PRAGMA recursive_triggers=0: RESTRICT and NO ACTION raise
   542	    -- `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, and CASCADE DOES fire this table's own

   547	    --
   548	    -- THE ORPHAN IT PERMITS IS HARMLESS BY CONSTRUCTION, and the reason is the
   549	    -- same reason envelope_raw exists. fills.fill_id is a plain rowid alias and
   550	    -- IS reused; a stale reading whose fill was deleted can therefore be
   551	    -- addressed again. But every consumer joins on BOTH fill_id AND

   554	    -- for which the stale reading is the correct reading. The only way the two

   556	    -- exactly that rather than preferring either answer.

   567	    -- THE VERSION IS RECORDED AND NO TRIGGER READS IT -- STATED ONCE, HERE,

   569	    --
   570	    -- THE CLASS, not the clause.  Round 12's new rung-6 population clause

   576	    --
   577	    -- WHAT IS EXPOSED, precisely.  The SERVICE re-runs the current
   578	    -- canonicaliser over the whole population before it scans

   580	    -- stored answer disagrees with today's.  SQL cannot re-run anything.  So
   581	    -- after a canonicaliser bump whose ANSWER changes for some document, a RAW

   584	    -- path.  It is declared at plan limitation L19 with its reason.
   585	    --
   586	    -- WHY NOT SIMPLY REQUIRE THE CURRENT VERSION IN EVERY CONSUMER -- the

   591	    --     Filtering those on the version makes a stale reading INVISIBLE to

   595	    --  2. AT THE OTHER FOUR IT MANUFACTURES A REFUSAL ON THE SERVICE PATH.

   605	    --
   606	    -- SO THE EXPOSURE IS CLOSED AT ITS ONLY ARMING ACTION INSTEAD.  A reading

   609	    -- which is L10/AL-10's declared class.  The anchor below therefore mirrors

   612	    -- representations -- the drift-test discipline: a bump FAILS THE SUITE
   613	    -- with the required work named, before any stale row can exist.  A comment
   614	    -- promising future work is unenforceable (gotcha #31); a failing test is
   615	    -- not.
   616	    --

   619	    -- `canonical_envelope_identity` ANSWERS -- a non-`str` document now reads
   620	    -- `refused` where it read `canonical` -- which is exactly the trigger the

   622	    -- a bump normally owes is RE-ATTESTATION of readings taken under the older

   657	-- THE CONFLICT-SCOPED INSERT BARRIER, for the reason measured three times in
   658	-- this same file: at the default PRAGMA recursive_triggers=OFF an
   659	-- INSERT OR REPLACE DELETES the conflicting row WITHOUT firing the DELETE
   660	-- trigger. Both unique keys are scoped -- the rowid PK and UNIQUE(fill_id,
   661	-- envelope_raw) -- because guarding one leaves the other live, which is the
   662	-- same half-swept shape as the bypass itself. The `!= -1` spelling is the
   663	-- CHARC-ruled sentinel contract: an OMITTED INTEGER PRIMARY KEY presents as
   664	-- -1 in a BEFORE INSERT trigger, not NULL (reproduced on sqlite 3.50.4).
   665	-- The ignore is only SAFE because the table's CHECK (identity_id > 0) makes a
   666	-- stored -1 impossible; without it the sentinel collides with a real row and
   667	-- the barrier can be walked straight past (Codex 22A-R11-06, measured).
   668	-- FEI-CONSUMER barrier_no_replace_conflict_scope :: NOT_A_READING
   669	-- It addresses the UNIQUE KEY, never a stored reading, so a version filter
   670	-- here would LET A SECOND ROW FOR THE SAME DOCUMENT THROUGH under a different
   671	-- version -- the append-only guarantee defeated by the guard meant to widen
   672	-- it.  This is the one occurrence in the file that must stay version-blind
   673	-- even after 22-A2's re-attestation lands.
   674	CREATE TRIGGER trg_fei_no_replace BEFORE INSERT ON fill_envelope_identity
   675	WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fill_envelope_identity
   676	              WHERE (NEW.identity_id != -1 AND identity_id = NEW.identity_id)
   677	                 OR (fill_id = NEW.fill_id
   678	                     AND envelope_raw = NEW.envelope_raw))
   679	BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, '22-A barrier trg_fei_no_replace: fill_envelope_identity is append-only. A conflicting INSERT (INSERT OR REPLACE / REPLACE / INSERT OR IGNORE) would DELETE the existing reading, bypassing trg_fei_no_delete at the default PRAGMA recursive_triggers=OFF, and substitute a different identity for the same document -- which is exactly the forgery the stored reading exists to make impossible. To retire the barrier see the reversibility header of 0037_latch_order_mandate_links.sql.'); END;
   680	
   681	
   682	-- ============================================================================
   683	-- 4. THE MINTING TRIGGER, and the BACKFILL.
   684	--
   685	-- A TRIGGER, NOT A SERVICE HOOK. A hook in record_intent or in the route is
   686	-- skippable and invisible to a raw INSERT -- the D36 shape. A trigger cannot be
   687	-- bypassed by any writer.
   688	--
   689	-- IT MUST BE INCAPABLE OF RAISING. Each copied value is guarded AT THE SOURCE
   690	-- by a CASE, so a junk fire lands NULL frozen values rather than aborting the
   691	-- operator's acceptance record.
   692	--
   693	-- THE TIER IS DERIVED, NEVER HARD-CODED (review 22A-R7-03). The specification
   694	-- for this trigger once read freeze_tier='live_at_acceptance' unconditionally,
   695	-- which would have given a POST-migration acceptance of a PRE-migration fire a
   696	-- false structural-proof label -- the exact defect the epoch exists to prevent,
   697	-- written into the epoch's own migration. It was the TWELFTH mirror site of the
   698	-- freeze-tier family and an eleven-site sweep could not have found it, because
   699	-- that sweep looked for the enum's VALUE SET and this line hard-coded ONE
   700	-- MEMBER of it. A value-set sweep does not find a hard-coded single member.
   701	-- The CASE below and the one in the backfill are the SQL twin of
   702	-- freeze_tier_for_candidate; a test runs both spellings over the same fixtures.
   703	-- ============================================================================
   704	CREATE TRIGGER trg_latch_link_mint_on_acceptance
   705	AFTER INSERT ON latch_order_intents
   706	FOR EACH ROW WHEN NEW.intent_kind = 'validity'
   707	             AND NEW.validity_outcome = 'accepted_by_broker'
   708	             AND NEW.actual_broker_order_id IS NOT NULL
   709	BEGIN
   710	    INSERT INTO latch_order_mandate_links (
   711	        validity_intent_id, place_intent_id, candidate_id, evaluation_run_id,
   712	        ticker, detection_date, broker_order_id,
   713	        frozen_pivot, frozen_invalidation, actual_quantity,
   714	        freeze_tier, linked_at)
   715	    SELECT NEW.intent_id,
   716	           NEW.validated_place_intent_id,
   717	           NEW.candidate_id,
   718	           NEW.evaluation_run_id,
   719	           NEW.ticker,
   720	           NEW.detection_date,
   721	           NEW.actual_broker_order_id,
   722	           CASE WHEN typeof(c.pivot) = 'real' AND c.pivot > 0
   723	                THEN c.pivot ELSE NULL END,
   724	           CASE WHEN typeof(c.initial_stop) = 'real' AND c.initial_stop > 0
   725	                THEN c.initial_stop ELSE NULL END,
   726	           NEW.actual_quantity,
   727	           CASE WHEN c.id > (SELECT max_candidate_id_at_barrier
   728	                               FROM candidates_immutability_epoch
   729	                              WHERE epoch_id = 1)
   730	                THEN 'live_at_acceptance' ELSE 'pre_barrier_reconstructed' END,
   731	           strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')
   732	      FROM candidates c
   733	     WHERE c.id = NEW.candidate_id;
   734	END;
   735	
   736	-- THE BACKFILL is a GENERAL statement over the ledger, never a hand-written
   737	-- row, and it derives the tier through the SAME CASE rather than stating a
   738	-- constant -- the second single-member site the corrected sweep found. Its
   739	-- expected result on the live database today is exactly ONE row at
   740	-- pre_barrier_reconstructed, and the test asserts that as an OUTCOME of the
   741	-- derivation rather than as an input to it: the epoch was seeded from
   742	-- MAX(candidates.id) moments ago, so every candidate that exists is at-or-below
   743	-- the boundary and no backfilled link can be post-barrier.
   744	INSERT INTO latch_order_mandate_links (
   745	    validity_intent_id, place_intent_id, candidate_id, evaluation_run_id,
   746	    ticker, detection_date, broker_order_id,
   747	    frozen_pivot, frozen_invalidation, actual_quantity,
   748	    freeze_tier, linked_at)
   749	SELECT v.intent_id,
   750	       v.validated_place_intent_id,
   751	       v.candidate_id,
   752	       v.evaluation_run_id,
   753	       v.ticker,
   754	       v.detection_date,
   755	       v.actual_broker_order_id,
   756	       CASE WHEN typeof(c.pivot) = 'real' AND c.pivot > 0
   757	            THEN c.pivot ELSE NULL END,
   758	       CASE WHEN typeof(c.initial_stop) = 'real' AND c.initial_stop > 0
   759	            THEN c.initial_stop ELSE NULL END,
   760	       v.actual_quantity,
   761	       CASE WHEN c.id > (SELECT max_candidate_id_at_barrier
   762	                           FROM candidates_immutability_epoch
   763	                          WHERE epoch_id = 1)
   764	            THEN 'live_at_acceptance' ELSE 'pre_barrier_reconstructed' END,
   765	       strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')
   766	  FROM latch_order_intents v
   767	  JOIN candidates c ON c.id = v.candidate_id
   768	 WHERE v.intent_kind = 'validity'
   769	   AND v.validity_outcome = 'accepted_by_broker'
   770	   AND v.actual_broker_order_id IS NOT NULL
   771	   AND v.validated_place_intent_id IS NOT NULL;
   772	
   773	-- ============================================================================
   774	-- 5. THE CORRECTION SURFACE LEARNS THE LATCH LADDER -- SIX ADD COLUMNs.
   775	--
   776	-- admission_tier takes a CONSTANT default, so NOT NULL DEFAULT is legal and the
   777	-- existing CADL row becomes 'last_word' -- which is true of it. The five
   778	-- citation columns default NULL, as SQLite requires for an added FK column.
   779	--
   780	-- The tier enum is TWO-VALUED in this arc; latch_ladder_tier2 arrives with
   781	-- 22-A2 and the tier-2 evidence class it belongs to. A column-level CHECK IS
   782	-- accepted and ENFORCED by ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN on the installed SQLite
   783	-- (3.50.4) -- verified at the prompt before this was written, per 0036's
   784	-- four-CHECK-semantics-surprises lesson -- so the SQL half of the enum mirror
   785	-- lives here and PROVENANCE_ADMISSION_TIERS mirrors it (#11).
   786	-- ============================================================================
   787	ALTER TABLE provenance_corrections ADD COLUMN admission_tier TEXT NOT NULL
   788	    DEFAULT 'last_word' CHECK (admission_tier IN ('last_word', 'latch_ladder'));
   789	ALTER TABLE provenance_corrections ADD COLUMN cited_latch_link_id INTEGER
   790	    REFERENCES latch_order_mandate_links(link_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT;
   880	-- exposed -- both raws stay bound to the cited link and the cited candidate, so
   881	-- a forger cannot name a different mandate -- and it is the unavoidable price
   882	-- of the rule, because ANY SQL-side recomputation re-creates the cross-domain
   883	-- comparison the rule exists to forbid.
   884	--
   885	-- THE $.authorization ROSTER IS THE MACHINE-READABLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. The
   886	-- json_remove path list below is the closure list; AUTHORIZATION_CLAUSES in
   887	-- swing/trades/latched_origin.py mirrors it, and a test parses the path list
   888	-- out of THIS FILE and asserts exact set equality with that roster -- the
   889	-- 0033 LATCH_BROKER_SNAPSHOT_KEYS precedent, so neither is a hand-maintained
   890	-- copy of the other. SIXTEEN entries: the ELEVEN ladder rungs plus the FIVE
   891	-- envelope guards enumerated SEPARATELY, because one lumped envelope_guards
   892	-- entry cannot distinguish "all five passed" from "one ran and four never did".
   893	-- ============================================================================
   894	DROP TRIGGER trg_provenance_corrections_citation_graph;
   895	
   896	CREATE TRIGGER trg_provenance_corrections_citation_graph
   897	BEFORE INSERT ON provenance_corrections
   898	FOR EACH ROW WHEN NOT (
   899	    -- the cited candidate belongs to the cited run, and is an aplus row
   900	    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM candidates ca
   901	            WHERE ca.id = NEW.cited_candidate_id
   902	              AND ca.evaluation_run_id = NEW.cited_evaluation_run_id
   903	              AND ca.bucket = 'aplus')
   904	    -- the frozen run anchors ARE that run's own columns
   905	    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM evaluation_runs er
   906	                WHERE er.id = NEW.cited_evaluation_run_id
   907	                  AND er.run_ts = NEW.cited_run_ts_raw
   908	                  AND er.action_session_date
   909	                      = NEW.cited_candidate_action_session_date)
   910	    -- the cited recommendation belongs to the same run and the same ticker,
   911	    -- is a today_decision, and carries the frozen anchor
   912	    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM daily_recommendations dr
   913	                WHERE dr.id = NEW.cited_daily_recommendation_id
   914	                  AND dr.evaluation_run_id = NEW.cited_evaluation_run_id
   915	                  AND dr.recommendation = 'today_decision'
   916	                  AND dr.action_session_date
   917	                      = NEW.cited_recommendation_action_session_date
   918	                  AND dr.ticker = (SELECT ca.ticker FROM candidates ca
   919	                                   WHERE ca.id = NEW.cited_candidate_id))
   920	    -- the cited pipeline row OWNS that run, is complete, and supplied the bound
   921	    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pipeline_runs pr
   922	                WHERE pr.id = NEW.cited_pipeline_run_id
   923	                  AND pr.evaluation_run_id = NEW.cited_evaluation_run_id
   924	                  AND pr.state = 'complete'
   925	                  AND pr.finished_ts = NEW.cited_pipeline_finished_ts_raw)
   926	    -- the cited interval belongs to the cited hypothesis and IS what was frozen
   927	    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hypothesis_status_history h
   928	                WHERE h.history_id = NEW.cited_hypothesis_status_history_id
   929	                  AND h.hypothesis_id = NEW.cited_hypothesis_id
   930	                  AND h.status = NEW.cited_hypothesis_status_at_record
   931	                  AND h.effective_from
   932	                      = NEW.cited_hypothesis_status_effective_from
   933	                  AND h.effective_to
   934	                      IS NEW.cited_hypothesis_status_effective_to
   935	                  AND h.recorded_at
   936	                      = NEW.cited_hypothesis_status_recorded_at)
   937	    -- the frozen NAME is that hypothesis's name as spelled right now
   938	    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hypothesis_registry hr
   939	                WHERE hr.id = NEW.cited_hypothesis_id
   940	                  AND hr.name = NEW.cited_hypothesis_name_at_correction)
   941	    -- the anchoring fill is an ENTRY fill of THIS trade on the frozen session
   942	    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM fills f
   943	                WHERE f.fill_id = NEW.entry_fill_id_at_correction
   944	                  AND f.trade_id = NEW.trade_id
   945	                  AND f.action = 'entry'
   946	                  AND substr(f.fill_datetime, 1, 10)
   947	                      = NEW.entry_fill_session_date)
   948	    -- and the trade and the cited candidate are the same instrument
   949	    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM trades t
   950	                WHERE t.id = NEW.trade_id
   951	                  AND t.ticker = (SELECT ca.ticker FROM candidates ca
   952	                                  WHERE ca.id = NEW.cited_candidate_id))
   953	
   954	    -- ===== THE AUTHORIZATION'S FOUR FILL-SIDE OPERANDS: PRESENT, AND BOUND
   955	    -- ===== TO THE CITED FILL (Codex 22A-R15-01).
   956	    --
   957	    -- `R14-02` added quantity / price / fill_origin / envelope to the frozen
   958	    -- entry-fill snapshot because the latch ladder's every rung reads them and
   959	    -- a stored proof whose operands are not frozen is not a proof.  NOTHING
   960	    -- OUTSIDE THE SERVICE then required them: `swing/data/models.py`'s
   961	    -- validator and `0036:390-397`'s CHECK both require only fill_id /
   962	    -- trade_id / action (+ fill_datetime).  So a RAW correction -- the AL-10
   963	    -- trust boundary this whole trigger exists to police -- could carry an
   964	    -- SQL-bound latch probe with the operands OMITTED or FALSIFIED, and every
   965	    -- layer read green.
   966	    --
   967	    -- INSERT-TIME RULE.  The five live pre-operand rows are untouched: they
   968	    -- were written before the freeze existed and no UPDATE or DELETE path
   969	    -- changes here.  The drift reader already reports them by name.
   970	    --
   971	    -- IT VERIFIES A FACT, NEVER A JUDGMENT.  Each freeze is compared to the
   972	    -- fill's OWN column, in SQL's own domain, with the NULL-safe `IS` -- same
   973	    -- value, same domain, no rounding and no cross-engine re-derivation.  It
   974	    -- is the identical shape as the four RAW OPERANDS block further down.
   975	    --
   976	    -- THE PRESENCE ASSERTION IS SEPARATE AND IS LOAD-BEARING.  `json_extract`
   977	    -- on an ABSENT path returns SQL NULL, so `IS <column>` alone reads an
   978	    -- OMITTED operand as agreement whenever the column is itself NULL --
   979	    -- which is every pre-22-A envelope.  `json_type(...) IS NOT NULL`
   980	    -- distinguishes an absent path (NULL) from a JSON `null` VALUE (the text
   981	    -- 'null'), and that is exactly the distinction the omission case turns on.
   982	    --
   983	    -- THE ORDINARY BRANCH BINDS THE **JSON TYPE** AS WELL AS THE VALUE (Codex
   984	    -- 22A-FIX-R2-01, verified by execution twice -- by the reviewer and here).
   985	    -- `IS` applies the SOURCE COLUMN'S AFFINITY, so a bare value comparison is
   986	    -- blind to the freeze's own storage class: MEASURED, JSON text `"2.0"`
   987	    -- compares EQUAL to a REAL `2.0`, and -- the sharper one -- a JSON OBJECT
   988	    -- compares EQUAL to a TEXT column holding the same minified document.
   989	    -- Production freezes an envelope as a JSON STRING and never as that
   990	    -- object, so both shapes are snapshots the freezer could not emit passing
   991	    -- the clause written to require its output.  Each ordinary branch
   992	    -- therefore pairs the value comparison with a `json_type` that must AGREE
   993	    -- with the column's `typeof()`, one storage class at a time.
   994	    --
   995	    -- THE `'object'` BRANCH IS THE FREEZER'S DECLARED DIGEST ESCAPE, AND IT IS
   996	    -- CLOSED AND TYPE-BOUND (Codex 22A-FIX-R1-01).  `_json_safe_operand`
   997	    -- writes a type-tagged object when the value cannot be written as JSON --
   998	    -- a BLOB (SQLite does not enforce column affinity; 22A-R13-01 measured
   999	    -- that shape reaching production) or a non-finite REAL (`json.dumps(inf)`
  1000	    -- emits the bare token `Infinity`, which `json_valid` reads FALSE, so a
  1001	    -- truthful freeze would be rejected by the row's own CHECK).
  1002	    --
  1003	    -- **THE FIRST DRAFT ADMITTED *ANY* OBJECT once the column was a BLOB or an
  1004	    -- infinity, and that was a REACHABLE WRONG ACCEPTANCE at the raw-write
  1005	    -- trust boundary** -- a forger could freeze `{}` beside a BLOB column and
  1006	    -- satisfy the clause the binding exists to enforce.  MEASURED by the
  1007	    -- reviewer against this exact predicate shape.  The escape now requires:
  1008	    --   * the column's `typeof()` to be the one that MAKES the escape legal;
  1009	    --   * the object to be CLOSED to the freezer's own key pair (`json_remove`
  1010	    --     of the two keys is `'{}'`), so no third key can ride along;
  1011	    --   * the `type` tag to be the one the freezer actually writes for that
  1012	    --     `typeof()` -- **`'bytes'` EXACTLY** (Codex 22A-FIX-R2-02, verified by
  1013	    --     execution): `sqlite3` returns a BLOB column as Python `bytes` for
  1014	    --     EVERY binding, including a `bytearray` or a `memoryview` written in,
  1015	    --     so `_json_safe_operand` can only ever tag a CITED FILL `'bytes'`.
  1016	    --     Admitting the other two tags left the declared type-tag consistency
  1017	    --     unverifiable in exactly the way the digest's VALUE already is, which
  1018	    --     is one declared residual too many; and
  1019	    --   * for a non-finite REAL, the `repr` to be the EXACT sign the column
  1020	    --     carries -- `'inf'` or `'-inf'`, which is what Python's `repr` emits
  1021	    --     (measured), so the two infinities cannot be interchanged.
  1022	    --
  1023	    -- **THE RESIDUAL, DECLARED: SQLite HAS NO `sha256`, so the BLOB digest's
  1024	    -- VALUE is not verified -- only its SHAPE (64 lower-case hex characters)
  1025	    -- and its type tag.**  That is AL-10's boundary exactly (the trigger
  1026	    -- verifies CONSISTENCY, never TRUTH) and it is strictly smaller than what
  1027	    -- the any-object branch exposed: a forger must now produce a well-formed
  1028	    -- digest object beside a genuinely BLOB column rather than an empty one.
  1029	    --
  1030	    -- `fill_origin` GETS NO ESCAPE AT ALL, and that is SCHEMA-PREVENTION
  1031	    -- rather than an omission: `fills.fill_origin` carries a five-value
  1032	    -- `CHECK (fill_origin IN (...))` (migration `0020:394`), and MEASURED by
  1033	    -- execution, that CHECK rejects BOTH a BLOB and an infinity -- SQLite
  1034	    -- compares a BLOB to TEXT as unequal, so no enum member matches.  A
  1035	    -- column that cannot hold either value needs no escape from either.
  1036	    --
  1037	    -- FAIL-CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION.  A malformed snapshot cannot reach a JSON
  1038	    -- function (the `json_valid` CASE, 22A-R3-12's class), and any NULL
  1039	    -- anywhere in the chain collapses through `COALESCE(..., 0)` to a REFUSAL
  1040	    -- rather than to a trigger that silently does not fire.
  1041	    AND COALESCE((
  1042	        SELECT CASE WHEN json_valid(NEW.entry_fill_snapshot_json) THEN (
  1043	                json_type(NEW.entry_fill_snapshot_json, '$.quantity')
  1044	                    IS NOT NULL
  1045	            AND json_type(NEW.entry_fill_snapshot_json, '$.price')

  2063	
  2064	         AND CASE WHEN json_type(NEW.cited_latch_probe_json, '$.authorization.guard_envelope_symbol')
  2065	                       = 'object'

  2067	                 '$.authorization.guard_envelope_symbol'), '$.input', '$.verdict') = '{}'

  2071	         AND json_type(NEW.cited_latch_probe_json,
  2072	                 '$.authorization.guard_envelope_symbol.input') = 'text'
  2073	         -- PERSIST-CANONICAL. The `json_extract` on the LEFT stays: the probe
  2074	         -- blob is the AUTHORITY'S OWN OUTPUT, and reading a value the service
  2075	         -- wrote is consuming its output, which is precisely what the ruling
  2076	         -- endorses. The `json_extract` that USED to be on the right read the
  2077	         -- OPERATOR'S document and re-derived the service's symbol reading;
  2078	         -- that one is gone, replaced by the stored reading of the same
  2079	         -- document.
  2080	         AND json_extract(NEW.cited_latch_probe_json,
  2081	                 '$.authorization.guard_envelope_symbol.input')
  2082	             -- FEI-CONSUMER guard_envelope_symbol_binding :: VERSION_BLIND
  2083	             = (SELECT fei.instrument_symbol

  2104	             = (SELECT f.quantity FROM fills f
  2105	                 WHERE f.fill_id = NEW.entry_fill_id_at_correction)
  2106	         -- AND THE GUARD'S VERDICT, NOT ONLY ITS INPUT (Codex 22A-R5-01). A
  2107	         -- fill of 100 could truthfully record input=100 against an accepted
  2108	         -- quantity of 2 and the row inserted: input FIDELITY is not predicate
  2109	         -- TRUTH, and both operands are SQL-reachable, so this is neither AL-3
  2110	         -- nor the rounding limit.
  2111	         --
  2112	         -- THE NULL BRANCH MIRRORS THE SERVICE EXACTLY: `actual_quantity` is
  2113	         -- nullable (0037's own CHECK is `IS NULL OR > 0`) and
  2114	         -- `assert_fill_consistent_with_order` skips the inequality when it is
  2115	         -- NULL. A bare `<=` would evaluate NULL, take the COALESCE to 0 and
  2116	         -- REJECT a row the service admits -- a twin STRONGER than its reader,
  2117	         -- which authorizes a correction that then aborts at the INSERT.
  2118	         --
  2119	         -- The `> 0` half of the service's guard is NOT restated: 0014 CHECKs
  2120	         -- `fills.quantity > 0` and the clause above binds the input to that
  2121	         -- column, so a non-positive input is schema-prevented rather than
  2122	         -- unchecked. Cited rather than defended twice.
  2123	         AND (

  3731	* **L18 -- THE CITATION TRIGGER CAN NO LONGER JUDGE A FILL'S ENVELOPE AT ALL; IT VERIFIES ONLY
  3732	  THAT THE AUTHORITY'S STORED READING AND THE CITATION AGREE. A RAW WRITER STORING TWO
  3733	  EQUAL-BUT-WRONG VALUES PASSES THE EQUALITY CHECK.** *(Declared at the PERSIST-CANONICAL reshape,
  3734	  CHARC + RD 2026-08-26, as a condition of the ruling -- stated NOW rather than discovered later.)*
  3735

  3737	  DISTINCT engine-semantic divergence between Python and SQLite -- `json.loads` ACCEPTS a document
  3738	  containing `NaN` where `json_valid` REJECTS it; `str.strip()` removes tab/newline/NBSP where
  3739	  `trim()` removes ASCII space only; `1002937461 == '1002937461'` is False in Python and True in
  3740	  SQL against a TEXT-affinity column. All three reproduced independently. Zero findings were ever
  3741	  reopened across 74, so this was never careless execution: it is a structural property of
  3742	  mirroring a nontrivial predicate across engines that disagree in at least three independent ways,
  3743	  and nothing said three was the last. **RD's sentence, adopted verbatim by CHARC into the
  3744	  convention: SQL VERIFIES A FACT; IT MUST NEVER RE-DERIVE A JUDGMENT ACROSS AN ENGINE BOUNDARY --
  3745	  the twin mirrors the AUTHORITY by consuming its OUTPUT, not by reimplementing its reasoning.**
  3746	
  3747	  **WHAT WAS LOST, EXACTLY.** The trigger previously re-derived, in SQL, whether the subject fill's
  3748	  envelope was canonical (duplicate root keys, value type, padding, blankness) and what order id it
  3749	  named. It can no longer detect ANY of that. What it detects instead is DISAGREEMENT between two
  3750	  stored places: `fill_envelope_identity` (the authority's reading, bound to the exact document by
  3751	  `envelope_raw`) and the correction row's citation columns.
  3752	
  3753	  **AND THIS IS THE SAME TRUST BOUNDARY AS BEFORE, which is why the loss is acceptable rather than
  3754	  merely accepted.** The old clause could equally be satisfied by a FORGED ENVELOPE: a raw writer
  3755	  who wrote a clean, canonical envelope naming an order it never came from passed every one of
  3756	  those checks. **The trigger never could judge truth -- only CONSISTENCY.** What changed is which
  3757	  two artefacts must agree, not whether truth was ever verifiable in SQL.
  3758	
  3759	  **What it still catches, and these are not small:** a citation naming a different order than the
  3760	  stored reading; a reading the authority REFUSED; a document the authority has NOT read (the raw
  3761	  writer's own shape); and a document that CHANGED after its reading was taken -- the join is on
  3762	  the fill AND the document, so a substituted envelope stops matching and the surface fails CLOSED.
  3763	
  3764	  **Pinned, not merely written down:** `tests/data/test_22a_task11_citation_evidence.py::
  3765	  test_THE_DECLARED_LIMITATION_two_equal_but_wrong_values_are_ACCEPTED` asserts the acceptance. If a
  3766	  later change makes that row REJECT, the limitation is narrower than declared and **the
  3767	  declaration must be corrected, not the test silenced.**
  3768	
  3769	  *V2 fix:* none available in SQL, by construction. The only instrument that could close it is an
  3770	  authenticated envelope (L10's server-side nonce or POST-time re-fetch), which would make the
  3771	  document itself trustworthy and is the same fix L10 already names.
  3772	
  3773	* **L19 (AL-11) -- NO CONSUMER OF A STORED READING CHECKS THE CANONICALISER VERSION IT WAS WRITTEN
  3774	  UNDER, IN SQL OR IN PYTHON.** *(Codex `22A-R13-02`, round 13. `canonicalizer_version` appeared
  3775	  EXACTLY ONCE in the shipped migration -- its column declaration -- while SEVEN trigger sites
  3776	  referenced the table; the round-12 clause that prompted this became the seventh by copying its
  3777	  neighbour's shape including its omission.)*
  3778	
  3779	  *Reason:* the SERVICE is strictly stronger and cannot be mirrored here. `ensure_entry_fill_identities`
  3780	  re-runs the CURRENT canonicaliser over the whole population before any scan and `record_identity`
  3781	  RAISES when a stored answer disagrees with today's; SQL cannot re-run anything, and re-deriving
  3782	  the reading in SQL is the engine-boundary violation L18 forbids. **What is exposed:** after a
  3783	  canonicaliser bump whose ANSWER changes for some document, a RAW correction can be accepted on the
  3784	  older reading the service would refuse. **Direction: WRONG ACCEPTANCE, raw path only.**
  3785	
  3786	  **THE OBVIOUS FIX -- "require the current version in every consumer" -- WAS MEASURED AND
  3787	  REJECTED, in both of its halves, and that is why this is a declaration rather than a patch:**
  3788	  1. **At TWO of the six it INVERTS.** `last_word_subject_order_id` and `rung6_consumption_scan`
  3789	     read a stored reading as EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE. Filtering them on the version makes a stale
  3790	     reading INVISIBLE, which WIDENS acceptance. A blanket sweep of "all seven" would have shipped
  3791	     exactly that -- the reason the treatment is a per-site READ and not a global edit.
  3792	  2. **At the other four it manufactures a REFUSAL ON THE SERVICE PATH.** An AGREEING older reading
  3793	     is deliberately left in place (`test_an_agreeing_older_reading_is_left_alone` -- filtering on
  3794	     the version LABEL would fail every historical reading on the day the constant moves). The
  3795	     service would authorize and the trigger would then ABORT: authorize-then-abort, met four times
  3796	     on this arc already.
  3797	
  3798	  **SO THE ARMING ACTION IS GUARDED INSTEAD -- BY A LABEL COMPARATOR, AND THAT IS WHAT IT IS CALLED
  3799	  (amended 22A-R14-01, operator-ruled 2026-08-31).** A reading can only be stale if
  3800	  `ENVELOPE_CANONICALIZER_VERSION` MOVED between two writes; a row bearing a version nobody shipped
  3801	  is a forged identity row, which is L10/AL-10's class. `0037` therefore carries a
  3802	  `CANONICALIZER-VERSION-ANCHOR` mirroring the Python constant, and
  3803	  `tests/data/test_22a_canonicalizer_version_closure.py` compares the two representations -- so a
  3804	  LABEL bump FAILS THE SUITE, naming the required work, before any stale row can exist.
  3805	
  3806	  **WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, AND THE COUNTEREXAMPLE IS THIS ARC'S OWN.** It compares a Python constant
  3807	  to a SQL COMMENT: **two hand-maintained copies of a LABEL, neither of which is the canonicaliser's
  3808	  BEHAVIOUR. A canonicaliser change without a version bump is INVISIBLE to it.** `22A-R13-01` made
  3809	  `canonical_envelope_identity` answer `refused` where it answered `canonical` for every non-`str`
  3810	  document; the constant did not move; and this tripwire -- shipped in the very next commit --
  3811	  passed. For six commits the paragraph above was FALSE while it still read TRUE. **This section
  3812	  previously said the exposure was "CLOSED"; it is not, and the earlier sentence was the same false
  3813	  claim this arc exists to remove**, which is why the wording is amended rather than the instrument
  3814	  widened: *the principle was never "make every instrument exact"; it is "do not claim exact when
  3815	  you are not."* The blindness is now PINNED, executed rather than described

    30	class EnvelopeIdentityDriftError(RuntimeError):
    31	    """A stored reading disagrees with what the authority reads TODAY.
    32	
    33	    The row is append-only and bound to its document by ``envelope_raw``, so
    34	    the only way this can fire is a canonicaliser change or a forged row.  It
    35	    is LOUD rather than silently re-derived: silently preferring either answer
    36	    would re-create the two-readings-of-one-document class the stored reading
    37	    exists to delete.
    38	    """

    60	def record_identity(
    61	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, fill_id: int, envelope_raw: str,
    62	) -> tuple[str, str | None, str | None]:
    63	    """Derive THIS document's reading once and append it.  Idempotent.
    64	
    65	    SELECT-then-INSERT, never ``INSERT OR REPLACE``: a REPLACE would DELETE the
    66	    existing reading without firing the append-only DELETE trigger (measured on
    67	    sqlite 3.50.4 at the default ``recursive_triggers=OFF``) and substitute a
    68	    different identity for the same document.
    69	    """
    70	    from swing.trades.latched_origin import (
    71	        ENVELOPE_CANONICALIZER_VERSION,
    72	        canonical_envelope_identity,
    73	    )
    74	
    75	    identity = canonical_envelope_identity(envelope_raw)
    76	    current = (identity.state, identity.broker_order_id,
    77	               identity.instrument_symbol)
    78	    existing = stored_identity(conn, fill_id, envelope_raw)
    79	    if existing is not None:
    80	        if tuple(existing) != current:
    81	            raise EnvelopeIdentityDriftError(
    82	                f"fill {fill_id}'s stored envelope reading {tuple(existing)!r} "
    83	                f"disagrees with what the canonicaliser "
    84	                f"({ENVELOPE_CANONICALIZER_VERSION}) reads out of the SAME "
    85	                f"document today ({current!r}). The reading is append-only and "
    86	                "bound to its document, so this is a canonicaliser change or a "
    87	                "forged row; it is refused rather than silently re-derived."
    88	            )
    89	        return current
    90	    conn.execute(
    91	        f"INSERT INTO {TABLE} (fill_id, envelope_raw, envelope_state, "
    92	        " broker_order_id, instrument_symbol, canonicalizer_version, "
    93	        " recorded_ts) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
    94	        (int(fill_id), envelope_raw, identity.state, identity.broker_order_id,
    95	         identity.instrument_symbol, ENVELOPE_CANONICALIZER_VERSION,
    96	         datetime.now(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")),
    97	    )
    98	    return current

   101	def ensure_entry_fill_identities(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> int:
   102	    """Read EVERY envelope-bearing ENTRY fill, appending or RE-VERIFYING.
   103	
   104	    THIS IS THE 'BACKFILL', AND IT IS PERFORMED BY THE AUTHORITY.  The scans
   105	    that consume the stored reading (rung 6 and rung 8's consumption check, and
   106	    the citation trigger's own twin) can only see documents the service has
   107	    read, so a population that has never been read is a population the scan
   108	    would silently treat as empty.  Called from inside the ladder's write
   109	    reservation, so the set it establishes cannot move under it.
   110	
   111	    IT RE-VERIFIES, IT DOES NOT ONLY POPULATE (Codex 22A-R11-03, PROVEN BY
   112	    EXECUTION).  This selected `fei.identity_id IS NULL`, so an EXISTING
   113	    reading never passed through ``record_identity``'s drift check -- and the
   114	    rows it excluded are exactly the population the consumption scans consult:
   115	    OTHER trades' entry fills.  ``ENVELOPE_CANONICALIZER_VERSION``'s own
   116	    comment claims a reading made under an older grammar is "DISTINGUISHABLE
   117	    rather than silently trusted"; the pass that walks that population was the
   118	    one place the claim was never tested.
   119	
   120	    MEASURED, one dimension apart on the same world: a reading written by the
   121	    PRODUCTION writer under an older grammar -- `(canonical, None)` -- let a
   122	    SECOND trade be admitted from a mandate the first trade's entry fill
   123	    already consumes, where the current-grammar reading refuses it
   124	    `mandate_already_consumed`.  Only the CODE was advanced, which is what a
   125	    canonicaliser bump IS; the data was never forged.
   126	
   127	    THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE ANSWER, NEVER THE VERSION LABEL.  An older reading
   128	    that says the SAME thing is left exactly as it is -- filtering on the
   129	    version string would fail every historical reading closed on the day the
   130	    constant moves, a refusal manufactured by the guard.  A disagreement RAISES
   131	    (append-only: the row cannot be corrected in place), and every caller on
   132	    the ladder contains that raise into a fail-CLOSED refusal.
   133	
   134	    Returns the number of readings APPENDED; re-verified rows are not counted,
   135	    so an idempotent second call still returns 0.
   136	    """
   137	    if not table_exists(conn):
   138	        return 0
   139	    rows = conn.execute(
   140	        "SELECT f.fill_id, f.schwab_source_value_json, fei.identity_id "
   141	        "  FROM fills f "
   142	        f" LEFT JOIN {TABLE} fei ON fei.fill_id = f.fill_id "
   143	        "        AND fei.envelope_raw = f.schwab_source_value_json "
   144	        " WHERE f.action = 'entry' AND f.schwab_source_value_json IS NOT NULL "
   145	        " ORDER BY f.fill_id",
   146	    ).fetchall()
   147	    appended = 0
   148	    for fill_id, raw, existing_id in rows:
   149	        record_identity(conn, fill_id=int(fill_id), envelope_raw=raw)
   150	        if existing_id is None:
   151	            appended += 1
   152	    return appended

  2607	def correct_cohort_provenance(
  2608	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
  2609	    *,
  2610	    trade_id: int,
  2611	    cited_candidate_id: int,
  2612	    cited_recommendation_id: int,
  2613	    reason: str | None = None,
  2614	    cfg: Any = None,
  2615	) -> CohortProvenanceCorrectionResult:
  2616	    """Outer: owns ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` / COMMIT / ROLLBACK, and REJECTS a
  2617	    caller-held transaction -- never auto-detects, because an auto-detect
  2618	    guard re-introduces the race the explicit lock closed.
  2619	
  2620	    THERE IS NO ``applied_at`` PARAMETER (Codex R3 Major 1). A caller could
  2621	    previously pass ``applied_at='1900-01-01T00:00:00'`` and the audit row
  2622	    would durably record that the correction happened then -- reachable
  2623	    through a direct service call, and grammar validation established only
  2624	    that the value LOOKED like a timestamp, never that this surface OBSERVED
  2625	    it. In a table whose entire purpose is to hold claims that are true, the
  2626	    one field nobody may supply is when it happened. The clock is stamped
  2627	    INSIDE the transaction; tests that need determinism patch
  2628	    ``_APPLIED_AT_CLOCK``.
  2629	
  2630	    ``cfg`` IS WHAT MAKES ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` LOAD-BEARING FOR THE 22-A LADDER
  2631	    (AL-2 / review 22A-R2-03). The latch resolution issues its own ledger
  2632	    SELECTs and the derivation issues more; they are ONE world only because
  2633	    THIS function holds a write reservation across all of them. The resolver
  2634	    cannot own a transaction itself -- the single-transaction contract makes it
  2635	    the CALLER's, and auto-detecting an outer one re-introduces the race the
  2636	    explicit lock closed -- so the obligation lands here, and a test pins it
  2637	    rather than a comment promising it.
  2638	    """
  2639	    if conn.in_transaction:
  2640	        raise CallerHeldTransactionError(
  2641	            "correct_cohort_provenance must be called with no open "
  2642	            "transaction; compose via _correct_cohort_provenance_inner inside "
  2643	            "an existing tx. Nothing was written."
  2644	        )
  2645	    # THE ACQUISITION IS INSIDE THE PROTECTED REGION (Codex 22A-FIX-R2-03).
  2646	    # ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` sat OUTSIDE this ``try``, so a ``KeyboardInterrupt``
  2647	    # landing between the statement TAKING the write reservation and the
  2648	    # ``try`` being entered skipped the handler and left the reservation held
  2649	    # on a connection the CLI goes on using.  Same one-bytecode window as the
  2650	    # preview path, same recovery, and the two now agree.
  2651	    try:
  2652	        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
  2653	        result = _correct_cohort_provenance_inner(
  2654	            conn,
  2655	            trade_id=trade_id,
  2656	            cited_candidate_id=cited_candidate_id,
  2657	            cited_recommendation_id=cited_recommendation_id,
  2658	            reason=reason,
  2659	            cfg=cfg,
  2660	        )

  2663	    except BaseException as write_error:

  2665	        # ``KeyboardInterrupt`` / ``SystemExit`` / ``GeneratorExit`` derive
  2666	        # from ``BaseException`` alone, so a Ctrl-C landing between

  2670	        #

  1961	    # Bug-fix-AB (2026-04-29): pure-OOB response architecture.
  1962	    #
  1963	    # Background. The prior architecture emitted the new open-position
  1964	    # `<tr>` as PRIMARY content (no `hx-swap-oob`) plus OOB chunks for
  1965	    # `#status-strip`, `#watchlist-top5`, and (on hyp-recs origin)
  1966	    # `#hypothesis-recommendations`. Two production-confirmed bugs:
  1967	    #
  1968	    #   Bug A: the form's `hx-target="closest tr" hx-swap="outerHTML"`
  1969	    #     directs HTMX to replace the form's `<tr>` (in the SOURCE tbody —
  1970	    #     watchlist or hyp-recs). The new open-position row briefly lands
  1971	    #     in that source tbody, then OOB rebuilds nuke it. Nothing in the
  1972	    #     response targets `#open-positions`, so the open-positions table
  1973	    #     never updates without a hard refresh.
  1974	    #
  1975	    #   Bug B: a leading `<tr>` in the response triggers HTMX's
  1976	    #     `makeFragment` to wrap the whole response in a synthetic
  1977	    #     `<table><tbody>` for parsing. HTML5 nested-table parse rules
  1978	    #     then DROP the `<table>`s inside the OOB `<section>` chunks
  1979	    #     during the browser-side fragment parse. Operator's DevTools
  1980	    #     capture (2026-04-29) confirmed `htmx:oobAfterSwap` fires for
  1981	    #     `#watchlist-top5` but the post-swap DOM contains only the `<h2>`
  1982	    #     heading — the `<table>` and rows vanished at parse time.
  1983	    #
  1984	    # Fix. Make the response purely OOB: NO `<tr>` at fragment root.
  1985	    # The new row reaches `#open-positions` via an OOB swap that mirrors
  1986	    # `partials/prices_refresh_container.html.j2`'s pattern. Primary swap
  1987	    # content is empty; HTMX's `makeFragment` does not wrap-in-`<table>`;
  1988	    # foster-parenting/nested-table-stripping does not fire; OOB chunks
  1989	    # parse and apply cleanly. The form's `<tr>` (in the source tbody)
  1990	    # disappears as a side-effect of the watchlist-top5 / hyp-recs OOB
  1991	    # rebuild that replaces its containing section.
