  2255	-- ============================================================================
  2256	-- THE REPLACE BYPASS ON provenance_corrections (Codex 22A-R3-11, VERIFIED BY
  2257	-- EXECUTION 2026-08-25 -- the FOURTH confirmed member of the family and the
  2258	-- one on Demand C's own audit table of record).
  2259	--
  2260	-- 0036 gives this table an append-only UPDATE trigger and an append-only
  2261	-- DELETE trigger and NO no_replace. MEASURED at production settings
  2262	-- (recursive_triggers default OFF) against the real correction shape, which
  2263	-- carries TWO conflict targets -- provenance_correction_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
  2264	-- AUTOINCREMENT and the UNIQUE index ux_provenance_corrections_trade:
  2265	--
  2266	--   control UPDATE      -> BLOCKED ("provenance_corrections is APPEND-ONLY")
  2267	--   control DELETE      -> BLOCKED ("a correction cannot be deleted")
  2268	--   INSERT OR REPLACE   -> SUCCEEDS: correction_reason rewritten in place
  2269	--   bare REPLACE        -> SUCCEEDS: same
  2270	--
  2271	-- with BOTH append-only triggers present, canonical and UNFIRED. The DELETE
  2272	-- trigger is bypassed because REPLACE's implicit DELETE does not fire DELETE
  2273	-- triggers unless PRAGMA recursive_triggers is ON; it is OFF by default and
  2274	-- this repo never turns it on.
  2275	--
  2276	-- WHY IT IS WORSE HERE THAN ALMOST ANYWHERE. This is the audit table of
  2277	-- record: every row is a claim about WHY a trade's cohort keys were changed,
  2278	-- and the whole point of 0036's two triggers is that such a claim can never be
  2279	-- edited. A REPLACE through the UNIQUE additionally MOVES the correction's own
  2280	-- id, which any citation of it then silently repoints -- the id-reuse class
  2281	-- 0036's AUTOINCREMENT was chosen to avoid, arriving through the other door.
  2282	--
  2283	-- BOTH CONFLICT TARGETS ARE SCOPED. Guarding one leaves the other live.
  2284	--
  2285	-- NO PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, and the search that establishes it:
  2286	-- insert_provenance_correction (swing/data/repos/provenance_corrections.py) is
  2287	-- the ONE writer and issues a PLAIN INSERT with no ON CONFLICT clause, and
  2288	-- correct_cohort_provenance refuses a second correction per trade at its own
  2289	-- SELECT-first ladder before reaching it. A case-insensitive grep for
  2290	-- "insert or replace|replace into" across swing/ (*.py, *.sql) returns ZERO
  2291	-- executable statements. The production writer is pinned by a test that drives
  2292	-- correct_cohort_provenance on a SECOND trade and asserts the append lands.
  2293	-- ============================================================================
  2294	CREATE TRIGGER trg_pc_no_replace BEFORE INSERT ON provenance_corrections
  2295	WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM provenance_corrections
  2296	              WHERE (NEW.provenance_correction_id != -1
  2297	                     AND provenance_correction_id = NEW.provenance_correction_id)
  2298	                 OR trade_id = NEW.trade_id)
  2299	BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, '22-A barrier trg_pc_no_replace: provenance_corrections is APPEND-ONLY. A conflicting INSERT (INSERT OR REPLACE / REPLACE / INSERT OR IGNORE) would DELETE the existing correction, bypassing trg_provenance_corrections_append_only_delete at the default PRAGMA recursive_triggers=OFF, and rewrite or renumber the audit row of record for this trade. V1 records provenance ONCE per trade and has no re-correction path. To retire the barrier see the reversibility header of 0037_latch_order_mandate_links.sql.'); END;
  2300	
  2301	-- Schema version bump. MUST be the FINAL statement before COMMIT per the
  2302	-- Phase 9 section A.0 precedent (a truncated transaction would leave the
  2303	-- version stamp ahead of the schema).
  2304	UPDATE schema_version SET version = 37;
  2305	
  2306	COMMIT;
  1980	    IT WRITES, AND THIS SENTENCE USED TO SAY IT DID NOT (self-sweep SS-10, the
  1981	    same class as Codex 22A-R11-05 one caller up). PERSIST-CANONICAL made the
  1982	    ladder persist the AUTHORITY'S reading of the subject fill's envelope, and
  1983	    rung 6 populate the whole entry-fill reading population, so this is a
  1984	    WRITING function that both entry points -- apply and dry-run -- share. The
  1985	    apply owns ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE``; the dry run unwinds through a SAVEPOINT.
  1986	
  1987	    SELECT-FIRST IDEMPOTENCY LEADS THE LADDER, and it sits ABOVE ``--reason``
  1988	    validation, not merely above the unset-state gate. CLAUDE.md states the
  1989	    rule directly: a terminal-state row must return its existing audit-row id
  1990	    even with a stale or None payload. With ``--reason`` checked first, an
  1991	    already-applied re-run carrying an empty reason REFUSES instead of
  1992	    returning its correction id -- and a happy-path test using a valid reason
  1993	    cannot catch that.
  1994	    """
  1995	    trade = _load_trade_or_refuse(conn, trade_id)
  1996	
  1997	    # THE CITATION IDS ARE THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY, NOT PAYLOAD (Codex R1 Minor 5,
  1998	    # partially adopted). CLAUDE.md's SELECT-first rule is about a stale or
  1999	    # None PAYLOAD; the citation is what makes a request the SAME request, so
  2000	    # it cannot be optional without weakening the contract to "any re-run on
  2001	    # this trade_id succeeds" -- under which a typo'd replay would silently
  2002	    # report success against a citation it never named. `--reason` is the
  2003	    # payload and IS optional on the replay path; the citations stay required.
  2004	    #
  2005	    # What IS adopted: a non-int citation must produce this surface's typed
  2006	    # refusal rather than a bare `TypeError` from `int(...)` inside the
  2007	    # comparison below, which is reachable from a direct service call.
  2008	    for name, value in (
  2009	        ("cited_candidate_id", cited_candidate_id),
  2010	        ("cited_recommendation_id", cited_recommendation_id),
  2011	    ):
  2012	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
  2013	            raise _refuse(
  2014	                f"{name} must be an int row id; got {value!r}. The citation "
  2015	                "is the idempotency KEY, so it is required even on a replay."
  2016	            )
  2017	
  2018	    from swing.data.repos.provenance_corrections import get_correction_for_trade
  2019	
  2020	    existing = get_correction_for_trade(conn, trade_id)
  2021	    if existing is not None:
  2022	        same = (
  2023	            int(existing.cited_candidate_id) == int(cited_candidate_id)
  2024	            and int(existing.cited_daily_recommendation_id)
  2025	            == int(cited_recommendation_id)
  2026	        )
  2027	        if same:
  2028	            return _Authorized(trade=trade, already_applied=existing)
  2029	        raise _refuse(
  2030	            f"trade {trade_id} already has provenance correction "
  2031	            f"{existing.provenance_correction_id}, which cites candidate "
  2032	            f"{existing.cited_candidate_id} and daily_recommendations row "
  2033	            f"{existing.cited_daily_recommendation_id} -- not candidate "
  2034	            f"{cited_candidate_id} / row {cited_recommendation_id}. V1 records "
  2035	            "provenance ONCE per trade and there is no supersession path: "
  2036	            "re-deciding provenance is a different authority question."
  2037	        )
  2038	
  2039	    # THE UNSET-STATE VERDICT PRECEDES THE REASON INSTRUCTION (Codex R3 Minor
  2040	    # 7). It is TERMINAL and true whatever payload arrives, while "supply a
  2041	    # reason" is an INSTRUCTION that implies the rest of the request is sound.
  2042	    # With the reason first, a trade whose cohort keys are already populated
  2043	    # sent the operator away to compose a justification for an operation that
  2044	    # can never be authorized. This is the plan's own ordering principle --
  2045	    # every VERDICT before any INSTRUCTION -- applied to its own ladder.
  2046	    _gate_on_unset_state(trade)
  2047	    _reason_or_refuse(reason)
  2048	
  2049	    # THE TIER IS RESOLVED BEFORE THE LAST-WORD GUARD, AND THE GUARD IS WHAT
  2050	    # THE DISPATCH TURNS OFF (plan S2.7). The last-word guard ranks the
  2051	    # framework's BUCKET SERIES; the latch ladder is a DIFFERENT AUTHORITY the
  2052	    # guard structurally cannot see -- an append-only row the broker's
  2053	    # acceptance created. Under that authority the guard's refusal of an
  2054	    # `aplus` citation superseded by a later `watch` row is CORRECT for what
  2055	    # the guard is and WRONG for the question being asked, so the two are
  2056	    # dispatched between rather than composed.
  2057	    entry_fill = resolve_authoritative_entry_fill(conn, trade_id)
  2058	    latch = _resolve_latch_citation(
  2059	        conn, cfg, trade=trade, trade_id=trade_id, entry_fill=entry_fill)
  2060	    anchored = _anchor_half(
  2061	        conn,
  2062	        trade_id=trade_id,
  2063	        cited_candidate_id=cited_candidate_id,
  2064	        cited_recommendation_id=cited_recommendation_id,
  2065	        entry_fill=entry_fill,
  2066	        run_last_word_guard=latch is None,
  2067	    )
  2068	    if latch is not None and latch.fire_candidate_id != cited_candidate_id:
  2069	        # THE CITATION IS FORCED, NOT CHOSEN. Silently substituting the fire
  2070	        # would write a correction the operator never asked for; refusing and
  2071	        # NAMING it leaves the decision where it belongs.
  2072	        raise _refuse(
  2073	            f"candidate {cited_candidate_id} is not the fire this trade's "
  2074	            f"accepted latch order was placed against: broker order "
  2075	            f"{latch.broker_order_id} (link {latch.link_id}) names candidate "
  2076	            f"{latch.fire_candidate_id}. Under the latch ladder the citation "
  2077	            "is FORCED to the fire an append-only broker acceptance created; "
  2078	            "there is nothing to choose among."
  2079	        )
  2080	    return _Authorized(
  2081	        trade=trade, anchored=anchored,
  2082	        derived=_derive(conn, anchored, run_fill_gate=latch is None),
  2083	        latch=latch)

  2086	def _na_suffix_note(anchored: _Anchored, derived: _Derived) -> str | None:
  2087	    """Explain a ``; failed: X`` suffix earned by an ``na`` result.
  2088	
  2089	    A NAMED WART, not a hidden one. ``_non_pass_criterion_names`` counts `na`
  2090	    as non-pass -- matching `bucket_for`'s VCP gating -- so a criterion whose
  2091	    result is `na` renders under a `failed:` heading. That inaccuracy is
  2092	    PRE-EXISTING in the framework's own builder and fixing it would change
  2093	    every future recommendation label, so this surface reuses the builder
  2094	    rather than minting a second implementation, and SAYS SO wherever the
  2095	    string is shown.
  2096	    """
  2097	    na_names = sorted(
  2098	        c.criterion_name for c in anchored.cited.candidate.criteria
  2099	        if c.result == "na"
  2100	    )
  2101	    if not na_names or "; failed:" not in derived.hypothesis_label:
  2102	        return None
  2103	    return (
  2104	        "the derived label's `failed:` suffix includes "
  2105	        f"{', '.join(na_names)}, whose result is `na` rather than `fail`. "
  2106	        "The framework's own label builder counts `na` as non-pass, so the "
  2107	        "wording is a pre-existing inaccuracy in that builder and not "
  2108	        "something this correction introduced."
  2109	    )
  2110	
  2111	
  2112	# The dry run's unwind point. Named rather than inlined so the ROLLBACK TO and
  2113	# the RELEASE cannot drift apart, which is how a savepoint leaks.
  2114	#
  2115	# **THE NAME IS PER-INVOCATION, NOT FIXED (Codex 22A-FIX-R4-01, verified by
  2116	# execution against real SQLite savepoint behaviour).**  A fixed name is a NAME
  2117	# COLLISION waiting for a caller: when this call runs inside a caller-held
  2118	# transaction and its own `SAVEPOINT` fails BEFORE taking effect, the
  2119	# acquisition recovery's `ROLLBACK TO` / `RELEASE` target whatever savepoint of
  2120	# that name already exists -- **the CALLER'S** -- discarding unrelated caller
  2121	# work and releasing a nesting level it owns.  Measured: with the authorizer
  2122	# denying only the new savepoint, an uncommitted caller row was rolled back and
  2123	# the caller's savepoint released.  A fixed name also STACKS across repeated
  2124	# previews inside one caller transaction, which is the other half of it.
  2125	#
  2126	# The PREFIX stays stable so a leaked savepoint is still identifiable by name
  2127	# in a log or an inspection; only the suffix moves.
  2128	_PREVIEW_SAVEPOINT_PREFIX = "cohort_provenance_preview_sp"
  2129	
  2130	
  2131	def _is_no_such_savepoint(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
  2132	    """SQLite explicitly saying the savepoint name does not exist.
  2133	
  2134	    The ONE failure this path may treat as silence (Codex 22A-FIX-R7-02).
  2135	    Matched on the engine's own message rather than on the exception TYPE,
  2136	    because `sqlite3.OperationalError` covers a busy database and a dozen
  2137	    other conditions that are NOT proof the savepoint is gone -- and the
  2138	    difference between "it never existed" and "I could not check" is exactly
  2139	    what the caller needs.
  2140	    """
  2141	    return (isinstance(exc, sqlite3.OperationalError)
  2142	            and "no such savepoint" in str(exc).lower())

  2144	
  2145	def _try(conn, sql: str) -> BaseException | None:
  2146	    """Run a cleanup statement; return its failure rather than raising it.
  2147	
  2148	    SELF-SWEEP SS-22A-FIX-2.  Every cleanup verb on this path must be
  2149	    ATTEMPTED even when an earlier one failed, and `BaseException` is the
  2150	    class rather than `sqlite3.Error` -- an interrupt is exactly the failure a
  2151	    cleanup path has to survive, and enumerating the raisable types is the
  2152	    hand-maintained-roster failure this module has now met four times.
  2153	    """
  2154	    try:
  2155	        conn.execute(sql)
  2156	    except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- the CLASS, not a roster
  2157	        return exc
  2158	    return None

  2161	def _new_preview_savepoint() -> str:
  2162	    """A savepoint name no caller can already hold.
  2163	
  2164	    ``uuid4().hex`` rather than a counter: a counter is per-PROCESS, and two
  2165	    processes sharing a database file (the CLI and the web app) can hold the
  2166	    same caller transaction chain in sequence.
  2167	    """
  2168	    import uuid
  2169	
  2170	    return f"{_PREVIEW_SAVEPOINT_PREFIX}_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"

  2173	def preview_cohort_provenance_correction(
  2174	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
  2175	    *,
  2176	    trade_id: int,
  2177	    cited_candidate_id: int,
  2178	    cited_recommendation_id: int,
  2179	    reason: str | None = None,
  2180	    cfg: Any = None,
  2181	) -> CohortProvenanceCorrectionPreview:
  2182	    """``--dry-run``: NET-ZERO, and that is a weaker claim than write-free.
  2183	
  2184	    Raises the SAME refusals the write path raises, because both call the same
  2185	    authorization function -- one authorization function, two entry points, so
  2186	    ``--dry-run`` cannot diverge from apply.
  2187	
  2188	    IT IS NO LONGER A READ-ONLY LADDER, AND THE TEXT SAYS SO (Codex
  2189	    22A-R11-05).  PERSIST-CANONICAL made the SHARED authorization WRITE: it
  2190	    canonicalises the subject fill's envelope and persists that reading, and
  2191	    behind it the latch rungs can populate the whole entry-fill reading
  2192	    population.  So this docstring's predecessor -- *"every read-only check,
  2193	    writing nothing"*, beside a comment claiming *"still takes no write
  2194	    lock"* -- was FALSE while it still read TRUE, which is gotcha #31 inside
  2195	    the very function the reshape moved.
  2196	
  2197	    WHAT IS GUARANTEED NOW, precisely: every write this call makes is unwound
  2198	    before it returns, in EVERY transaction posture, by a SAVEPOINT rolled
  2199	    back unconditionally.  What is NOT guaranteed, and is stated rather than
  2200	    implied: for the duration of the call the connection takes a WRITE LOCK.
  2201	    """
  2202	    # A DRY RUN MUST AT LEAST BE COHERENT WITH ITSELF (Codex R2 Major 4). The
  2203	    # authorization ladder runs a dozen separate SELECTs, and under sqlite3's
  2204	    # default isolation each one sees whatever is committed at that instant --
  2205	    # so a pipeline run, a status transition or a reconciliation landing
  2206	    # MID-LADDER could make the preview report a mix of two worlds. A DEFERRED
  2207	    # read transaction pins ONE snapshot for the whole ladder and is rolled
  2208	    # back unconditionally.
  2209	    #
  2210	    # AND THE UNWIND IS A SAVEPOINT, NOT THE `owns_read_tx` ROLLBACK (Codex
  2211	    # 22A-R11-05). That rollback fires only when this function OWNS the
  2212	    # transaction; called inside a caller-held one it fired not at all, so the
  2213	    # dry run's writes survived and the CALLER'S OWN COMMIT made them durable
  2214	    # -- a `--dry-run` that persists. MEASURED: one `fill_envelope_identity`
  2215	    # row remained after the caller committed. The savepoint unwinds the same
  2216	    # way in both postures, and the caller's transaction is LEFT OPEN, because
  2217	    # closing someone else's transaction would be a second defect wearing this
  2218	    # one's clothes.
  2219	    #
  2220	    # WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUY, stated rather than implied: it does not bind the
  2221	    # preview to a LATER apply. The apply re-runs the ENTIRE ladder, so it can
  2222	    # never write on stale inputs -- it either derives afresh or refuses -- but
  2223	    # the operator may be shown one reading and get another outcome. Closing
  2224	    # that needs a digest threaded preview -> apply, and the CLI parameter
  2225	    # manifest is pinned at EXACTLY five by a test that exists to keep a VALUE
  2226	    # out of the operator's hands. Recorded as a V2 dependency; the apply
  2227	    # prints the anchors it actually used so a divergence is visible at the
  2228	    # moment of the write.
  2229	    # THE ACQUISITION IS INSIDE THE PROTECTED REGION (Codex 22A-FIX-R2-03).
  2230	    # `BEGIN DEFERRED` used to sit OUTSIDE this `try`, so a `KeyboardInterrupt`
  2460	        cited_hypothesis_id=derived.hypothesis_id,
  2461	        cited_hypothesis_name=derived.hypothesis_name,
  2462	        cited_hypothesis_status_history_id=derived.status_interval.history_id,
  2463	        entry_fill_id=anchored.entry_fill.fill_id,
  2464	        entry_fill_session_date=anchored.fill_session,
  2465	        candidate_action_session_date=anchored.candidate_anchor,
  2466	        recommendation_action_session_date=anchored.recommendation_anchor,
  2467	        run_ts_raw=anchored.run_ts_raw,
  2468	        run_ts_utc=anchored.run_ts_utc,
  2469	        pipeline_finished_ts_raw=derived.pipeline_finished_ts_raw,
  2470	        status_window_upper_utc=derived.status_window_upper_utc,
  2471	        derivation_rule_version=DERIVATION_RULE_VERSION,
  2472	        pre_values={
  2473	            "trades.hypothesis_label": trade.hypothesis_label,
  2474	            "trades.candidate_id": trade.candidate_id,
  2475	            "trades.trade_origin": trade.trade_origin,
  2476	        },
  2477	        post_values={
  2478	            "trades.hypothesis_label": derived.hypothesis_label,
  2479	            "trades.candidate_id": derived.candidate_id,
  2480	            "trades.trade_origin": derived.trade_origin,
  2481	        },
  2482	        na_criterion_suffix_note=_na_suffix_note(anchored, derived),
  2483	        admission_tier=tier,
  2484	        cited_latch_link_id=None if latch is None else latch.link_id,
  2485	        cited_latch_validity_intent_id=(
  2486	            None if latch is None else latch.validity_intent_id),
  2487	        cited_latch_place_intent_id=(
  2488	            None if latch is None else latch.place_intent_id),
  2489	        cited_latch_broker_order_id=(
  2490	            None if latch is None else latch.broker_order_id),
  2491	        cited_latch_admission_basis=(
  2492	            None if latch is None else latch.admission_basis),
  2493	    )

  2567	def _compose_reason(
  2568	    operator_reason: str, anchored: _Anchored, derived: _Derived,
  2569	) -> str:
  2570	    """The operator's reason plus the clause only the server can write.
  2571	
  2572	    The audit trail explains its OWN string: which two rows were cited, what
  2573	    their anchors were, which fill supplied `F`, which hypothesis and interval
  2574	    authorized the label, and -- when it applies -- why the label carries a
  2575	    `failed:` heading over a criterion whose result was `na`.
  2576	    """
  2577	    parts = [
  2578	        operator_reason.strip(),
  2579	        "[server-derived: cohort keys taken from candidates row "
  2580	        f"{anchored.cited.candidate_id} (evaluation run "
  2581	        f"{anchored.cited.evaluation_run_id}, action session "
  2582	        f"{anchored.candidate_anchor}) confirmed by daily_recommendations row "
  2583	        f"{anchored.recommendation.id} (action session "
  2584	        # "NEITHER POST-DATES", NOT "BOTH PRE-DATE" (Codex 22A-R7-05). The
  2585	        # admission predicate is `<=`: an anchor EQUAL to the fill session is
  2586	        # admissible, because a session-N record is normally produced on the
  2587	        # EVENING of session N-1. So a valid same-session correction stored
  2588	        # prose claiming STRICT precedence beside frozen anchor columns showing
  2589	        # equality -- a permanently false sentence in the audit narrative,
  2590	        # which is the one thing this table exists to not contain.
  2591	        f"{anchored.recommendation_anchor}); NEITHER post-dates the "
  2592	        f"entry fill {anchored.entry_fill.fill_id}'s session "
  2593	        f"{anchored.fill_session}. Hypothesis {derived.hypothesis_id} "
  2594	        f"({derived.hypothesis_name}) was 'active' over "
  2595	        f"[{anchored.run_ts_utc}, {derived.status_window_upper_utc}] UTC per "
  2596	        f"status-history row {derived.status_interval.history_id}. Label "
  2597	        f"written verbatim from the framework's own builder "
  2598	        f"(derivation rule {DERIVATION_RULE_VERSION}): "
  2599	        f"{derived.hypothesis_label!r}.]",
  2600	    ]
  2601	    note = _na_suffix_note(anchored, derived)
  2602	    if note:
  2603	        parts.append(f"[{note}]")
  2604	    return " ".join(parts)
  2605

  2607	def correct_cohort_provenance(
  2608	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
  2609	    *,
  2610	    trade_id: int,
  2611	    cited_candidate_id: int,
  2612	    cited_recommendation_id: int,
  2613	    reason: str | None = None,
  2614	    cfg: Any = None,
  2615	) -> CohortProvenanceCorrectionResult:
  2616	    """Outer: owns ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` / COMMIT / ROLLBACK, and REJECTS a
  2617	    caller-held transaction -- never auto-detects, because an auto-detect
  2618	    guard re-introduces the race the explicit lock closed.
  2619	
  2620	    THERE IS NO ``applied_at`` PARAMETER (Codex R3 Major 1). A caller could
  2621	    previously pass ``applied_at='1900-01-01T00:00:00'`` and the audit row
  2622	    would durably record that the correction happened then -- reachable
  2623	    through a direct service call, and grammar validation established only
  2624	    that the value LOOKED like a timestamp, never that this surface OBSERVED
  2625	    it. In a table whose entire purpose is to hold claims that are true, the
  2626	    one field nobody may supply is when it happened. The clock is stamped
  2627	    INSIDE the transaction; tests that need determinism patch
  2628	    ``_APPLIED_AT_CLOCK``.
  2629	
  2630	    ``cfg`` IS WHAT MAKES ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` LOAD-BEARING FOR THE 22-A LADDER
  2631	    (AL-2 / review 22A-R2-03). The latch resolution issues its own ledger
  2632	    SELECTs and the derivation issues more; they are ONE world only because
  2633	    THIS function holds a write reservation across all of them. The resolver
  2634	    cannot own a transaction itself -- the single-transaction contract makes it
  2635	    the CALLER's, and auto-detecting an outer one re-introduces the race the
  2636	    explicit lock closed -- so the obligation lands here, and a test pins it
  2637	    rather than a comment promising it.
  2638	    """
  2639	    if conn.in_transaction:
  2640	        raise CallerHeldTransactionError(
  2641	            "correct_cohort_provenance must be called with no open "
  2642	            "transaction; compose via _correct_cohort_provenance_inner inside "
  2643	            "an existing tx. Nothing was written."
  2644	        )
  2645	    # THE ACQUISITION IS INSIDE THE PROTECTED REGION (Codex 22A-FIX-R2-03).
  2646	    # ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` sat OUTSIDE this ``try``, so a ``KeyboardInterrupt``
  2647	    # landing between the statement TAKING the write reservation and the
  2648	    # ``try`` being entered skipped the handler and left the reservation held
  2649	    # on a connection the CLI goes on using.  Same one-bytecode window as the
  2650	    # preview path, same recovery, and the two now agree.
  2651	    try:
  2652	        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
  2653	        result = _correct_cohort_provenance_inner(
  2654	            conn,
  2655	            trade_id=trade_id,
  2656	            cited_candidate_id=cited_candidate_id,
  2657	            cited_recommendation_id=cited_recommendation_id,
  2658	            reason=reason,
  2659	            cfg=cfg,
  2660	        )
  2661	        conn.commit()
  2662	        return result
  2663	    except BaseException as write_error:
  2664	        # ``BaseException``, NOT ``Exception`` (reviewer B, P3).
  2665	        # ``KeyboardInterrupt`` / ``SystemExit`` / ``GeneratorExit`` derive
  2666	        # from ``BaseException`` alone, so a Ctrl-C landing between
  2667	        # ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` and ``COMMIT`` skipped this rollback and left an
  2668	        # open WRITE transaction -- holding the reservation -- on a connection
  2669	        # the CLI goes on using.
  2670	        #
  2671	        # AND THE ROLLBACK'S OWN FAILURE IS NOT SUPPRESSED EITHER (Codex
  2672	        # 22A-FIX-R2-04).  This was `contextlib.suppress(sqlite3.Error)`, which
  2673	        # is the EXACT composition the preview path one function up declares
  2674	        # MORE DANGEROUS and surfaces with a chained error -- `AL-15`'s
  2675	        # standard, applied to the preview four commits earlier and not to the
  2676	        # path that actually WRITES.  A leg cannot hold one standard for its
  2677	        # dry run and another for its apply.
  2678	        #
  2679	        # `conn.in_transaction` rather than a remembered flag, for R2-03's
  2680	        # reason: on the interrupted-acquisition path only the connection knows
  2681	        # whether the transaction opened.
  2682	        if conn.in_transaction:
  2683	            try:
  2684	                conn.rollback()
  2685	            # SELF-SWEEP SS-22A-FIX-2: `BaseException`, not the roster.
  2686	            except BaseException as cleanup_error:  # noqa: BLE001
  2687	                log.error(
  2688	                    "22-A: the cohort-provenance correction failed (%s) AND "
  2689	                    "could not roll back (%s). The WRITE transaction is STILL "
  2690	                    "OPEN, its reservation still held, and this connection "
  2691	                    "MUST BE DISCARDED rather than reused.",
  2692	                    write_error, cleanup_error)
  2693	                raise cleanup_error from write_error
  2694	        raise

  3698	  reasoning is recorded because it marks where the boundary is.** Cohort membership is decided by
  3699	  `label_matches_hypothesis` (`swing/metrics/label_match.py:26-37`, **read in full and VERIFIED
  3700	  here**: it matches on exact equality, on `name + " "`, or on `name + ";"`), **so a label matches
  3701	  its hypothesis with or without the failed-criteria suffix.** Criteria drift can therefore change
  3702	  the SUFFIX but **cannot move a trade between cohorts**; it can only make a re-derivation's suffix
  3703	  disagree with the stored label, and Demand C's drift reader is already the instrument that
  3704	  surfaces exactly that. Extending the barrier to a second table on a cosmetic-drift consequence
  3705	  would be scope creep past the evidence. **REVISIT TRIGGER, stated so this is a decision with an
  3706	  expiry rather than a permanent shrug: if the drift reader ever fires on a criteria-suffix
  3707	  mismatch in PRODUCTION, L13 re-opens and the barrier is re-proposed.**
  3708	
  3709	  **Trade 25 is affected**: its derived label `'A+ baseline (aplus)'` has no suffix, and a criteria
  3710	  deletion would produce the same empty suffix, so the absence is not self-proving -- **but under
  3711	  the ruling above that is a suffix-fidelity question, not a cohort-membership one**, which is
  3712	  precisely the bound CHARC drew.
  3713	* **L9 -- The `fill` terminal is heuristic evidence** (S2.3.1). *Reason:* `_match_fill`'s windowed
  3714	  rung does not inspect order ids. Mitigated: consumption is established by the order-id envelope
  3715	  scan above, and a `fill`-driven refusal names the trade and its `fill_link_basis`. The residual
  3716	  is a possible FALSE REFUSAL -- fail-closed, never a false admission.
  3717	* **L11 -- Decisions are time-scoped conservatively and coarsely** (S2.3.4b). *Reason:*
  3718	  `recorded_ts` is naive LOCAL and a fill carries only a DATE, so the as-of comparison is
  3719	  date-to-date in one domain and refuses same-session ambiguity outright rather than inventing a
  3720	  third clock domain to order them. It can only refuse, never admit.
  3721	* **L12 -- A future `candidates` pruner becomes a migration-level operation** (S4.5). *Reason:* the
  3722	  DELETE barrier is what makes the epoch's id comparison sound; relaxing it silently unsounds the
  3723	  freeze tier. Pruning is still possible -- drop trigger, prune, recreate, re-stamp the epoch -- it
  3724	  is simply no longer an ordinary write.
  3725	* **L10 -- The fill envelope is operator-submitted and its order id is not authenticated**
  3726	  (S2.4.1). *Reason:* `record_entry` cannot re-verify with the broker, and `fill_origin` is derived
  3727	  from the same hidden inputs, so no rung of the ladder is independent evidence. Threat model:
  3728	  single-operator local application; the realistic failure is a stale or mis-copied envelope, which
  3729	  every guard must simultaneously fail to catch. **What still gets through is named in S2.4.1.**
  3730	  V2 fix: a server-side nonce or a POST-time re-fetch. **Flagged for CHARC/RD.**
  3731	* **L18 -- THE CITATION TRIGGER CAN NO LONGER JUDGE A FILL'S ENVELOPE AT ALL; IT VERIFIES ONLY
  3732	  THAT THE AUTHORITY'S STORED READING AND THE CITATION AGREE. A RAW WRITER STORING TWO
  3733	  EQUAL-BUT-WRONG VALUES PASSES THE EQUALITY CHECK.** *(Declared at the PERSIST-CANONICAL reshape,
  3734	  CHARC + RD 2026-08-26, as a condition of the ruling -- stated NOW rather than discovered later.)*
  3735	
  3736	  *Reason:* ten review rounds never converged, and three CONSECUTIVE rounds each produced a
  3737	  DISTINCT engine-semantic divergence between Python and SQLite -- `json.loads` ACCEPTS a document
  3738	  containing `NaN` where `json_valid` REJECTS it; `str.strip()` removes tab/newline/NBSP where
  3739	  `trim()` removes ASCII space only; `1002937461 == '1002937461'` is False in Python and True in
  3740	  SQL against a TEXT-affinity column. All three reproduced independently. Zero findings were ever
  3741	  reopened across 74, so this was never careless execution: it is a structural property of
  3742	  mirroring a nontrivial predicate across engines that disagree in at least three independent ways,
  3743	  and nothing said three was the last. **RD's sentence, adopted verbatim by CHARC into the
  3744	  convention: SQL VERIFIES A FACT; IT MUST NEVER RE-DERIVE A JUDGMENT ACROSS AN ENGINE BOUNDARY --
  3745	  the twin mirrors the AUTHORITY by consuming its OUTPUT, not by reimplementing its reasoning.**
  3746	
  3747	  **WHAT WAS LOST, EXACTLY.** The trigger previously re-derived, in SQL, whether the subject fill's
  3748	  envelope was canonical (duplicate root keys, value type, padding, blankness) and what order id it
  3749	  named. It can no longer detect ANY of that. What it detects instead is DISAGREEMENT between two
  3750	  stored places: `fill_envelope_identity` (the authority's reading, bound to the exact document by
  3751	  `envelope_raw`) and the correction row's citation columns.
  3752	
  3753	  **AND THIS IS THE SAME TRUST BOUNDARY AS BEFORE, which is why the loss is acceptable rather than
  3754	  merely accepted.** The old clause could equally be satisfied by a FORGED ENVELOPE: a raw writer
  3755	  who wrote a clean, canonical envelope naming an order it never came from passed every one of
  3756	  those checks. **The trigger never could judge truth -- only CONSISTENCY.** What changed is which
  3757	  two artefacts must agree, not whether truth was ever verifiable in SQL.
  3758	
  3759	  **What it still catches, and these are not small:** a citation naming a different order than the
  3760	  stored reading; a reading the authority REFUSED; a document the authority has NOT read (the raw
  3761	  writer's own shape); and a document that CHANGED after its reading was taken -- the join is on
  3762	  the fill AND the document, so a substituted envelope stops matching and the surface fails CLOSED.
  3763	
  3764	  **Pinned, not merely written down:** `tests/data/test_22a_task11_citation_evidence.py::
  3765	  test_THE_DECLARED_LIMITATION_two_equal_but_wrong_values_are_ACCEPTED` asserts the acceptance. If a
  3766	  later change makes that row REJECT, the limitation is narrower than declared and **the
  3767	  declaration must be corrected, not the test silenced.**
  3768	
  3769	  *V2 fix:* none available in SQL, by construction. The only instrument that could close it is an
  3770	  authenticated envelope (L10's server-side nonce or POST-time re-fetch), which would make the
  3771	  document itself trustworthy and is the same fix L10 already names.
  3772	
  3773	* **L19 (AL-11) -- NO CONSUMER OF A STORED READING CHECKS THE CANONICALISER VERSION IT WAS WRITTEN
  3774	  UNDER, IN SQL OR IN PYTHON.** *(Codex `22A-R13-02`, round 13. `canonicalizer_version` appeared
  3775	  EXACTLY ONCE in the shipped migration -- its column declaration -- while SEVEN trigger sites
  3776	  referenced the table; the round-12 clause that prompted this became the seventh by copying its
  3777	  neighbour's shape including its omission.)*
  3778	
  3779	  *Reason:* the SERVICE is strictly stronger and cannot be mirrored here. `ensure_entry_fill_identities`
  3780	  re-runs the CURRENT canonicaliser over the whole population before any scan and `record_identity`
  3781	  RAISES when a stored answer disagrees with today's; SQL cannot re-run anything, and re-deriving
  3782	  the reading in SQL is the engine-boundary violation L18 forbids. **What is exposed:** after a
  3783	  canonicaliser bump whose ANSWER changes for some document, a RAW correction can be accepted on the
  3784	  older reading the service would refuse. **Direction: WRONG ACCEPTANCE, raw path only.**
  3785	
  3786	  **THE OBVIOUS FIX -- "require the current version in every consumer" -- WAS MEASURED AND
  3787	  REJECTED, in both of its halves, and that is why this is a declaration rather than a patch:**
  3788	  1. **At TWO of the six it INVERTS.** `last_word_subject_order_id` and `rung6_consumption_scan`
  3789	     read a stored reading as EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE. Filtering them on the version makes a stale
  3790	     reading INVISIBLE, which WIDENS acceptance. A blanket sweep of "all seven" would have shipped
  3791	     exactly that -- the reason the treatment is a per-site READ and not a global edit.
  3792	  2. **At the other four it manufactures a REFUSAL ON THE SERVICE PATH.** An AGREEING older reading
  3793	     is deliberately left in place (`test_an_agreeing_older_reading_is_left_alone` -- filtering on
  3794	     the version LABEL would fail every historical reading on the day the constant moves). The
  3795	     service would authorize and the trigger would then ABORT: authorize-then-abort, met four times
     1	"""AL-3 IS CLOSURE-CHECKED, NOT HAND-MAINTAINED (operator-ruled 2026-08-27).
     2	
     3	AL-3 -- limitation **L17** in the arc plan -- declares which citation-trigger
     4	clauses are SERVICE-VALIDATED: SQL asserts presence, type and verdict, and the
     5	judgment rests on state no subquery can reach.  It has always ended with the
     6	words *"AL-3's roster is exactly those three."*
     7	
     8	**THAT ROSTER HAS BEEN WRONG THREE TIMES, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE MIGRATION
     9	RECORDS THE FIRST AGAINST ITSELF.**  ``22A-R9-05`` found a migration comment
    10	citing AL-3 for a clause AL-3 does not name -- *"silently broadened a declared
    11	limitation roster to cover something nobody had ruled on"*
    12	(``0037:1279-1283``).  ``SS-12`` found the no-REPLACE barrier roster one member
    13	short of what the schema installs.  ``22A-R12-02``/``22A-R12-03`` found AL-3
    14	short by two.
    15	
    16	The implementer's own sentence at ``SS-12`` is the instruction this file
    17	encodes: **the roster is not the fix; the closure check is.**  So there is
    18	exactly ONE hand-written AL-3 roster in the repo -- the marked region inside
    19	L17 -- and this module holds it against what the CODE actually classifies and
    20	what the MIGRATION actually binds, **in both directions**.  A clause added
    21	later as service-validated without an L17 entry fails here; an L17 entry
    22	claiming a clause the code calls SQL-bound fails here; an L17 entry whose
    23	declared axis disagrees with the migration fails here.
    24	
    25	WHAT THE CHECK FOUND ON ITS FIRST RUN, recorded because a closure check that
    26	never reported anything would be indistinguishable from a decorative one:
    27	
    28	  * ``fill_session_is_session`` -- classified ``SERVICE_VALIDATED`` in
    29	    ``PROBE_GUARD_CLAUSES`` since ``22A-R6-06``, with a comment explaining that
    30	    no subquery can enumerate the NYSE calendar, and named NOWHERE in AL-3.
    31	    Its acceptance was already pinned by an executing test.  **The code was
    32	    truthful and the declaration was not** -- which is the exact defect this
    33	    arc spent twelve rounds eliminating everywhere else.
    34	  * the anchoring-fill clause -- service-validated in AL-3's own sense and
    35	    outside both blob rosters, so no amount of walking the blob rosters would
    36	    ever have surfaced it; it is declared as a NON-BLOB member and carries its
    37	    anchor in the migration text.
    38	  * L17's PROSE was additionally stale in a THIRD way nobody had reported: it
    39	    said *"rungs 7 and 8 and the five envelope guards ... these seven"* and
    40	    *"the nine SQL-bound rungs"*, while the shipped migration SQL-binds all
    41	    five envelope guards at correction time.  Measured: 14 SQL-bound and 5
    42	    service-validated of 19 clauses, not 9 and 7 of 16.
    43	
    44	FROZEN CLOCK: nothing here reads a clock.
    45	"""
    46	from __future__ import annotations

    54	    AUTHORIZATION_CLAUSES,
    55	    PROBE_GUARD_CLAUSES,
    56	    SERVICE_VALIDATED,
    57	    SQL_BOUND,
    58	)

    60	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    61	MIGRATION_0037 = (
    62	    REPO_ROOT / "swing" / "data" / "migrations"
    63	    / "0037_latch_order_mandate_links.sql"
    64	)
    65	PLAN = (
    66	    REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "superpowers" / "plans"
    67	    / "2026-08-24-phase22-arc-a-entry-path-order-mandate-binding.md"
    68	)

    70	ALL_CLAUSES = AUTHORIZATION_CLAUSES + PROBE_GUARD_CLAUSES
    71	BY_KEY = {c.key: c for c in ALL_CLAUSES}
    72	
    73	# The axis vocabulary.  A two-valued SQL_BOUND/SERVICE_VALIDATED label cannot
    74	# say WHICH half is unproved -- ``decision_ordering``'s own comment says so in
    75	# the source -- and that ambiguity is precisely how a clause whose INPUT is
    76	# bound and whose VERDICT is not went unnamed for eleven dispatches.
    77	INPUT_UNBOUND = "INPUT_UNBOUND"
    78	VERDICT_UNPROVEN = "VERDICT_UNPROVEN"
    79	PREDICATE_WEAKER = "PREDICATE_WEAKER_THAN_THE_SERVICE"
    80	SET_INCOMPLETE = "SET_INCOMPLETE"
    81	AXES = (INPUT_UNBOUND, VERDICT_UNPROVEN, PREDICATE_WEAKER, SET_INCOMPLETE)
    82	
    83	# Axes whose members are blob clauses and must therefore be SERVICE_VALIDATED
    84	# in the code roster.
    85	_BLOB_AXES = (INPUT_UNBOUND, VERDICT_UNPROVEN, SET_INCOMPLETE)

    88	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    89	# The plan's marked regions -- the ONE hand-written roster.
    90	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    91	_REGION = "<!-- AL3-{name}-{edge} -->"
    92	_BACKTICK = re.compile(r"`([^`]+)`")
    93	
    94	
    95	def _region(name: str) -> str:
    96	    text = PLAN.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    97	    begin, end = _REGION.format(name=name, edge="BEGIN"), _REGION.format(
    98	        name=name, edge="END")
    99	    assert begin in text and end in text, (
   100	        f"the plan carries no AL-3 {name} region; L17 is the ONE place the "
   101	        f"roster is written and this check cannot verify a roster that is not "
   102	        f"there")
   103	    return text.split(begin, 1)[1].split(end, 1)[0]
   104	
   105	
   106	def _bullets(region: str) -> list[str]:
   107	    out: list[str] = []
   108	    for line in region.splitlines():
   109	        if line.lstrip().startswith("* "):
   110	            out.append(line.strip()[2:])
   111	        elif out and line.strip():
   112	            out[-1] += " " + line.strip()
   113	    return out
   114	
   115	
   116	def _parse(region: str) -> dict[str, dict[str, str | None]]:
   117	    entries: dict[str, dict[str, str | None]] = {}
   118	    for bullet in _bullets(region):
   119	        ticks = _BACKTICK.findall(bullet)
   120	        assert ticks, f"an AL-3 bullet names no clause: {bullet[:80]!r}"
   121	        key = ticks[0]
   122	        axes = [a for a in AXES if a in bullet]
   123	        assert len(axes) == 1, (
   124	            f"AL-3 entry `{key}` must name EXACTLY ONE axis from {AXES}; "
   125	            f"found {axes}")
   126	        pin = re.search(r"PIN: `([^`]+)`", bullet)
   127	        anchor = re.search(r"ANCHOR: `([^`]+)`", bullet)
   128	        assert pin, (
   129	            f"AL-3 entry `{key}` carries no PIN. A declared limitation with no "
   130	            f"executing test is an unfalsifiable claim -- the convention L18 "
   131	            f"states and this check enforces on every member")
   132	        assert key not in entries, f"AL-3 names `{key}` twice"
   133	        entries[key] = {
   134	            "axis": axes[0],
   135	            "pin": pin.group(1),
   136	            "anchor": anchor.group(1) if anchor else None,
   137	        }
   138	    return entries
   139	
   140	
   141	def _roster() -> dict[str, dict[str, str | None]]:
   142	    return _parse(_region("ROSTER"))
   143	
   144	
   145	def _exclusions() -> dict[str, dict[str, str | None]]:
   146	    return _parse(_region("EXCLUSIONS"))
   147

   149	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   150	# The migration half -- what the SQL actually binds.
   151	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   152	_TRIGGER = "CREATE TRIGGER trg_provenance_corrections_citation_graph"
   153	# `\\s*` BETWEEN THE PAREN AND `SELECT` IS LOAD-BEARING, and its absence was a
   154	# live defect in THIS walk on its first run: SQL wraps long subqueries, so
   155	# `NOT EXISTS (` followed by `SELECT 1` on the next line is the ordinary
   156	# spelling -- and `decision_ordering`, whose every supplied pair IS bound by
   157	# subquery, measured UNBOUND.  The same multi-line-spelling class as
   158	# `22A-R12-04`, reappearing inside the instrument written to close it, and
   159	# caught only because the axis is asserted in BOTH directions.
   160	_BOUND_TO_A_SOURCE = re.compile(
   161	    r"\(\s*SELECT|NEW\.(?!cited_latch_probe_json)\w+")
   162	
   163	
   164	def _when_body() -> list[str]:
   165	    """The citation trigger's WHEN clause, comment lines blanked.
   166	
   167	    Blanked rather than dropped so a clause's span cannot silently absorb its
   168	    neighbour's prose, and so a comment DESCRIBING a binding is never mistaken
   169	    for one.
   170	    """
   171	    lines = MIGRATION_0037.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
   172	    start = next(i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.startswith(_TRIGGER))
   173	    end = next(i for i in range(start, len(lines)) if lines[i] == "BEGIN")
   174	    return ["" if ln.lstrip().startswith("--") else ln
   175	            for ln in lines[start:end]]
   176	
   177	
   178	def _spans() -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
   179	    """Each clause key's span in the WHEN body, in file order.
   180	
   181	    A span runs from the key's first mention to the NEXT key's first mention;
   182	    the LAST key runs to the end of the WHEN body.  Getting that final boundary
   183	    wrong is not hypothetical -- a first draft of this walk ended the last span
   184	    at its own last mention and reported ``guard_broker_limit_bound``
   185	    UNBOUND, because the subquery binding it sits on the following lines.
   186	    """
   187	    body = _when_body()
   188	    first: dict[str, int] = {}
   189	    for clause in ALL_CLAUSES:
   190	        block = ("probe_guards" if clause in PROBE_GUARD_CLAUSES
   191	                 else "authorization")
   192	        needle = f"$.{block}.{clause.key}"
   193	        hits = [i for i, ln in enumerate(body) if needle in ln]
   194	        assert hits, (
   195	            f"clause `{clause.key}` is in the Python roster and appears "
   196	            f"NOWHERE in the citation trigger")
   197	        first[clause.key] = hits[0]
   198	    order = sorted(first, key=lambda k: first[k])
   199	    spans: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
   200	    for i, key in enumerate(order):
   201	        end = first[order[i + 1]] if i + 1 < len(order) else len(body)
   202	        spans[key] = (first[key], end)
   203	    return spans
   204	
   205	
   206	def _input_bound() -> dict[str, bool]:
   207	    """Does the migration bind this clause's recorded input to a SOURCE?
   208	
   209	    A source is a subquery or a ``NEW.<column>`` other than the probe blob
   210	    itself -- reading the blob is reading the writer's own claim, which is the
   211	    whole thing AL-3 says is not proof.
   212	    """
   213	    body = _when_body()
   214	    spans = _spans()
   215	    return {key: bool(_BOUND_TO_A_SOURCE.search("\n".join(body[a:b])))
   216	            for key, (a, b) in spans.items()}
   217

   219	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   220	# THE CLOSURE, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS
   221	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   222	def test_every_service_validated_clause_is_declared_or_excluded() -> None:
   223	    """DIRECTION 1: nothing the code calls service-validated is unnamed.
   224	
   225	    This is the direction that fired on the first run.  A clause added later
   226	    with ``binding=SERVICE_VALIDATED`` and no L17 entry NARROWS a declared
   227	    limitation silently -- the reader concludes SQL proved something it did
   228	    not -- and it now fails loudly instead.
   229	    """
   230	    declared = set(_roster()) | set(_exclusions())
   231	    service_validated = {c.key for c in ALL_CLAUSES
   232	                         if c.binding == SERVICE_VALIDATED}
   233	    missing = sorted(service_validated - declared)
   234	    assert not missing, (
   235	        f"these clauses are SERVICE_VALIDATED in the code and named nowhere "
   236	        f"in AL-3: {missing}. AL-3 declares its roster EXACT, so an omission "
   237	        f"is a false claim in the document whose entire job is to state what "
   238	        f"is true")
   239	
   240	
   241	def test_every_declared_blob_member_is_service_validated_in_the_code() -> None:
   242	    """DIRECTION 2: nothing AL-3 claims is actually SQL-bound.
   243	
   244	    The failure this catches is ``22A-R9-05``'s, from the other end: a roster
   245	    BROADENED to cover a clause nobody ruled on.  A member the code SQL-binds
   246	    would make AL-3 understate what the trigger proves, which reads as
   247	    conservative and is simply false.
   248	    """
   249	    wrong: dict[str, str] = {}
   250	    for key, entry in (_roster() | _exclusions()).items():
   251	        if entry["axis"] == PREDICATE_WEAKER:
   252	            continue
   253	        assert key in BY_KEY, (
   254	            f"AL-3 names `{key}` on a blob axis and it is not a clause in "
   255	            f"AUTHORIZATION_CLAUSES or PROBE_GUARD_CLAUSES")
   256	        if BY_KEY[key].binding != SERVICE_VALIDATED:
   257	            wrong[key] = BY_KEY[key].binding
   258	    assert not wrong, (
   259	        f"AL-3 declares these service-validated and the code SQL-binds them: "
   260	        f"{wrong}")
   261	
   262	
   263	def test_a_non_blob_member_names_an_anchor_that_exists_in_0037() -> None:
   264	    """A member outside both blob rosters must still be findable.
   265	
   266	    The anchoring-fill clause is not a ``$.authorization`` entry, so no walk
   267	    over the blob rosters could ever surface it -- which is exactly why it
   268	    survived eleven dispatches.  Its declaration therefore carries a verbatim
   269	    ANCHOR into the migration, held here so the entry cannot rot into a
   270	    reference to text that no longer exists.
   271	    """
   272	    sql = MIGRATION_0037.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   273	    non_blob = {k: e for k, e in _roster().items()
   274	                if e["axis"] == PREDICATE_WEAKER}
   275	    assert non_blob, (
   276	        "no NON-BLOB member is declared, so this check is vacuous and the "
   277	        "anchoring-fill clause has quietly left the roster")
   278	    for key, entry in non_blob.items():
   279	        assert key not in BY_KEY, (
   280	            f"`{key}` is declared NON-BLOB and IS a blob clause")
   281	        assert entry["anchor"], f"non-blob member `{key}` carries no ANCHOR"
   282	        assert entry["anchor"] in sql, (
   283	            f"non-blob member `{key}`'s ANCHOR is not in 0037 verbatim: "
   284	            f"{entry['anchor']!r}")

   287	@pytest.mark.parametrize("key", sorted(_roster() | _exclusions()))
   288	def test_every_al3_member_is_pinned_by_a_test_that_exists(key: str) -> None:
   289	    """Every declared limitation is EXERCISED, never merely written down.
   290	
   291	    L18 states the convention -- *"Pinned, not merely written down"* -- and
   292	    AL-3b and 49j already follow it.  Enforcing it on every member is what
   293	    stops the roster from growing entries nobody can falsify: the pin is the
   294	    thing that fails if a later change makes the limitation narrower than the
   295	    declaration.
   296	    """
   297	    pin = (_roster() | _exclusions())[key]["pin"]
   298	    assert pin and "::" in pin, f"`{key}`'s PIN is not a node id: {pin!r}"
   299	    path, func = pin.split("::", 1)
   300	    module = REPO_ROOT / path
   301	    assert module.is_file(), f"`{key}`'s PIN names a missing file: {path}"
   302	    assert f"def {func}(" in module.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), (
   303	        f"`{key}`'s PIN names `{func}`, which is not defined in {path}")

   306	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   307	# THE MIGRATION HALF -- the declared axis against what the SQL actually does
   308	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   808	-- prohibited in CHECK constraints and permitted in a trigger WHEN clause --

   810	--
   811	-- THE COALESCE WRAPPER ON THE LATCH BLOCK IS LOAD-BEARING, AND MEASURED. In a

   813	-- predicate NULL, and a NULL WHEN DOES NOT FIRE THE TRIGGER -- so an evidence
   814	-- blob with a MISSING required key silently passes: json_type(blob,'$.absent')

   817	-- ACCEPTED; with COALESCE(..., 0) it is REJECTED. 0036's own CHECKs use the

   821	-- WHAT THIS TRIGGER CLAIMS, NARROWED TO WHAT IT CAN ESTABLISH. Four limits,

   954	    -- ===== THE AUTHORIZATION'S FOUR FILL-SIDE OPERANDS: PRESENT, AND BOUND
   955	    -- ===== TO THE CITED FILL (Codex 22A-R15-01).
   956	    --

   959	    -- a stored proof whose operands are not frozen is not a proof.  NOTHING

   966	    --
   967	    -- INSERT-TIME RULE.  The five live pre-operand rows are untouched: they

   970	    --
   971	    -- IT VERIFIES A FACT, NEVER A JUDGMENT.  Each freeze is compared to the

   973	    -- value, same domain, no rounding and no cross-engine re-derivation.  It

   975	    --
   976	    -- THE PRESENCE ASSERTION IS SEPARATE AND IS LOAD-BEARING.  `json_extract`
   977	    -- on an ABSENT path returns SQL NULL, so `IS <column>` alone reads an
   978	    -- OMITTED operand as agreement whenever the column is itself NULL --
   979	    -- which is every pre-22-A envelope.  `json_type(...) IS NOT NULL`
   980	    -- distinguishes an absent path (NULL) from a JSON `null` VALUE (the text
   981	    -- 'null'), and that is exactly the distinction the omission case turns on.
   982	    --
   983	    -- THE ORDINARY BRANCH BINDS THE **JSON TYPE** AS WELL AS THE VALUE (Codex
   984	    -- 22A-FIX-R2-01, verified by execution twice -- by the reviewer and here).
   985	    -- `IS` applies the SOURCE COLUMN'S AFFINITY, so a bare value comparison is
   986	    -- blind to the freeze's own storage class: MEASURED, JSON text `"2.0"`
   987	    -- compares EQUAL to a REAL `2.0`, and -- the sharper one -- a JSON OBJECT
   988	    -- compares EQUAL to a TEXT column holding the same minified document.
   989	    -- Production freezes an envelope as a JSON STRING and never as that
   990	    -- object, so both shapes are snapshots the freezer could not emit passing
   991	    -- the clause written to require its output.  Each ordinary branch
   992	    -- therefore pairs the value comparison with a `json_type` that must AGREE
   993	    -- with the column's `typeof()`, one storage class at a time.
   994	    --
   995	    -- THE `'object'` BRANCH IS THE FREEZER'S DECLARED DIGEST ESCAPE, AND IT IS
   996	    -- CLOSED AND TYPE-BOUND (Codex 22A-FIX-R1-01).  `_json_safe_operand`
   997	    -- writes a type-tagged object when the value cannot be written as JSON --
   998	    -- a BLOB (SQLite does not enforce column affinity; 22A-R13-01 measured
   999	    -- that shape reaching production) or a non-finite REAL (`json.dumps(inf)`
  1000	    -- emits the bare token `Infinity`, which `json_valid` reads FALSE, so a
  1001	    -- truthful freeze would be rejected by the row's own CHECK).
  1002	    --
  1003	    -- **THE FIRST DRAFT ADMITTED *ANY* OBJECT once the column was a BLOB or an
  1004	    -- infinity, and that was a REACHABLE WRONG ACCEPTANCE at the raw-write
  1005	    -- trust boundary** -- a forger could freeze `{}` beside a BLOB column and
  1006	    -- satisfy the clause the binding exists to enforce.  MEASURED by the
  1007	    -- reviewer against this exact predicate shape.  The escape now requires:
  1008	    --   * the column's `typeof()` to be the one that MAKES the escape legal;
  1009	    --   * the object to be CLOSED to the freezer's own key pair (`json_remove`
  1010	    --     of the two keys is `'{}'`), so no third key can ride along;
  1011	    --   * the `type` tag to be the one the freezer actually writes for that
  1012	    --     `typeof()` -- **`'bytes'` EXACTLY** (Codex 22A-FIX-R2-02, verified by
  1013	    --     execution): `sqlite3` returns a BLOB column as Python `bytes` for
  1014	    --     EVERY binding, including a `bytearray` or a `memoryview` written in,
  1015	    --     so `_json_safe_operand` can only ever tag a CITED FILL `'bytes'`.
  1016	    --     Admitting the other two tags left the declared type-tag consistency
  1017	    --     unverifiable in exactly the way the digest's VALUE already is, which
  1018	    --     is one declared residual too many; and
  1019	    --   * for a non-finite REAL, the `repr` to be the EXACT sign the column
  1020	    --     carries -- `'inf'` or `'-inf'`, which is what Python's `repr` emits
  1021	    --     (measured), so the two infinities cannot be interchanged.
  1022	    --
  1023	    -- **THE RESIDUAL, DECLARED: SQLite HAS NO `sha256`, so the BLOB digest's
  1024	    -- VALUE is not verified -- only its SHAPE (64 lower-case hex characters)
  1025	    -- and its type tag.**  That is AL-10's boundary exactly (the trigger
  1026	    -- verifies CONSISTENCY, never TRUTH) and it is strictly smaller than what
  1027	    -- the any-object branch exposed: a forger must now produce a well-formed
  1028	    -- digest object beside a genuinely BLOB column rather than an empty one.
  1029	    --
  1030	    -- `fill_origin` GETS NO ESCAPE AT ALL, and that is SCHEMA-PREVENTION
  1031	    -- rather than an omission: `fills.fill_origin` carries a five-value
  1032	    -- `CHECK (fill_origin IN (...))` (migration `0020:394`), and MEASURED by
  1033	    -- execution, that CHECK rejects BOTH a BLOB and an infinity -- SQLite
  1034	    -- compares a BLOB to TEXT as unequal, so no enum member matches.  A
  1035	    -- column that cannot hold either value needs no escape from either.
  1036	    --
  1037	    -- FAIL-CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION.  A malformed snapshot cannot reach a JSON
  1038	    -- function (the `json_valid` CASE, 22A-R3-12's class), and any NULL
  1039	    -- anywhere in the chain collapses through `COALESCE(..., 0)` to a REFUSAL
  1040	    -- rather than to a trigger that silently does not fire.

  2180	-- EVERY ONE OF THE SIX IS COMPARED WITH `IS`, NEVER `=`. Five are NULLABLE
  2181	-- (only admission_tier carries NOT NULL DEFAULT), and NULL = NULL evaluates to
  2182	-- NULL, which makes the WHEN guard NULL and DOES NOT FIRE THE TRIGGER -- so an

  2264	-- AUTOINCREMENT and the UNIQUE index ux_provenance_corrections_trade:

  2271	-- with BOTH append-only triggers present, canonical and UNFIRED. The DELETE

  2291	-- executable statements. The production writer is pinned by a test that drives
  2292	-- correct_cohort_provenance on a SECOND trade and asserts the append lands.
  2293	-- ============================================================================
  2294	CREATE TRIGGER trg_pc_no_replace BEFORE INSERT ON provenance_corrections
  2295	WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM provenance_corrections
  2296	              WHERE (NEW.provenance_correction_id != -1
  2297	                     AND provenance_correction_id = NEW.provenance_correction_id)
  2298	                 OR trade_id = NEW.trade_id)
  2299	BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, '22-A barrier trg_pc_no_replace: provenance_corrections is APPEND-ONLY. V1 records provenance ONCE per trade and has no re-correction path. To retire the barrier see the reversibility header of 0037_latch_order_mandate_links.sql.'); END;

    13	-- the 0035 gate) -- on the audit table of record, it would strand the existing

   153	    -- Three-predicate date guards, per migration 0033's own lesson: a SQLite

   189	    -- junk. `datetime(substr(...,1,19))` then rejects an impossible calendar

   191	    -- The NOT-GLOB clause is what stops `substr(x,21) GLOB '[0-9]*'` from

   199	        -- ROUND-TRIP, not `IS NOT NULL` (Codex R3 Major 5). SQLite
   200	        -- NORMALISES an impossible date rather than returning NULL:
   201	        -- datetime('2026-02-30T00:00:00') is '2026-03-02 00:00:00', so
   202	        -- the row INSERTed and then CRASHED the supported reader at
   203	        -- hydration. Verified at the prompt: the round-trip catches
   204	        -- Feb 30, but SQLite HAPPILY ECHOES hour 24 and year zero --
   205	        -- both of which Python's fromisoformat RAISES on -- so the hour
   206	        -- bound and the year floor are separately load-bearing.
   207	        AND datetime(substr(cited_run_ts_raw,1,19))
   208	                = replace(substr(cited_run_ts_raw,1,19),'T',' ')
   209	        AND substr(cited_run_ts_raw,1,4) >= '1900'
   210	        AND substr(cited_run_ts_raw,12,2) <= '23'),
   211	    CHECK (
   212	        (cited_pipeline_finished_ts_raw GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]T[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]'
   213	         OR (length(cited_pipeline_finished_ts_raw) BETWEEN 21 AND 26
   214	             AND substr(cited_pipeline_finished_ts_raw,1,19) GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]T[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]'
   215	             AND substr(cited_pipeline_finished_ts_raw,20,1) = '.'
   216	             AND substr(cited_pipeline_finished_ts_raw,21) NOT GLOB '*[^0-9]*'))
   217	        -- ROUND-TRIP, not `IS NOT NULL` (Codex R3 Major 5). SQLite
   218	        -- NORMALISES an impossible date rather than returning NULL:
   219	        -- datetime('2026-02-30T00:00:00') is '2026-03-02 00:00:00', so
   220	        -- the row INSERTed and then CRASHED the supported reader at
   221	        -- hydration. Verified at the prompt: the round-trip catches
   222	        -- Feb 30, but SQLite HAPPILY ECHOES hour 24 and year zero --
   223	        -- both of which Python's fromisoformat RAISES on -- so the hour

   225	        AND datetime(substr(cited_pipeline_finished_ts_raw,1,19))

   235	        -- ROUND-TRIP, not `IS NOT NULL` (Codex R3 Major 5). SQLite
